In the fourth month of the twenty-first year of the Yongle era of the Great Ming Emperor Chengzu, the Emperor composed this work:
*The Imperially Composed Praising the True Awakening and Manifesting Rewards of Puan Zhishan Hongren Yuantong Zhihui Jigan Miaoying Ciji*.
Preface to the Veritable Record of the Great Virtuous Bodhisattva Gyeonghu-guk Seonggyo:

I, the Emperor, reflect that the Tathāgata, with his vast and profound wisdom, universally employs skillful means for all humans and devas, serving as a boat upon the sea of suffering and a staircase upon the perilous path.
Thus, he brings to perfection the grandeur of his meritorious virtues and fully embodies the array of his honored titles.
The Supreme One, the Wondrous Path of Perfect Enlightenment, was transmitted to the land of India; transcending heaven and earth and enduring through vast kalpas, it remains forever inexhaustible.

In recent times, there have been those who were able to embody the essence of True Suchness and accord with the heart of Great Compassion, propagating the Way and expounding the Dharma to rescue all things and deliver all people, so that every sentient being might equally receive its benefits. Their meritorious virtues are manifest and renowned, not only...
He was seen by all of his contemporaries and his legacy has been transmitted to future generations.
He is none other than the Great Virtuous Bodhisattva Pujian Zhishan Hongren Yuantong Zhihui Jigan Miaoying Ciji Zhenjue Zhaoxiang Huigui Huguo Xuanchao.
This Bodhisattva’s wisdom-nature is perfectly penetrating, and his faculties are vast and profound; he continues the dharma-lineage of Linji.

He inherited the essential tenets of Mugaṇ and possessed profound, subtle discernment. He attained a wondrous resonance with the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, was fully endowed with the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), and sported in *samādhi*.

His spiritual responses were unfathomable and his transformations were boundless. During his stay in this world, his mind was intent on benefiting and saving others, enlightening both humans and devas.
Whenever anyone offered prayers or petitions, they were all answered according to their wishes and desires. For this reason, the fourfold assembly turned toward him in devotion.

I look up with reverence. From the time the Buddha was in the world until after his final manifestation, his conduct and practice have become ever more exalted, his spiritual resonance has grown increasingly manifest, and his merit and virtue are so vast that they defy full expression in words.

Thereupon, the assembly of monastics compiled the lineages of his transmission of the Dharma, the years and eras spanning successive generations, and the sharp flashes of awakening in his encounters, arranging these refined selections into a volume titled "True Record" (*Shilu*). I have frequently taken it up and...

Upon examining him and investigating his compassionate mind and power of wisdom, it was found that they were nothing other than means to ward off calamities and resist afflictions, to rescue those in peril and relieve urgent distress, to transform people toward goodness so as to accumulate virtuous causes, and to restrain people from evil so as to liberate them from miserable realms.

Thus, he flourished the tradition of our school, providing superior benefit to the royal governance above and bestowing advantageous grace upon the common people below; the abundance of his merit and virtue is beyond measure.
How could one fathom this? Yet, were it not for something to manifest its excellence, how could one express the Emperor’s heart of reverent devotion and sublime veneration?
For this reason, I have conferred upon it a grand title and composed a preface to be placed at the beginning of the volumes.

It shall be carved into printing blocks and circulated so that not only may the Bodhisattva’s extraordinary deeds and miraculous traces be made clearly visible to the ears and eyes of all people, but also so that all practitioners who cultivate themselves [may benefit].

Those who peruse this compilation will, without exception, reverently observe the *vinaya* and diligently cultivate pure deeds, thereby all attaining the fruit of supreme enlightenment and sharing together in the illumination of the Buddha’s sun.
Thus, they shall enjoy the infinite blessings of great peace and prosperity; how truly admirable this is!
The aforementioned *Xù Wénxiàn Tōngkǎo*, fascicle 247,
records that in the first month of spring in the year of Xīnmǎo (1711) of the Bǎoyǒng era, Dàozhōng transcribed [this work] and placed it at the beginning of the *Běn Lù*.
The Imperial Edict for the Investiture of Master Puan, issued by the Yongle Emperor of the Great Ming in the twelfth month of the eighteenth year of Yongle, states:
"I, the Emperor, consider that the Buddha-way takes compassion as its essence and skillful means as its function. It transcends all things and delivers all classes of beings;
its vast salvation is boundless, and its wondrous spiritual powers are unfathomable. Were it not for one to grandly succeed to the Dharma..."
How could he not be able to vigorously revitalize the ancestral style? It was Master Puan, whose myriad practices were perfectly integrated and whose six supernatural powers were fully realized.
Dignified and self-possessed, his transformations were boundless. He vowed to awaken the multitude of deluded beings and to universally benefit all classes of living things.
Like pouring a vast, sweet rain over the four quarters, his nourishing grace was evenly distributed; like manifesting the full moon in a thousand rivers, its radiance...

His brilliance shines alongside [the sun and moon], and his spiritual transformations are here magnificently manifested; it is therefore fitting that he be further bestowed with a formal title. We now specially confer upon him the title:

Bodhisattva Mahāsattva of Universal Hermitage, Ultimate Goodness, Great Benevolence, Perfect Penetration, Wisdom, Silent Resonance, Wondrous Response, Compassionate Aid, True Awakening, Manifesting Blessings, Beneficent Felicity, Protector of the State, and Propagator of the Teachings.
Alas! The teachings have expounded the core vehicle of the school, transmitting the lamp of a thousand generations.

This lineage has bestowed its merit upon both the hidden and the manifest realms, bringing blessings to the living beings of the four seas and supporting our Imperial Radiance so that ultimate governance may be forever attained.
The above is recorded in the two hundred and forty-seventh volume of the *Continued Wenxian Tongkao*.
In the first month of spring in the year of Xinmao of the Baoyong era, Daozhong transcribed and issued [this work], placing it at the beginning of the *Benlu* (Original Record).
It includes the Imperial Preface to the *Shilu* (True Record) of the Great Virtuous Bodhisattva Puan Zhishan Hongren Yuantong Zhihui Jigan Miaoying Ciji Zhenjue Zhaoxiang Huiguo Huanxiao:
"Imperial Preface to the True Record of the Great Virtuous Bodhisattva Puan Zhishan Hongren Yuantong Zhihui Jigan Miaoying Ciji Zhenjue Zhaoxiang Huiguo Huanxiao."
A boat and oar for the sea of suffering; a staircase for the perilous path. His nature of wisdom was perfectly penetrating, and his faculties were vast and profound.
He succeeded to the Dharma-lineage of Linji and inherited the essential tenets of Muguan. With lofty mechanisms and profound eloquence, he wondrously harmonized with the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.

With a heart set on benefiting and rescuing others, he transformed and enlightened humans and devas. The fourfold assembly looked up to him with devotion, as if the Buddha were still in the world. His conduct and practice were ever more exalted, and his spiritual resonance—
Their merits became even more manifest. They warded off calamities and resisted afflictions; they rescued those in peril and aided those in urgent distress;

they transformed people toward goodness, thereby accumulating roots of merit, and they cautioned people against evil, thereby liberating them from miserable realms. Their titles were further augmented, and I have composed this preface for the beginning of these various collections.
By strictly observing the *vinaya* and diligently cultivating pure practices, they all attained the fruit of unsurpassed *bodhi* and entered the same sphere as the Buddha.
Under the illuminating grace of the Sun’s descent, we shall together enjoy the infinite blessings of great peace and vast serenity. Is this not truly commendable?
This serves as the preface.

It is as if spreading sweet dew throughout the six realms, so that its nourishing moisture is evenly bestowed; it is like manifesting the full moon upon a thousand rivers, so that its radiance shines everywhere.

He expounded the teachings of the fundamental vehicle, transmitting the lineage of the thousand lamps; his merit was bestowed upon both the hidden and the manifest realms, bringing blessings to the living beings of the four seas.

Chronological Biography of Heguang’s Response to the World: Year Běiwèi.
On the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month of this year, at the hour of Chén, the Master was born. Year Gēnzǐ: The Master arrived.
He was then only six years old. He dreamed of a monk who marked his heart, saying, "In the future, you shall attain self-awakening.
Upon waking, he described this to his mother, Lady Huang; when she looked at him, there was a single red, translucent mark upon his heart that closely resembled a cherry seed of the world.
In the year Jiayin, the eighth month of that year, the Master followed the Venerable Shoulong Xian to leave the household life, and thus Huaguang Yingsheng was born.
In the year of Xinyou, on the eighth day of the fourth month, he was registered in the temple registers as a monk and received the Venerable Shoulong Xian as his preceptor.
In the year of Renxu, in the fifth month of that same year, he received the Great Precepts of Amṛta at Kaiyuan Temple in Yuanzhou.
Guihai (the tenth day of the tenth month). This year, the Master entered Xiang Province to visit Chan Master Mukan Zhong of Mount Wei.

The Master asked, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return? Master Zhong held up his whisk and showed it to him. The Master attained realization and immediately returned to his place of training. In this year, Yuan Tong was born.

Jiazi (the first day of the first month of the eleventh year). Yuan Cheng was born. Dingmao (the first day of the first month of the fourteenth year). Yuan Ying was born. Wuchen (the first day of the first month of the fifteenth year). Yuan Xin was born. Ji si (the first day of the first month of the sixteenth year).

On the full moon day of the eleventh month in the year of Guiyou (1293), when the Master was thirty-nine years old, Muan passed away at Huanglong. The Master then received an official appointment to reside at Cihua.

While reading the *Huayan He lun* (Comprehensive Commentary on the Avatamsaka Sutra), he reached the passage concerning "the forgetting of emotions upon reaching the fundamental" and "the mind realizing its identity with the essence.
At that moment, he attained a sudden and great awakening; sweat poured from his entire body, and he exclaimed with joy, "I have now personally realized the Dharmadhātu of the Avatamsaka!"
From this point on, he propagated his great vows and transformed both humans and devas. In the fifty-second year of his life, the year of Bingzi, in the fifth month, Master Xian passed away.
In the seventh month, the Master received an official decree and concurrently took charge of Shoulong Monastery. In the autumn of the year Jia Shen, Yuantong shaved his head at Cihua Monastery.
By the year Jichou, the Master was fifty-five years old; meanwhile, his disciple Yuantong [was ordained] on the third day of the third month.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the Master requested a brush and wrote a verse on the western wall of the abbot’s quarters. He then sat in the full lotus posture and passed away.
This was the causal condition for his realization of the Way.
The Master’s name was Yinsu; his style name was Puan. He was a native of Yichun in Yuanzhou, belonging to the Yu clan by family name.
He was a descendant in the twelfth generation of Linji and followed in the lineage of Chan Master Muchan Zhong. During the Song dynasty, he was born in Taipingli of the county.
Before the Master was born, a neighbor saw from her house at night a radiant light illuminating the heavens, visible to those far and near.
They exchanged glances in astonishment. Shortly thereafter, lotuses sprang up along the paths, or appeared in the fields and lanes; the multitude was even more amazed.
When the Master was born, his five limbs were full and lustrous, just as the worldly saying had predicted. From this, people first recognized these as signs of a supreme sage.
This was indeed on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month in the fifth year of the Zhenghe era (1113 CE), at the hour of Chén. On the day of Gengzi, the Xuanhua era began.
In the second year [of his ordination], the Master dreamed that a monk pointed at his chest and said, "In the future, you shall attain self-realization.
Upon waking, he informed his mother, Lady Huang; she saw that the spot was a brilliant red, much like a cherry bead (*sāra*) of the world.

In the eighth month of the fourth year of the Shaoxing era (1134), the Jia-yin year, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, the Master sent the venerable monk Shoulong Xian to receive the *Lotus Sūtra*. The Master said, "The Buddhas..."
The original intent is to value awakening within the mind; what benefit does counting characters and following the lines of script bring to the Way? Xian held him in high esteem.

On the eighth day of the fourth month in the year of Xinyou (the eleventh year of Shaoxing), he shaved his head and donned the dyed robes. In the fifth month of the year of Renxu (the twelfth year of Shaoxing)...
He received the Great Amṛta Precepts at Kaiyuan Temple in Yuanzhou. Having heard that Master Mukan Zhong was propagating the Dharma at Mt.
Gui, the Master traveled to Xiang to visit him and asked, "All dharmas return to One; where does the One return? Mukan held up his whisk and showed it to him.
He had an audience with the Emperor. Upon his return to Shoulong, it was the year of Guihai, the thirteenth year of the Shaoxing era; the Master was then just twenty-nine years old.
In the year of Guiyou, the twenty-third year of Shaoxing, an official decree invited him to preside over Cihua Temple.
On the first day of the first month of the second year of the Qiandao era (the Bingxu year), construction of the Buddhist monastery began; by the twelfth month of the fourth year, it was completed.
The disciple Wontong, through his perfect integration and realization, has diligently assisted in this undertaking and thus shares in its merit.

Regarding the original site of the temple, it was traditionally said to have been donated by Li Cangjian, though the exact era of its founding remains unclear. Master Lishi, who remained humble and unassuming, once remarked:
Having abandoned home to enter the monastic life, for whose son do you act? Having donned the black robes and shaved your hair, what was your original cause?

If you do not repay the state and support your family, you vainly bear the imperial grace and decree; if you do not guide and transform donors, you falsely claim to be a son of the Buddha in the Empty Gate.

For twelve years, he wore paper robes and ate coarse food, using a staff of sorrel wood and sandals of wild grass, never letting his side touch the mat. One day, while reciting the *Avataṃsaka-śāstra*, he reached the passage:

"When the fundamental nature is realized, emotional attachments are forgotten; when the mind is known, its essence is unified. At this, he attained a sudden and great awakening, and sweat flowed from his entire body.
He then said, "I have now personally realized the Dharma-realm of the *Avataṃsaka*. He subsequently addressed the assembly, saying, "This is Master Li Gongchang."

At the very beginning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, he struck a decisive blow, shattering the trichiliocosm as if hot water were dissolving snow, leaving not even a hair’s breadth behind. This would have served as an obstacle for later practitioners;
however, when the Elder Puan saw it, he involuntarily swallowed the five thousand and forty-eight fascicles, transforming them into a single breath that filled all of space.
Only then will you truly believe the words of Śākyamuni regarding his inability to breathe out;
subsequently, he shatters a single atom to bring forth this *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, which pervades the entire Dharma-realm, leaving no principle uncontained and no phenomenon unpenetrated.
Thereupon, you will see that Lady Māyā is your own body, the terraces of Maitreya are your own essence, and as for the youth Sudhana—what a mere gourd! (Text)
He was no different from Samantabhadra; he had practiced alongside me. Without moving from his place of practice, he pervaded the entire Dharma-realm.

With tears of compassion and joy, he leaped for immeasurable delight, as if returning to life from death or suddenly waking from a dream. After a long while, he said: "Inexpressible, inexpressible—and yet again, inexpressible.
Only then did he believe the words of the *Vajracchedikā*: "When the mind of faith is pure, the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*) is immediately produced. The true...
Once the marks have arisen, deluded thoughts arise and perish; when the entire body of the Dharma-body (dharmakāya) pervades all places, only then does the great function manifest before one.
He then spoke a verse: "It cannot be pinched into a ball, nor can it be pushed open; why seek Mount Nanyue or Tiantai?
At the gates of the six sense-faculties, no one makes use of it—only to provoke a foreign monk to come all this way. One day, the Master again brought up the matter of "mind" (citta).

The Master said to his two disciples, Zhai and Yuan-tong, "When the fundamental is reached, emotions are forgotten; when the mind is known, its essence is realized. How do you understand this? The two looked at each other and smiled, saying, "We have not yet reached it. The following day, each presented a verse. The Master then inscribed a preface, saying: "Judging by the eye of the school with a single glance: Zhai: The great matter is not far away; It lies right within the ordinary mind. If you seek it outside of yourself, You will wander for ten thousand miles. Yuan-tong: The Way has no gate; How could there be anything to enter? If you wish to see the Buddha-nature, Look directly at your own face. The Master remarked: "Based on a single observation through the eye of the school, these two have both attained the state of 'the fundamental being reached and emotions forgotten. He then added: "I have already bestowed upon them the seal of the Dharma; they shall surely transmit it to others. Later, he composed a verse to commemorate them: The two disciples of the Great Master, Have both attained the state of "the fundamental being reached and emotions forgotten. One has become a dragon among dragons; The other has become a tiger among tigers. They have both received the transmission of the Dharma-seal; They shall surely transmit it to others. In the future, they will surely bring forth the Way; They shall surely cause the Dharma to flourish. I now write this verse to commemorate them; May those who see it all rejoice.
