he showed people the truth only at the tip of his finger.
Directly beneath, there is no place to avoid the Sovereign; sound and form fully manifest the primary meaning. Ordinary people who grasp at appearances will never know it;
only through sudden awakening to the perfect resonance can one realize its benefit.

Host within guest: these days the lineage style has discarded the old and embraced the new. Meeting face-to-face and hearing one another’s names, there is no error. From time to time, laughter awakens the spirit within dreams;
the great earth, mountains, and rivers are but dust in the eyes. From antiquity to the present, names have been forcibly established; yet this alone is the seamlessness that transcends all limits.
Stupa. Never coming or going to follow the whims of others;
if you wish to understand the true livelihood within this, Śākyamuni the Old Man did not cover himself with a blanket.
Yet, seeking further outside the patriarchs, you run wild in pursuit—be certain that in the end you will fall under the sway of demonic delusions.
The leaping lion reveals his entire body; he swallows the forms of the myriad phenomena. Without head or tail, he strides alone;
his unblinking gaze strikes all with great awe.

The Lord of Lords, within the light of formlessness, bestows the rain of Dharma; with the single flavor of *amṛta*, he irrigates all capacities, causing them all to enter the abode of unconditioned *nirvāṇa*.
Vivid and free, it cannot be grasped; when the true command is enacted, there is no fundamental basis—unless one hides within the Big Dipper.
The body—vague and profound, submerged in its dwelling place. *Du!* Yet it is right here. (He further said:
To realize the boundless and unmanifest is truly extraordinary. Taking empty space as the drum and Mount Sumeru as the mallet, strike lightly and the sound of gold is produced.

Turtle hair commits the offense; rabbit horns receive the retribution. Mountains and rivers shake together—this interpretation loses the core principle. The core principle is not mountains and rivers; that they shake together is a dream.
Even shaking is non-shaking; if brought back, it is of no use. This time you are caught and defeated; henceforth, you shall never again expend effort.
The guest is also not a guest; how can the Way be named? Now that the father has fled, true realization is finally intimate. The host attains the true host, as praised by both Buddhas and Patriarchs.

The lifeblood of the lineage remains unbroken; those who attain it rejoice. To add further annotations is like a blind man groping about—seeking vision within what is already seen, seeking medicine while the illness has vanished.

Verses on Samādhi.

Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings are but this single mind. Awakening and delusion are without interval; past and present are the same. What connection can there be with a thousand names and ten thousand characters?

Spiritual: Spiritual light pervades the realms; its essence is like adamant. Its majestic power is firm, causing heterodox schools to vanish.

when its function is employed, it transcends antiquity and surpasses the present. Only by understanding how the wooden man pulls the saw can one begin to let the stone woman thread the needle.

A bottomless well of lapis lazuli—suddenly one falls into its midst. Though one has cultivated merit for ten thousand kalpas, one may leap out or fail to leap out;
yet one remains mute, blind, and deaf.
Clearly there is no front or back; meeting yet not seeing one another. Year after year, the face of the peach blossoms;
as the boat descends the river toward the prefecture, the boatman’s skillful power provides the means.
[○@∴] A one-legged tiger kills people in secret when it is dark; you do not recognize its eyes, so there is no place for you to exert your strength.
Valley clouds shroud the ancient city.
The child of the rootless tree mingles with time, neither entering nor exiting; head and tail must both be urgent.
Wondrously realizing that which lies beyond this side, one crosses the sea—how could one ever get wet?
The Dharma Words of the Fragrant Accumulation Kitchen:
*Ei*. [Symbol: Good; Symbol: Discernment; Symbol: Mind]. Taking these three dharmas as samādhi, they have not been realized throughout immeasurable and boundless eons.
I now cultivate offerings for the Buddhas and sentient beings; ten thousand sages and a thousand worthies all partake together. The flavor of Mahāprajñā is True Suchness. Ten.

The *pāramitās* are shared equally; all you great ones must apply yourselves with single-minded devotion. Not even a speck of dust is permitted to stir. To repay the dragons, devas, and the eight classes of beings:
do not enter the kitchen to engage in idle clamor. The *zhikai shizhe* (Supervisor of the Refectory) stands before your very eyes;
he guards Puan [the Buddha] without a single flaw or gap. Not even a needle can pierce him as he gives rise to fragrant incense. The eighteen [elements] have been, from the beginning, the Buddha.
Incomparable is he who protects and upholds the land of the Teaching;
Anāthapiṇḍada, who offered his grounds, transformed through compassion and became a venerable one. He protected beings so they might attain Buddhahood—how can his merit be measured?
The Two Kings: Yangshan reveals his traces and accords with the Patriarchal Master. Their single Dharma-nature body benefits all beings through vast compassion.
King Jing of Nanyue: by means of the provisional and the correct, he responds to things without a self-centered mind; his majestic virtue establishes the school—do not treat him with negligence.
Lord Guan: Trapping Sun Quan to restore the Right; cultivating the Way at Yuquan. Formless and empty, his meaning is sufficient before Heaven.
Five Supernatural Powers: Only when one power accords with the One do the six functions become complete. Protecting and upholding Prajñā, the Dharma-body remains unmoving.
The Brahma King stands tall, performing wondrous deeds. Turning the light back upon the nature of consciousness, the universe is magnificently revealed;

his single body is pure and serene. Furthermore, Samantabhadra: when one is accomplished, all are accomplished; when one is destroyed, all are destroyed. The Dharma-body has no dual characteristics; the general and the particular are without obstruction.
Ordinary beings and sages are fundamentally non-existent; the natural state of the essence is eternally present. I send word to those dwelling among the mountains: it is you!
How do you understand this?

Shifting the five pestilential spirits out to the center of the marketplace, he assists the Buddha in spreading his fame and transforming the common folk. He banishes the heterodox to return to the orthodox, nourishing the withered hearts. The national air is refined and prosperous, and the people rejoice.
Joy! This very harmony is the great man.
Verse on the Song of Realizing the Way (with Preface):
The Tathāgatas of the past have already accomplished this gate; The Bodhisattvas of the present now each enter perfect luminosity.
Future practitioners of the Way should rely upon such a Dharma. O worthy ones, this gate is perfectly luminous;
its ultimate realization is just like this. But how do you understand it? I say: Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha—the son’s growth was accomplished within the house.

Bodhidharma faced the wall at Shaolin—his compassionate heart was urgent. Before the Buddhas and Patriarchs were born, the Dharma was not lacking; when the Buddhas and Patriarchs entered [the world], [the Dharma was already complete].

The Dharma of cessation is not lacking. Yongjia recognized this and went to knock at Caoxi; his dream was manifested, and he was invited to stay for one night. Alas for those who practice blindly, calculating with false causes!
They all say that by hearing a single word during that one night, the fragrance will permeate heaven and earth. Such a view is far from the Way and deeply erroneous.
When the mechanism [of awakening] is like a flash of lightning, why labor over deliberation? It is like the King’s Highway, where both the new and the old ascend together.

The author has forgotten all artifice; the man of realization has no proof. This "Song of Realizing the Way" by Master Yongjia takes the twelve divisions of the teachings as pointers and realizes hundreds of thousands of wondrous gates as being manifest before one. We, having joyfully encountered it, add this verse of praise.
The Great Year Jia-shen, the second year of Longxing (1163). On the final day of the seventh month, the Elder Puan wrote this preface for the *Song of Realizing the Way*.

Its universal resonance joins with the wind and moon across the heavens; throughout the great chiliocosm, it is heard as a single sound. This wondrous accord transcends that which can be expressed by voice—how many times has it been heard?
A case. Do you not see? The Golden Immortal with the Face of the Sun is like the Face of the Moon; seeing is not seeing, for there is no one who can see.
The moon reflects in the crystal palace under a frosty sky.
The man of the Way who has severed study and is non-active is at leisure; he never prostrates himself nor reads the sutras. Immovable, he pervades the ocean of all dust-like lands;
standing solitary and aloof, he blends with the white clouds.
Without eliminating delusive thoughts, one does not seek the Truth. The great treasury is opened wide to bestow pearls and jewels;
yet the destitute man, unacquainted with it, stands outside the gate—a pauper within a golden cave.
The true nature of ignorance is itself Buddha-nature; when the mind is pure, it is identical to the purity of a Buddha-land.
Amidst the sounds of waterfowl and the colors of trees and forests, there is not even a hair’s breadth of contention.
The illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body; it is free from both conceptual discrimination and emotional conditions. Every verdant bamboo is none other than the Buddha-nature;
every lush yellow chrysanthemum is a spiritual being that embraces the earth.

The Dharmakāya awakens to the realization that there is not a single thing; entering extinction and descending to birth are neither emerging nor disappearing. Contemplating the true mark of the body is likewise so:
ultimately, how could it ever have left Tuṣita?
The fundamental source, the self-nature, is the original, true Buddha. A single essence, boundless, contains all things within it. When deluded, one speaks only of the "Western Heaven";
when awakened, what need is there for a dried radish?
The five aggregates are like floating clouds, empty in their coming and going; it is only the ordinary person whose eyes remain unopened.
They boil solid ice until it dissolves to serve as their midday meal, and they simmer blocks of snow to make oil.
The bubbles of the three poisons emerge and submerge in emptiness; taking what is non-existent as existent, they bury one in a deep pit.
Luopo once used this to metaphorize the physical body—who among those who understand these words can rely upon the numinous substance?
Realizing the true mark, there is neither person nor dharma; Without using a ruler, a knife, or even a fingernail, The entire army of Māra fully realizes bodhi;
The great earth and Mount Sumeru are contained within a single mustard seed.
In a single instant, the karma of Avīci is extinguished; Yama and I shall no longer distinguish between us. Molten copper and iron dross are the very essence of *amṛta*;
the wheel of fire is itself the moon of the meditative mind.
If one deceives sentient beings with false speech, one will not return to this world for kalpas on end. Within the seamless stupa, there is no fixed form;
it was Old Lu who sat right through the top.
I have invited this calamity of having my tongue plucked out for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; yet my tongue alone pervades the myriad worlds, never ceasing to preach the True Sutra.
I only pray that all sentient beings may attain complete and pervasive clarity.

Suddenly awakening to the Tathāgata-dhyāna—how could it be limited to the East or to India? Pervading all of empty space without any vacancy, within a single pore, the three thousandfold world-system appears.
The essence of the myriad practices of the six perfections is perfectly complete; from this point on, not even a pinch of oil or salt is needed.
Carrying the moon of the mind upon a single mountain staff, one can do nothing but weep to the heavens whenever meeting others.
Within the dream, the six realms of existence are clearly manifest; the womb of a donkey and the belly of a horse have their own distinct flavors.
Bearing saddles and wearing iron bits to repay debts to others—why not bring this present life to rest early?

After awakening, all is empty and void; there is not even a "great chiliocosm. This year is no different from the heavens of old. Through the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, the flowering and budding of plants all manifest the true mark (*dharmatā*), illuminating the source of the mind.
There is neither sin nor merit, neither loss nor gain; do not waste further time contemplating the pāramitās. To dwell on future years for so long will only result in becoming a māra;
it leads instead to slandering one's own practice as lacking the power of the sages.
Within the nature of quiescent extinction, do not seek or inquire. It is just like a traveler lost on a foreign road;
knowing nothing of east, west, south, or north—this very ignorance is most extraordinary.
Lately, the dusty mirror has never been polished; Xuefeng, with his many mouths, is a great old woman.
The celestial mechanism leaks its light directly before one’s face, yet the deluded monkey still tries to strain the clear waves.
Today, one must clearly analyze and discern this: the heavens look down and the sun shines, their light merging into a radiant azure. Xuan Sha, carrying his board, did not permit it to be named;
from antiquity to the present, there has been no trace or shadow.

Who is without thought? Who is without birth? The mind of the past, present, and future does not abide. When not a single thought arises and there is no sense of "mine," this is none other than Amitābha’s own elder brother.
If there is truly neither arising nor non-arising, yet one seeks non-arising within non-arising, it is much like raising a shout in an attempt to silence an echo,
or placing a solitary lamp within the glare of the sun.
Summon the wooden man of the mechanism and ask him: when enlightenment is encountered at every turn, who can debate it? The deceased monk may be likened to the mechanism of a wooden man;
why labor over Xuansha’s direct pointing?

Seeking the Buddha’s grace, the merit will be accomplished sooner or later; in a single thought of non-mind, the Way is naturally manifest. Like withered wood or cold ashes, one is spontaneously free;
the wisdom of non-action is equal to empty space.
Release the four great elements; do not grasp at them. Originally, there is not even a hair’s breadth to rely upon. Earth, water, fire, and wind are but provisional names;
the twelve links of dependent origination are like the horns of a rabbit.

Within the nature of quiescent extinction, one follows the rhythms of drinking and eating; whether parched or hungry, there is no dwelling in attachment. One does not suffer from scarcity, but rather from inequality;
through this, sentient beings find harmony and joy.
All conditioned phenomena are impermanent; all are empty. The state of universal emptiness accords with the fundamental source. Do not give rise to views of self or extremes regarding suchness.
The dharma-realm is without duality, for its single nature is identical.
This is precisely the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment. One must strictly avoid using the mind to engage in further conceptualization.
When Niaoke picked up a tuft of cloth and blew upon it, if you have not yet penetrated the profound ford, do not continue to grope for it.
Decisively declaring that he manifests the true Sangha, he blends with the light everywhere and does not act on his own authority. At times, his nostrils reach toward the heavens as he laughs;
every single sentient being suffers from blindness of the eyes.
There is one who refuses to allow his own feelings to be examined; the great earth, mountains, and rivers raise questions of feeling.
At the tip of a single finger there is no duality; heaven and earth are all at once illumined.

Directly cutting through to the root is what the Buddhas have certified; otherwise, one lives in vain within the three realms and loses one's true nature. Whether stamping on mud, stamping on water, or stamping on empty space, those who engage in blind practice while wearing this seal only give rise to mental afflictions.
I am unable to pluck the leaves and seek out the branches; I uproot it from the very source to show it to all sentient beings. This very Bodhi tree has never existed at all;
reaching for the heavens and reflecting the peaks, its green layers rise tier upon tier.
People do not recognize the mani-jewel; the patriarchs follow after sounds while their minds remain restless. Nanquan vainly sets forth a wheel of light;
for ten thousand autumns and ten thousand springs, people but recall it in empty remembrance.
The Tathāgatagarbha personally holds it within; at all times it manifests as blue, yellow, or white. The essence of the pearl is fundamentally not of a single color;
for no reason, it was nonetheless sought by Guishan.

The six supernormal powers are both empty and non-empty; the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and body are all the same. There is no drumhead for anyone to strike—since ancient times, this has been entrusted to the Thunder God.
A single orb of light, neither form nor non-form—why laboriously carve a boat upon a sword? Form is itself emptiness;
emptiness is not empty. To grasp at marks, the ordinary person is face-to-face with separation.
Purifying the five eyes, one attains the five powers. The five supernormal knowledges were once sought by Gautama; yet realization, knowledge, vision, and awakening do not interfere with one another.
Because of the heterodox, the orthodox strikes through, reaching the azure heavens.
Only through realization can one know that it is difficult to fathom. Do not pursue fame and profit as a seeker of literary artifice. Cleverness cannot withstand the barrier of birth and death.
When the five aggregates are all empty, what suffering or calamity can there be?
To see one's form in a mirror is not difficult; it is merely a weary labor to cross waters and climb mountains.
When the head of Śaṇmukha is not lost, his frantic terror subsides of its own accord, and he finds joy for the rest of his life.
Grasping at the moon in the water—who could possibly seize it? He surely does not concern himself with various appearances. Even the painters Wu Daozi and Zhi Sengyou could not depict it;
the deluded monkey reaches into the empty night, clutching and grasping.

Always walking alone and always treading alone, at every step he does not depart from the Buddha-land; he has never seen a single sentient being who has not entered the gateway of nirvana without remainder.
Those who have attained enlightenment travel together on the path to nirvāṇa; each one is without shirt and lacks trousers. One lamp continues the succession of hundreds of thousands of lamps;
their names are countless in the *Chuan deng lu*.

His bearing is ancient and his spirit pure; the wind naturally rises high. Having forgotten worldly glory and disdain for the age, his nature is firm and steadfast. He demonstrates that there is nothing to come or go;
when seeing people, he waves his hand—do not be so talkative.
His countenance is haggard and his bones are firm; people do not look upon him. Yet he alone drives a single vehicle, proclaiming universal salvation. Who would be willing to board this lotus boat?
He alone can fully express the rhapsody of the clear breeze and the bright moon.

The destitute Śākya son claims in his own mouth that he is poor; he sings the "Snow Song" with such loftiness that no one can join in harmony. When people come and go to ask about the Way, he remains without words—like the moon in the blue sky and the water in the stream.
In truth, it is this body that is poor; the Way is not poor. Within the seven-catty robe there is no room for a needle. Shaking the head, one allows only the state of no-mind.
Entering the water, one originally does not move the ice.

In poverty, my body is always clad in coarse hempen garments; I teach and transform sentient beings so they may seek liberation. Yet these beings increasingly bind themselves with colorful silks and reds;
seeing me in such a state, they scold and revile me bitterly.
The Way is the priceless treasure hidden within the mind. The Buddhas of the ten directions and I are one and the same body. All dharmas are devoid of marks;
there is not a single phenomenon that is not my own mind.
Priceless and precious, its utility is inexhaustible; in every land and every mote of dust, its radiance shines forth brilliantly. Transcending past and present, it is beyond form and name;
it is the life-force of wisdom for the patriarchs of the four, seven, two, and three lineages.
Benefiting beings and responding to their capacities, he never begrudges his efforts; in Vaiśālī, he provisionally spoke of the illnesses of sentient beings.
Once sentient beings realize the nature of illness, they immediately penetrate the light and grasp the original handle of the ancient seal.

The three bodies and four wisdoms are perfectly complete within the essence; yet one still speaks of the three thousandfold world-system and the great chiliocosm. From this, the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates emerge.
Alas! Prince, why do you go away to seek immortality?
The Eight Liberations and Six Supernatural Powers are the Seal of the Mind-ground; brilliantly radiant and vast, they are neither distant nor near.
When the Six Supernatural Powers and Eight Liberations are fully manifested, one brings to mind those weary beings to uplift later generations.
The superior person makes a single decisive resolution and understands all things; throughout the twelve periods of the day, they remain ever luminous.
A great man who casts his sword into the void turns his head and awakens to the boundless expanse within himself.

Those of middling and inferior capacity are often learned yet largely lacking in faith; their literary studies and intellectual understanding increase the sickness of the mind. Lord Yama is not yet willing to let them off;
though pounded in the mortar and ground in the millstone, they will never find peace.
Simply strip away the defiled robes from within yourself. You must know, King of Dignified Sound Buddha, that even what was previously considered wondrous attainment still constituted duality;
how much more so now, when one speaks of right and wrong?
Who can boast of their diligence to others? Hearing this, five thousand have withdrawn from their seats out of lack of faith.
I would rather enter nirvana quickly than allow myself to fall into the nature of a śrāvaka.
Let others slander as they will; let others be wrong as they please. One's essence is like empty space, equal toward all things. It is no different from children quarreling over pebbles;
one merely adds yellow leaves to stop their crying.

To burn fire toward the heavens is but to exhaust oneself in vain; to stubbornly cling to the Ten Powers while failing to assist others is not the way. When afflictions cease, the whole body is the Buddha-nature;
quickly cause them to directly resolve upon Bodhicitta.

Hearing this, it was as if I were drinking nectar. Neither self nor other—who could have created it? Through successive lifetimes I have failed to realize this true body, which has caused me to enter the chamber of dreams along with others.
Melted away, one enters suddenly into the inconceivable. Upon careful examination, I am not found. Within the light of formlessness, the ancient Buddhas transmit;
all have had their noses pierced through by the absolute void.
Contemplate harsh words as being merit; how could wondrous clarity require carving from sandalwood? With every word and every shout, one penetrates the perfect sound;
it need not be heard with the ears, but must be realized through direct attainment.
This person is indeed my spiritual friend; though they speak of the Way as non-existent, they provide true benefit. From beneath their brows, white light radiates in all directions;
without moving, they manifest hundreds, thousands, and billions of transformation bodies.
Do not give rise to enmity or kinship because of slander; cut off the cat and remain silent. It is especially thanks to Zhaozhou who grasped the wedge;
with straw sandals over his head, he laughs with joy.
What manifests the power of unborn compassion and patience? One strikes down the void at Lake Dongting and swallows it whole.
Not a single hair’s breadth is left for others to know: *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
The fundamental principle is both pervasive and communicative; from these two sources, the blade-edge emerges. The essential meaning of the eight essentials is a sky-reaching instruction;
the seven points of inquiry reveal that the mind and principle are one.
Concentration and wisdom are perfectly luminous, not lingering in emptiness; beneath the yellow banner, a pure breeze rises directly.
Had it not been for the Elder Yinzong at that time, Huineng would have had neither fault nor merit.

It is not that I alone have now attained realization; throughout the ten thousand ages, those who have grasped the fundamental mind must be many. All enter from the signless into the state of no-remainder;
yet as long as one has not transcended form and name, one will never understand.
The essence of all Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges is identical; they sit upright now upon the Great Hero Peak. The myriad phenomena of the forested universe have no place to hide;
from the beginning, they have resided within a single speck of dust.

The Lion’s Roar is spoken with fearlessness; towering and immovable, its majestic radiance gathers all. It manifests its entire body throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, yet remains without peer or companion in its interaction.
Upon hearing this, the hundred beasts’ brains split asunder; it pierces mountains and penetrates rocks, causing the hosts of demons to break. At night, it remains as before, towering in the vast sky;
it is satiated by the pure breeze and rinsed by the bright moon.
The fragrant elephant rushes about, having lost its majesty; the wooden woman comes calling, "Who is there?
Samantabhadra snaps his fingers in the open field—this one great failure few people know.

The devas and nāgas listened in silence, giving rise to joy; they came to scatter celestial flowers, which lined the sides of the cliffs. Understanding emptiness and being immeasurable, the Way is beyond capacity;
the earth shook as flowers rained down, once more revealing the profound.

Wandering through rivers and seas, traversing mountains and hills; parting the clouds and girding the rain, my feet reach to the very heavens. Even if you could speak the Way, you would still die beneath the staff;
from three thousand miles away, I transmit it for you.

Seeking teachers and visiting paths to practice Zen, he first pierced people’s nostrils; with one great shout, he left them dazed for three days, yet a speck of dust still clings to the edge of his curved bench.
Since recognizing the path of Caoxi, I have traversed the empty sky along the bird-track and walked upon level ground. Grasping the mist and seizing the clouds, even the wind fears me;
having finished the task of subduing demons, I chant "Sulu."
Having realized that birth-and-death are not interconnected, he instead takes empty space as a drumhead. Those who strike it are many, but those who hear it are few;
Old Man Heyshan was truly without cause.
Walking is Zen, sitting is Zen; facing the wall, he passed nine years in stillness. Losing his money and meeting with divine retribution, Shen Guang was startled;
dividing his skin and marrow, he crossed to the Western Heaven.
In speech, silence, movement, and stillness, his essence is serene. Xie San cast down his fishing boat;
he insisted that traveling to study does not require leaving the mountain pass, yet even this fool still wanders about like smoke.
Even when encountering sharp blades, one remains ever serene; this is simply because one has attained the Vajra Eye. Within the radiance of the single form, there is no second shape;
though the kalpa-fire blazes fiercely, there is no retreating or returning.
Even were it potent poison, it would remain tranquil; drinking the Western River in a single gulp is not yet difficult. Bodhidharma passed through it unharmed;
later, he left behind a single shoe for his burial at Xiong Mountain.
My Master beheld the Buddha Dīpaṃkara; through kalpas of conditioned existence he has since vanished. Mind-to-mind, they were sealed with the realization of non-arising;
for your sake, he descended several times into the Azure Dragon’s Cave.

Throughout many kalpas, you were once the Rishi Kṣāntivādin; yet you never suddenly awakened to the source of this mind. Having endured such suffering as being alive-skin flayed by others, students should likewise rescue [the world] even at the cost of their own brains burning.
How many times have I been born and how many times have I died? I have been submerged in the ocean like a bubble; fierce winds strike the waves without ceasing.
When the wind subsides and the source becomes calm, it is no longer mine.
Birth and death drift on endlessly, with no fixed end. One changes head and face, alternating between anger and joy.
Why not recognize the person of original nature? This very anger and joy is entirely you.

Since attaining sudden enlightenment to non-arising, every movement and stillness is nothing other than the Buddha’s practice. When asked about the True Cause, there is nothing by which it can be represented;
beyond the raising of an eyebrow, there is nothing else that can be done.

Regarding all honors and insults, what cause for sorrow or joy? The precious throne of the Golden Wheel, Gautama has cast aside; he has abandoned the grass mat and taken up the burden of gold, which shall never end.
The living beings of the great earth cannot lift him up.
Entering deep mountains to dwell in an araṇya, detached from form and sound, there is neither day nor night. One does not notice the tolling of bells or the beating of drums;
one has no fear at all of the earth turning or the heavens revolving.
Amidst steep crags and deep seclusion beneath tall pines, the moon is bright and the wind high as cold water cascades down. This gurgling, ancient resonance is truly rare;
who would place a price upon it when offered before the public?
Leisurely and at ease, I sit in the dwelling of a wild monk; too lazy to emerge from the marketplace to show my fangs and claws. Do not wonder that this man of the Way has nothing to offer;
there is only clear wind to moisten the white-cloud tea.

Tranquil and secluded in summer retreat, truly carefree and elegant; leaning on my staff to prop up the heavens, I am still too lazy to grasp it. Raising clouds and spreading rain to sustain all living beings—let me ask:
who in this world of heaven and earth is thirsty?
Upon awakening, one realizes it requires no effort; one circumambulates three times and bows to the Master. Although he allowed me to stay for one night, this was not something obtained from another;
the numinous light of one's own nature is fundamentally vast and unobstructed.
All conditioned phenomena are not the same; refined gold of a hundred smeltings surpasses red copper. To hold it for oneself and use it for oneself, it shall never be exhausted;
it relieves the aged, pities the poor, and shines through the rising sun.

Giving with attachment to signs produces the merit for rebirth in heaven; there is no need to consult tortoise shells or purchase divinations. Not a single hair’s breadth of profit is gained, yet one cultivates for oneself;
like a shadow following a form, all things are fully present.
It is like an upward-pointing arrow shot into the void; when its strength is exhausted, there is no achievement, and it ends in emptiness. How can one become like the old man Sanping?
Upon merely hearing [his name], he looked at the arrow and split open his chest.
When the momentum is exhausted, the arrow falls back; as before, there is no escape from the six realms. Rising and sinking do not occur outside the Dharmakāya;
it is simply that one is stubbornly deluded and lacks wisdom.
They invite an unfavorable rebirth in the next life; taking little for much, they play like children.
They refuse to wander through the vast courtyard, only to yoke iron collars and drag plows while sleeping in the mud.
How can it compare to the gate of the unconditioned true mark? Singing at dawn and drumming at dusk, it brings the universe into order. Striking the east, the sound resonates in the west;
in the end, it employs but a single light to swallow all.

One directly transcends and enters the stage of the Tathāgata. From this point on, sentient beings fail to understand this benefit; whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, everything is entirely true.
Yet, by pursuing the superficial and giving rise to the deluded mind, they fall into attachment and stagnation.
If you only obtain the root, do not worry about the branches. Seeking teachers from afar leads to much loss and deception. A gentleman attends to the root, and the Way will surely arise.
There is no need to pull hemp or drag kudzu.
Like a pure lapis lazuli gem containing a precious moon, that which was not realized in the past is now fully penetrated.
There is only this mind and no other mind; do not peruse the textual formulas of false teachers.
I have now understood this wish-fulfilling jewel; within the garment of the poor child it shines with radiant light. Walking wherever one goes, it is never lost;
only upon meeting a true friend once more does one become free of doubt.
Benefiting oneself and others is never exhausted; a single flower with five petals is discerned within the [wooden] frame. The myriad phenomena of the universe cast their reflections therein;
from antiquity to the present, nothing has been leaked.
The river moon shines, the pines sigh in the wind. It is not he, but who else could it be? You wander restlessly, practicing Zen and seeking the Way;
do you not know that you yourself possess a luminous pearl?
In the eternal night and clear sky, what is there to do? The precious moon in the vast heavens shines together with them. The clay ox enters the sea without a trace;
a single sound from the wooden horse follows the sun.
The Buddha-nature, the pearl of precepts, and the seal of the mind-ground shine brilliantly even in brothels and wine shops.
When Baoshou saw another strike him with a single punch, from that moment he was liberated from the afflictions of illness.
Fog, dew, clouds, and mists are the garments upon his body; why must he don a hundred patches to rely on external dust? At the head of Mount Taiyú, it could not be lifted;
Master Lú coldly laughed at Master Xiù’s folly.

The dragon-subduing bowl and the tiger-taming staff were established by the Tathāgata according to circumstances; manifesting expedient means to lead toward the ultimate reality, he transformed sentient beings, all of whom ultimately emerge from concentration and wisdom.
The two-pronged golden rings ring out clearly; they are much like the pattering raindrops from a roof eave. I ask those traveling to study under masters:
what sound is this? It is because their deluded minds have not yet attained the power of Bodhi.
It is not a matter of displaying forms or empty affairs; Old Śākyamuni simply wishes for people to know. Picking it up and putting it down is no other thing;
carrying water and hauling firewood are matters that are perfectly appropriate.
The Tathāgata’s precious staff follows his own tracks; it cannot be compared to the idle games of the world.
At times it is called a stringless lute, and suddenly it is said to be without holes.
Seeking not for truth, nor severing delusion; from antiquity to the present, there has never been two kinds. Truth and delusion are like frost in the sixth month;
under the bright sun and scorching heavens, there is only the wondrous manifestation.
To realize that these two dharmas are empty and signless— whether one fashions a Buddha image from clay or adorns it with gold, offering incense and flowers by day and lamps by night—
who would know that all this rests upon the tip of a single hair?
Without marks, without emptiness, and without non-emptiness; raising the mallet and brandishing the whisk to awaken the blind and deaf.
If one understands that the dog has no Buddha-nature, how could one know that its entire being is identical to emptiness?
This is the true mark of the Tathāgata; it is like a signboard displayed in a bustling marketplace. Subhūti’s dog bites through the three barriers;
failing to penetrate the profound mechanism invites karmic obstructions.
The mirror of the mind is a bright reflector, unimpeded; the lands of the ten directions are boundless and face it from all sides. Break the mirror open and you shall see him.
Do you recognize this perfect radiance?

Vast and empty, brilliantly transparent, it pervades the realms of sand; difficult to express in words, there is nothing that can be understood. This single phrase of the separate transmission is beyond speech;
it is the wondrous realization of the perfect penetration of Avalokiteśvara.
Within the manifestation of the myriad phenomena, there is neither head nor tail, yet it shines with brilliant clarity. From where does this ever-moving constant light arise?
Upon initial awakening, one’s entire body is revealed as a vivid, bare reality.
A single orb of light is neither inside nor outside; the bright pearl that anchors the sea remains even now. Yangshan did not dare to bury it away himself;
when questioned, its numinous awareness is ever unclouded.

Vastly dismissive of emptiness, they reject cause and effect; wearing not even a scrap of clothing, they crave the warmth of fire. Seeing the wealth and status of others, they give rise to anger and disdain.
How deep is the ocean of karma—where can one find its end?
Vast and boundless, it invites calamity and misfortune. The Buddha-treasure and the golden wheel turn into iron grinders; the ten pāramitās transform into molten copper.
Having eaten their fill in abundance, they shall surely not hunger.
Abandoning existence for the sickness of clinging to emptiness is likewise so; yet you take the aggregates and sense-bases as fixed and settle into meditation.
The *ālaya-vijñāna* is a Kunlun treasury, where for ten thousand kalpas you have been stubbornly deluded and entangled by karma.
It is like avoiding drowning only to throw oneself into fire; since neither state is clarified, the Dharma will fall away.
One must quickly draw near to those of right knowledge, remaining as one always dwells upon this seat of Bodhi.
Abandoning the deluded mind to grasp at ultimate truth is like seeking cold water within a mass of raging fire.
When Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa invited him to ascend the mountain, he entered samādhi in an instant.

The mind of acceptance and rejection becomes artful and hypocritical; at night, one rests upon a skull and speaks of sleep as if it were real. To find pleasure in being honored with a southern-facing seat is not a light matter, yet one remains unaware that one possesses no ground of one's own mind.

If a student of the Way does not understand this and merely practices, they will surely tread step by step into the pit of shadows. Though the great light shines everywhere, the blind have no perception;
at the improper time, one must not contend with wild foxes.

Deeply convinced, they recognize the thief as their own son; a pity that the ancestral fields and lands are shared with such a one. Now that they have fallen into ruin, it is difficult to recover them;
they will die in vain and endure suffering for long kalpas.

They deplete the wealth of the Dharma and destroy their merit; it would be better to remain a perpetual pauper, a traveler on the crossroads. Though the body is capable of contact, it cannot perceive, solely because its prior causes lack a guiding principle.

There is nothing that does not arise from this mind, intellect, and consciousness. The three corpses and six thieves press upon one in vain, like trying to bind a fierce wind with hair from a tortoise;
ordinary people do not realize this, so there is no news of liberation.
Therefore, in the Chan gate, the mind is brought to final resolution: mind after mind, there is no other mind apart from the mind itself. Now it is simply that which was there all along;
without changing its fundamental source, one lets it roam freely in song.

Suddenly entering the power of the vision of non-arising, one asks not whether it is sunny and dry or rainy and damp. Encountering the occasion, one performs the play that manifests the flower of the mind;
while others may be in a state of bustling confusion, this is no matter of urgency for me.

The Great Man wields the sword of wisdom; he sweeps away demonic influences like a flash of lightning. Possessing the singular majesty and heroism of the Vajra Samādhi, who but Avalokiteśvara could behold this?
The sharpness of Prajñā is like the flame of a vajra; beyond speech and hearing, it is neither sudden nor gradual. Leaning against the sky, it constantly emits the white tuft of light;
whether praying for rain or for clear weather, there is nothing that does not come to pass.

Not only did you utterly crush the minds of the non-Buddhists, but humans and devas have looked up to you in devotion until this day. Whether seeking a son or praying for a daughter, your every response is fulfilled;
when music is played and songs of joy are sung, it is with your voice.
Long ago he already caused the demons of Māra to lose their courage. Neither increased nor decreased; even if he froze to death, he would not wear the clothes of a lowly person;
even if he starved to death, he would not eat the crumbs from the edge of a beard.
Thundering the Dharma-thunder and striking the Dharma-drum, the needle-point pierces and releases the thousand-jin bow. The great earth, mountains, and rivers lose their majesty;
sitting alone on the solitary peak, the single eye is universal.
Spreading the clouds of compassion and sprinkling the nectar of ambrosia, it moistens all things and brings forth life beyond compare. The price of rice in Luling is beyond anyone’s recompense;
in profound stillness, they naturally accord with one another.

The treading of the dragon-elephants brings boundless moisture; leaping through clouds and riding the mists, he pays homage to the various heavens. Śakra, the Lord of Devas, is struck with alarm and has nowhere to hide;
seeking the light that illuminates the principle, he knocks at the gate of the Golden Immortal.
Those of the three vehicles and five natures all awaken; only then do they know that they themselves possess a treasury of pearls. At the opportune moment, it is bestowed upon their descendants;
there is no need to labor further by relying on another's gate.
The snowy mountains are lush and pure, free from all impurity; they are composed solely of mani jewels interspersed with one another. Pearls and jeweled nets cast layered reflections.
I prostrate and take refuge in this seamless stupa.
Purely issuing forth the *amṛta*, I have always maintained it within. The child in the open field points to the White Dharma; The decrepit Muzhou rides alone.
For a moment, borrow the warbling of the oriole for the fluttering of the butterfly.

The single nature perfectly penetrates all natures; O Lord, do not violate the decree from the Western Heaven. The Ultimate Way is without difficulty, yet it is loathed by those who engage in discrimination;
Mañjuśrī remained silent at Vaiśālī, for he fundamentally did not realize it.
A single dharma universally encompasses all dharmas. The wind blows light and the rain falls briskly; a single note from a fisherman’s flute brightens the springtime.
Waves strike the solitary boat, its sound echoing against itself.
The single moon universally appears in all waters; though divided into four places, the boat is of one essence. Within the many there is the one, and within the one there are the many.
Do not act like the foolish monkey who tries to catch the bottom of a pond.
All waters and moons are encompassed within a single moon. Why does the blind man with cataracts point to it for resolution? It is all but this one light of the mind;
year after year he comes crying out to the peach blossoms and the moon.
The Dharma-body of all Buddhas enters my own nature; it is like a thousand lamps reflected in a single mirror. Layer upon layer, the meanings are inexhaustible;
this absolute, numinous clarity is beyond any object of realization.
My nature is identical and united with that of the Tathāgata; do not resent this mountain monk for his lack of worldly sentiment. Though we meet, we do not truly know one another;
only when you liberate yourself can you untie the bonds of the other.
All things are fully present throughout all stages; yet ordinary people, failing to understand this, contend for fame and profit. When will fame and profit ever reach their end?
In vain they labor night after night to lock away the mountain ravines.
Neither form nor mind, neither karma nor action; cease pointing to yellow flowers and green leaves. When spoken of, it seems to exist; when realized, it is not there.
From this, the realm shall be in great peace and security.

In a single snap of the fingers, the eighty thousand gates are perfectly realized; how could existence and non-existence, or having and not having, be fit for discussion? Even if one were to provisionally set forth a thousand sutras and ten thousand treatises, it would simply be that Kāśyapa hears what has never been heard.
In a single kṣaṇa, three asaṃkhyeya kalpas are extinguished; there is not even a hair’s breadth of mutual interference. Before names existed, heaven and earth were not yet;
once names arose, the myriad things shone in layered splendor.
All numerical phrases and non-numerical phrases—your profound words, along with their excellent commentaries—are brilliantly radiant, filling all of space;
they do not abide in form or sound, yet they bestow light.
What connection has this with my numinous awakening? Yunmen received guests through his three modes of engagement; his discourse remains unclouded by the passing of a thousand springs.
One who deeply understands this nature knows it is beyond time and eon.
Neither to be disparaged nor to be praised, it has shone brilliantly from antiquity until now: "The radish of Zhenzhou weighs three catties;
water in the bucket, rice in the bowl."
Its essence is like empty space—do not seek its boundaries. The whole body is a mouth, yet one can only speak half of it. It can heal even the three types of patients;
the lamp-stand and the pillar are ever in companionship.
Without leaving its current place, it is eternally serene; the divine light does not travel to the Western Heaven. Deshan’s talk fell into the Dragon Pond, where he laughed;
swallowing his breath and voice, he said no more.
Seeking it, you know it cannot be seen; it pierces through the skull without exception. Lifting one's head, the hawk flies off to Silla;
lost is the face of the peach blossoms and the autumn moon.

One cannot grasp it, nor can one let it go; thus the eyes are blind and the heart is dark. Dwelling at the mouth of the great ocean, parched and withered, one reaches out both hands to ask others for water.

Within that which cannot be attained, there is nothing to be gained; furthermore, there are no demonic factions to deceive or intimidate. When wild panic subsides of its own accord, that is itself bodhi.
It is truly pure, wondrously luminous, and without interval.

Silence when speaking, speech when silent; the wondrous pivot of the Buddhas and Patriarchs has no fixed rules. Unless one personally arrives within this gate, how can one take up the true staff as a guest of the Dharma?
The gate of great giving stands open without obstruction; why wait for distant kalpas to cultivate and attain it? It requires only that you cease directly below with no-mind.
This single sphere of radiant light is not of a different color.
When someone asks me which school I understand, I can only wave my hand to tell them they are deaf. A sharp-witted monk must have a sudden flash of insight;
what need is there to labor further explaining the five houses?
The report proclaims the power of the Mahāprajñā; yet this realm and this mind are entirely unrecognized. One who soars above the clouds vainly claims to have seen peach blossoms;
the moon-like countenance remains as before, beyond words.
Whether it be right or wrong, people do not recognize it; when right and wrong no longer reach you, cease your doubts and recollections. His truth is not equal to your own truth;
if you overturn the rope-bench, what loss or gain is there?
Moving backward or forward, even the heavens cannot fathom it; Deng Yinfeng shattered the rules of Chan. The forest of monasteries stirs in thousands of ways;
who can surpass him in returning to the truth by standing on his head?
I have long undergone cultivation through many kalpas; the Great Universal Wisdom-Victor was originally perfected through this cycle. Why do the Buddha-dharma not manifest before you?
It is because you fail to realize them, remaining mired in the flow of delusion.
This is no mere idle deception; once a human body is lost, it is difficult to regain. One's roots of goodness are subtle while evil causes abound;
there is no interval between this life and the Avīci Hell of Uninterrupted Suffering.
Erecting the banner of the Dharma and establishing the fundamental purpose—whether in speech or silence, wind or cloud, it is present everywhere. Do not say that the Way ends at Caoxi;
what benefit is there in losing your original constancy?
Clearly and brightly is the Buddha’s command: Caoxi is it. A single drop from Caoxi pervades all under heaven. The Dharma-ocean is clear and still, moistening past and present.
Flying through the air and touching the earth—who knows its worth?
The first Kāśyapa first transmitted the lamp; a million humans and devas craned their ears to listen. The golden-colored dhūta heard it but did not comprehend;
when the flower was held up, his smile was sharp and fresh.
The Record of the Twenty-Eighth Patriarch of the Western Heaven: transmitted from patriarch to patriarch, there is no separate wisdom.
The Chan of the Eight Meditations and Four Empties of the Tang Dynasty is conditioned and fails to reach the stage of true emptiness.
Traversing rivers and seas, I have entered this land; ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains share but one path. When coming there was nothing; when departing, all is empty.
I prostrate to the Muni, who grants his full protection.

Bodhidharma was the First Patriarch. When the King of Liang failed to attain resonance with him, he was like one who is deaf and blind; though the realm was vast and empty of sages, the King still sought his fame.
Shaking his sleeves, Bodhidharma departed for the state of Wei, leaving no fixed abode.

The transmission of the robe through six generations is renowned throughout the world; seekers of Chan and the Way are as numerous as motes in a sunbeam. But how can they compare to Danxia, who burned the wooden Buddha?
Onlookers were left red with rage, falling into a state of dark confusion.

The number of later generations who attain the Way is beyond measure; though there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand variations, they all follow this same path. Those who achieve success are few, while those who fail are many.
To reach the principle and accord with the scriptures, there is nothing to be done or contrived.

The Real does not establish the false; the false is fundamentally empty. I urge you: when the thief has passed, do not draw your bow. Transcending past and present, there is nothing that can be grasped;
even the slightest obstruction cannot be penetrated.
Both existence and non-existence are cast aside; it is not empty, yet not non-empty. Emptiness is fundamentally without emptiness, for there is no room for a needle.
Amitābha Buddha is of true golden hue; his marks and signs are boundless, which we share in common.
The twenty gates of emptiness have never attached; the three vehicles and five teachings are all cast aside. The message at the fingertip is most clear;
once the illness is cured, what need is there to apply more medicine?
The single nature of the Tathāgata’s essence is inherently identical; yet śrāvakas, clinging to appearances, perceive east and west.
When suddenly one strikes the path from which one emerges, the ninety-thousand-league journey of the great garuḍa bird is traversed in an instant.
The mind is the faculty and phenomena are the objects; when faculty and object encounter one another, deluded emotion arises. To use fire to extinguish fire is the wondrous method;
it burns away the former mind of karmic consciousness.
These two are like scratches upon a mirror; they reach directly to the ability of Lingnan Nan. This immediately reveals that Master Xiu lacked any leaping or transcending;
it was all in vain to labor over disputes of four-line phrases.
When stains and impurities are completely removed, the light finally appears; its illumination reveals a face unlike that born of a mother. Without head and without tail, it is all one and the same;
even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes cannot see it.
When both mind and phenomena are forgotten, the nature is itself the Truth. Last night I dreamed of the stars in the heavens; the Southern Bureau and the Northern Dipper have no place to hide.
Each and every one contains radiance, reflecting the Dharmakāya.

Alas for this degenerate Dharma and evil age! Though their minds are like sharp blades, they call themselves "wise"; yet when they come beneath the trees, they create a clamor that deafens the heavens, even going so far as to slander the original masters, claiming they were not at all right.
Sentient beings of meager merit are difficult to discipline; they spend their days contending for fame and seeking profit. Among ten million, not one person [truly understands].
Tell me, by whose light do they appear in the world?
The Sage is distant and false views run deep; the Patriarch seeks a kindred spirit within his own belly. Two Zen monks inquire of one another:
"The Buddha-dharma of old is not as it is today."

When Mara is strong and the Dharma weak, there is much resentment and harm. Walking barefoot in ascetic practice with only a cloth for a canopy, he sacrificed his body to seek rain until the crimson heavens cleared.
To those of ordinary mind, such acts appear trivial and lead them to retreat.
Upon hearing the teaching of the Tathāgata’s sudden (sudden) gate, they immediately take poison and swallow it;
the old barbarian has his front teeth broken, yet he remains whole in body despite the many demons.
Regretting that it was not extinguished and destroyed to shatter the tiles, they employ a hundred schemes and a thousand stratagems to display their monstrosities.
Sitting upright with a serene smile atop the ancient peak, if one were to take refuge, one would simply bow to oneself.
The mind depends on the body, yet calamities reside within the body. Your physical form is not the same as my true self; it is foul, putrid, and stinking, a place of no utility.
Consciousness sinks into kalpas of suffering, falling into the ford of delusion.
There is no need to harbor resentment or blame others; for such actions, one will surely be drenched in molten brass and iron liquid.
Furthermore, one shall enter the wheel of fire and the crushing millstone, where the ox-headed hell-wardens will carve out one's liver and heart.
If you wish not to incur karma of the Avīci Hell, let the mind cease of its own accord when facing objects. Why must you toil in weary pursuit abroad?
The numinous light shines alone, like the bright moon.
Do not slander the True Dharma Wheel of the Tathāgata. My Teacher spent countless kalpas to finally achieve it; King Dīpaṃkara personally transmitted it to him.
You descendants of future generations must never treat it with contempt.
In a sandalwood forest there are no other trees; the juniper seeds before the courtyard are not for play. When small, the large is used and all is level at once;
when large, the small is used and there is no limit.
Densely shaded and profoundly still, he dwells like a lion; jackals, foxes, and dogs find it difficult to escape his station.
Transversely swallowing the azure heavens, his form is majestic and grand—where has the "True Person of No Rank" gone?
Wandering alone in the quietude of the forest, his dignified majesty is unmoving yet pervades all forms.
Originally unconcerned with the affairs of others, he lets the bridge flow while the water remains still.
The running beasts and flying birds all depart afar; they know that the Way has no place of abiding from the beginning.
Empty, with no bird tracks and no footprints on the ground—the blue-eyed barbarian monk gazes at the wall.
A pride of lion cubs follows behind; how different from hounds chasing a deer? Where shall one seek the horned antelope?
Let it not turn its head to let out a roar that reaches the heavens.
At three years old, he was already able to let out a great roar; Mañjuśrī said it was difficult to subdue him in battle.
In his restless state, he was temporarily tethered by Kapiśa, but now, his entire being is free, with no one left to guard him.
If this jackal pursues the Dharma King, he has already stumbled before he has even taken a step. He expends his precious spirit for a meager price;
he reveals his entire body, and you are in a frantic hurry.
For a hundred years, demons and monsters have opened their mouths in vain; throughout five hundred lifetimes, one’s kin flee like foxes and hares.
Before the Hundred-Fathom Peak, a single phrase is ever new, yet within the unobscured light, it remains unresolved.
The Perfect and Sudden Teaching has vanished from human sentiment; beneath Mount Jiyun are the four rattan roots. Who in the world’s great Chan can recognize them?
In the wasteland of weeds and wild earth, few people till the soil.
When doubt arises and cannot be resolved, one must simply contend. He forcibly took a brick and ground it before Mazu. The ox’s movement does not depend on the cart’s mind;
at that moment, his nostrils reached across the vast heavens.
It is not that this mountain monk is displaying a sense of self and other; this matter has always been non-dual.
To explain it through the eighteen unique qualities—when they are both common and uncommon, what is that?

In their practice, they fear falling into the pits of nihilism or eternalism; whether asserting existence or non-existence, they do nothing but quarrel. The essence of the teaching remains unmanifested as they fall into mere words and phrases;
their conscious minds follow after sounds and forms.
It is not non-non, nor is it is-not-is. Such is-and-is does not enter into samādhi. In a single thought-moment, one universally contemplates immeasurable eons;
there is no going, no coming, and no abiding.

To err by a hair’s breadth is to lose a thousand li. When the mechanism is like a flash of lightning, do not attempt to deliberate upon it. It does not lie in bowing the head or in further reflection;
the Universal Radiance is itself the teacherless wisdom.

Thus the dragon girl attained Buddhahood instantaneously; this single bright pearl is no external object. In the South, at the Land of No Defilement where Light Ceases, she personally beheld Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa and distinguished right from wrong.
If this were not so, then Śunakṣatra would have been born in the fallen states; his extensive explanations failed to clarify the fundamental principles of the True Dharma.
Pursuing fame and profit to engage with the capacities of the masses, once his karma was fulfilled, he sank to the bottom of the Avīci Hell.
Since my early years, I have accumulated learning; braving wind and rain, I often felt lost and distressed. Upon reaching Caoxi, I no longer harbor doubts;
only now do I realize that my past efforts were in vain.
I have also investigated commentaries and sought out sutras and treatises; throughout long nights and clear skies, I practiced what I had seen and heard.
I thought that extensive learning was itself the truth, but who would have known that all dharmas reside within the square inch of the heart?
Discriminating names and forms, one knows no rest; how can one seek after mirages or flowers in the sky?
When the dragon boat and the old pavilion lie fallow upon the fields, only then does one truly come to rest.
Entering the sea to count grains of sand is but a futile exhaustion; lacking capital, one follows merchants across the ocean gate.
Though the eyes behold thousands of treasures and myriad jewels, upon returning, not a single coin can be divided.
Yet I was harshly rebuked by the Tathāgata. How could my true mind be separated from him? In my greed and haste, I sought only outwardly;
thus it has come to this, that even my eyes are blocked.
What benefit is there in counting the treasures of others? With a mind of delusion, one leans against the door and huddles by the window. Though treated with contempt, one remains silent;
yet the bright pearl within one's own garment remains unrecognized.
From of old, I have wandered aimlessly, realizing my journey was in vain; yet I did not shrink from mountains far away or deep ravines.
This single shoulder-load of Mount Sumeru is difficult to set down, as I love to gaze upon the peaks' exquisite and jagged grandeur.
For many years you have lived in vain as a traveler in the dust and wind; you have not asked whether it be east or west, north or south. You should simply dwell well and settle yourself at ease.
I hear that when you were brought up for questioning, your body and mind were like ink.

With a fundamentally mistaken understanding of the nature of reality, they fail to grasp the profound mechanism of the Way while maintaining the five precepts; whether walking or sitting, they cling to the contemplation of emptiness, perceiving objective realms and sensory dust as increasing their demonic delusions.
Failing to comprehend the Tathāgata’s perfect and sudden teaching, you take this six-foot golden body to be yourself. Apart from knowing names and forms, there is nothing else to know;
day and night you burn incense and offer empty prostrations to yourself.
The diligence of the Two Vehicles does not equal the Bodhicitta; the Southern School and Northern Patriarchs are in chaotic confusion. Though these may be good causes, they invite evil fruits;
when will you ever realize and see the True Nature?
The heterodox teachers are clever but lack true wisdom; in nourishing life, they seek only to crave fame and profit. They burn cinnabar and refine elixirs, studying to become immortals;
yet, because their conditioned efforts are incomplete, they ultimately fall back into ruin.
They are both foolish and utterly deluded; five hundred or three hundred form a single mass. Grandfather Tai Gong made a vow and burned incense of milk-fragrance;
yet they move like snakes or mice, destined in the end to perish.

From an empty fist, one gives rise to the realization of reality; wandering about, one delights in tracing the characters of the sutras. When the full moon’s luminous essence and the pointing finger are both misunderstood, one enters the three miserable realms in vain and suffers punishment for naught.
To grasp the finger and mistake it for the moon is to labor in vain; when one place is illuminated, both places are penetrated.
The form of the moon and the finger do not intersect, yet the nature of the oceans of lands in the ten directions is harmoniously fused.

Within the dharmas of the sense bases and their objects, you falsely fabricate the strange and the marvelous; upon hearing someone called "Master," you immediately prostrate. From where have you come to be among them?
For now, act as a street monk and also go about begging for vegetables.
Not seeing a single dharma is the Tathāgata; all functions suddenly cease, and one laughs heartily. Where is the general’s warhorse now?
Wild grasses and idle flowers bloom everywhere across the ground.
Only then can one be named Avalokiteśvara. The vast, luminous spirit shines neither within nor without; wild bridges and village shops mingle with the flow of the mundane world.
Beg from me a single coin to fill your cloth bag.
When fully realized, karmic obstacles are originally empty. A rabbit’s horn staff strikes the wild wind; a rope of tortoise hair pierces the cloud-nose.
Thus one understands whether the universe is empty or not.
If you have not yet settled it, you must still repay your old debts; when will this karmic enemy be released? If you wish for rest, then simply rest;
do not enter another’s house, lest they sell you out.
Starving, I encountered the royal banquet but could not eat; a hundred kinds and a thousand varieties dazzled my eyes.
I had thought these were for Your Majesty’s own private use, but who would have known they would bring me such hardship?

When the sick encounter the King of Physicians, how could they fail to be cured? Lu’s physician possessed a most stern and strange appearance; seeing his majestic bearing, my heart and gall were struck with alarm.
Failing to receive the immortal elixir, I have since been ruined.
Practicing dhyāna amidst desire through the power of knowledge and vision, he recognizes none of the myriad ways of livelihood. The ten pāramitās abide forever;
the old man Pang Gong conveys this message.
A lotus born from fire can never be destroyed; yet in every thought-moment, beings toil in existence without autonomy. Since he was a man of great capacity, so am I;
casting aside my shortcomings and following what is long, I shall proceed without hindrance.
When Yongshi committed a grave offense, he realized non-arising; he picked up his three robes and immediately set forth. Encountering people, he pointed them out as mindless objects;
in that very moment, he turned the light back within, as if it had never been otherwise.

Having attained Buddhahood long ago, he remains here and now; though the vessel is overturned, his voice does not cease to pervade the world-systems of sand. His wondrous sound resonates afar, widely proclaimed and extolled;
those who remember him remember him, and those who bow before him bow before him.
The lion’s roar is spoken without fear; speaking directly seems almost clumsy. When asked where he dwells in his home, he points distantly to the front slope, offering no further instruction.
I deeply lament this dull-witted, stubborn, and callous skin-bag; it simply thinks no one will come to pry it open.
Whether I am young or already decrepit, I shall recklessly spend my life managing this mass of flesh.
Knowing only that committing grave offenses obstructs Bodhi, they think, "That person is fit for cultivation, but I am not suitable. A dragon girl manifested in human form to warn the world:
"I am a beast—a donkey or a horse—and I am the same as them."
If one does not see the Tathāgata’s opening of the secret instructions, enemies will overlap from the past, present, and future. The nature of sin is like space, and all phenomena are likewise;
when both sin and phenomena are forgotten, the mind becomes crystal clear.

There were two bhikṣus who committed sexual misconduct and murder; they lamented and reproached themselves, yet lacked self-awareness. Dwelling far away in forests and wilds, they hoped to realize the truth;
but in the vast expanse of one's own karma, who can escape it?
Upāli, your increasing of karmic fetters through the glow of mere words is merely reciting the texts of the Hīnayāna; when one reaches this point, doubt gives way to trepidation.
Do not blame the sutras, for it is simply that I am personally unskilled.

The Great Being Vimalakīrti suddenly dispels all doubt; transcending the four propositions and severing the hundred negations, within the gateway of true reality there is no "mine"—the single wheel of the moon of mind shines eternally bright.
Just as the blazing sun melts frost and snow, the ocean of karma is exhausted in an instant. The body of Vairocana is revealed without division;
there is no other artifice or understanding capable of being established.
The power of inconceivable liberation is not attained outside of the mind of contemplation. One phrase encompasses the eighty thousand gates;
by the wild bridge, the golden willows display their lingering hues.

Its wondrous function is as infinite as the sands of the Ganges; how could it begrudge those from all quarters who come to question and examine it? Why labor to raise a finger or employ verbal explanations?
At the tip of the staff is a single eye, as bright as the sun.
I dare not decline the toil of the fourfold offerings; yet the *maṇi* jewel possesses the highest value. Let your treasures fill the three thousandfold world-system at will;
their nature brings no benefit, being merely abundant and grand.
Even ten thousand taels of gold could not exhaust it; what common dealings can a man of the Way have? In his family home, from generation to generation, there was not a single coin;
yet he broadly ferries across the sands of the three realms all those who wander as guests.
To grind one's bones to powder would not suffice as recompense; consider how they have diligently cultivated their strength through many kalpas. Now that it is entrusted to me, no one seeks it;
let the body be released to sleep at ease upon the tips of the hundred grasses.
A single phrase, clearly understood, transcends ten billion worlds. Suchness is unmoving; not even a hair’s breadth of effort is required. With the Universal Eye, one should contemplate it as such:
on a spring morning, the mist blends with the azure sky.

The King of Dharmas is most supreme; within a single mote of dust, his light is inexhaustible. His boundless physical forms enter into every atom, constantly and universally responding by turning the Great Dharma Wheel.
Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges all bear witness together; their lights interpenetrate one another without exception.
Each extends his right hand to stroke his crown, while billions of devas and nāgas all take refuge.

I now understand this wish-fulfilling jewel. Regardless of whether one is poor or wealthy, it bestows its grace upon all; appearing and disappearing, coming and going, without deficiency, it enters the four modes of birth and the six realms of existence without exception.

Those who receive it with faith all attain resonance; they do not fall into the extremes of existence or non-existence, nor the categories of ordinary or sage. A pure breeze blows from all eight directions as the universe expands;
the sun and moon follow their own nature entirely.
Clearly seeing that not a single thing exists, there is only the natural, original oneness of the Buddha. Within the belly of Samantabhadra, one meets Avalokiteśvara;
Sudhana bows his head and calls it marvelous.
There is neither person nor Buddha; within the vast, towering halls of Maitreya’s residence, the gates are flung wide open to welcome all living beings.
In a single thought-moment, when free from the calculating mind, one attains full mastery.
The great trichiliocosm is but a bubble on the ocean; why need the spring breeze nod its head in assent? A single branch amidst the snow reveals all secrets;
dispatch it swiftly by courier to the Prince.
All worthy sages vanish like a flash of lightning; the Immutable Wisdom-Honored One is the color of lapis lazuli.
A mass of purple-gold light disappears behind the balustrade, as he speaks of Shan Shan and Shi De.

Even if an iron wheel were to spin upon the crown of one’s head, the divine light of ten thousand miles would manifest naturally within the body. Demons and spirits would be like snowflakes flying into boiling water;
how could they possibly disturb the old woman’s Chan?
Samādhi and prajñā are perfectly clear and bright, never lost; though heaven turns and earth revolves, the light remains luminous and tranquil.
The extinguished fire blazes forth again, ever new; in this matter of suchness, who truly understands?

The sun may become cold and the moon may become hot; ordinary people, through their inverted application, bring about destruction. The Great Way is perfectly luminous, its single nature all-pervading;
who can distinguish between spring, summer, autumn, and winter?
The various Māras cannot destroy the True Teaching; the True Teaching is wordless, its light vast and penetrating. It encompasses all phenomena yet has never been born.
Heaven and earth lose their sharpness, and all tongues are rendered mute.

The majestic elephant carriage advances in vain upon the rugged path; its vital energy surges toward the Ox and Dipper constellations, illuminating the dark thoroughfare. The sun and moon lose their luster—dare anyone dare look upon them?
Ten thousand evils are melted away by the frost, leaving no trace of their form.
Who has seen a mantis able to block a chariot track? A firefly on the seventh night attempts to swallow the bright moon;
the Weaver Girl’s heart is broad and she makes no sound, while the Oxherd’s single blow is broken against the void.
The great elephant does not wander upon the rabbit’s path; one pays homage to Avalokiteśvara atop the point of a needle. Even from the top of a hundred-foot pole, one must advance further;
throughout the dust-motes of the ten directions, the entire body is revealed.
Great enlightenment is not constrained by minor details. One plucks snowflakes from within a fierce furnace of flames.
When Shitou extended his feet to show Changzi, what room was there for the practice of cultivation to intervene?
Do not slander the vast azure sky with your narrow, biased views; like a frog at the bottom of a well or an ox by a riverbank, you boast of the great ocean.
Heaven, earth, and the great world are but a single eye; when brought into use, it is like a mere hair-tip.

I have not yet clarified this; now I shall resolve it for you: Not a single word remains, there is nothing to be said. Shining through antiquity and soaring through the present, it is a brilliance that penetrates to the very bottom.
Without departing from its own substance, it is eternally radiant and pure.
The Song of Pupan: This very Pupan is pure treasure; adorned with wondrous wisdom, it is truly exhilarating. Taking the Gateless as the door, those who reach it are rare;
ten-thousand-mile divine light forms a perfect canopy. This formless body is nowhere not present; its essence is revealed in full majesty within sound and form.

Externally, how could one follow the world’s dreams and illusions? Having transcended the world, who would be willing to cherish it? With the cessation of mental consciousness and the absence of the realm of form, Vimalakīrti lay ill while Śāriputra sought his explanation.
Pointing to the provisional to lead toward the real, he delivered sentient beings. Do not say that the ancient sages were practicing deception or eccentricity;

awakening to the fact that Pú-ān (Universal Abode) is fundamentally indestructible, even though the empty kalpa has its limits, he remains sovereign. How could the four modes of birth and the six paths of existence [confine him]?
Interrelated. When both self and object are forgotten, the mind alone is supreme. There is neither "within" nor "not within. The Ocean Seal emits light—whom would dare to face it?

The myriad phenomena of the universe are gathered within the Universal Hut (Puan). This absolute, numinous clarity is fully realized; forget subject and object, and do not rely on intellectual understanding.
Among tiles and pebbles, who would dare to purchase the true gold? If it were not for the arrival of the Old Barbarian (the Buddha), one could hardly encounter it face-to-face.
Lun Jieqin, with snow reaching his waist, sought instruction; having attained the essential meaning, he forgot words and advanced without regression.

A hundred-forged vajra, a holeless hammer—intended to sever the sins of tortoise-hair and rabbit-horns. Now I have understood the wish-fulfilling jewel: it dispels the obscurations and delusions across every land and every atom of dust.
Upon the tip of a single hair, the magnitude of the great thousandfold world-system shines forth, piercing through the bag of ignorance and birth-and-death.
The *Xianyuan ge* reveals that one fails to recognize the original jewel of one’s own house; submerged in the dust of conditions, one finds pleasure in the cycle of birth and death.

The *ālayavijñāna* stores ignorance, while the eighteen realms form a web of entanglements and a covering. Greed, anger, and delusion are ever-present; within the mirror of the mind, they are like empty flowers appearing in the sky.
Externally, they do not know that the body is a provisional formation of the four great elements; they falsely cling to the six sense objects, increasing their craving.

Deluded regarding this mind, they remain within the three realms; the vast expanse of the great earth—who understands it? Relying on a teacher, one studies the precepts, meditative concentration, and the sutras;

yet upon hearing that all is empty and true, one immediately gives rise to strangeness. Among worldly things, there is nothing that does not decay; only the Dharma-body remains eternally present. A single hair swallows the vast ocean...

Who would have known? To contain Mount Sumeru within a mustard seed is truly most wondrous. Fundamentally there is neither outside nor inside; the dharmas of mind are formless and without counterpart.
Even if one were to hypothetically bestow the seven treasures filling the three thousandfold world-system, the Way-eye remains unopened and the mind does not accord with it.

Do not speak of knowing, cease talking of understanding; the Dragon Pearl is not for purchase. Where its use is inexhaustible, it is shown to sentient beings; those whose consciousness cannot break through will still [be lost].
□□. To listen to words as if they were instruction is to fail to transcend the arising and retreating of the Śrāvakas;
in a single thought-moment, one enters the ranks of Māra, and for ten thousand kalpas, one vainly incurs the sins of Avīci Hell. Originally there is nothing to transmit, so do not seek a solution;
this very numinous light is ultimately never obscured. Vast, it has no boundaries; subtle, it is without dust. The single wheel of Perfect Enlightenment is a wish-fulfilling pouch.
A single mani-ga is not a mani-jewel made of jade or shell; it is the unshakable, expedient skillfulness that adapts to conditions. Boundless and unmanifest, it truly precedes heaven;
