from antiquity until now, it remains without cover or concealment. The six harmonies do not reside in a shared mind; they flow freely and expansively throughout the mundane world.

Externally, there is nothing within this that can represent True Suchness (*tathatā*). Who would not love that which is neither extinguished nor born? Standing firm upon empty space, it establishes the world;

yet who understands that which is neither the realm of elements nor empty space? Turn back and look within yourself—there is not a single thing. The light is great, perfectly interfused, containing a hundred wonders.
The substance of the pearl is solid, yet the hundred wonders dissolve. Illusory transformations are originally empty, for the numinous source remains. For thirty years I have watched the water.
The ox; this alone is the true marvel of Mount Huai. Linzi’s penetration is not within the conventional. He kicks over the pure pitcher, transcending all opposition;
above heaven and below heaven, he alone is mysteriously numinous. To this very day, few people understand. Old Nanquan displays his own views;
he picks up the cat, yet no one buys it. With a single stroke, he cuts through both ends without division; lords and attendants are layered upon one another.
From the beginning there was no turning away. To realize that which is beyond words is to hear the wondrous ocean; when drilling for fire, one must not let up even upon encountering stubble.

Suddenly, the bright sun melts the frost and ice. When not a speck of dust remains standing, who would suffer retribution? The heavenly net is vast, neither bound nor released; it is all-pervasive and expansive—this very samādhi.
How laughable is the measureless man of Hengyang, dragging his cloth bag within the light of Maitreya!

The Great Being Dazhi composed the *Song of the Twelve Hours* to warn those of the Two Vehicles who cling to signs and pursue them in haste, and to uplift those who stagnate in emptiness or dwell in silence, failing to achieve full realization.
Regarding these sincere words, the Elder Puan has turned them over a hundred times and a thousand ways; their exquisite subtlety lies in being beyond words.
This teaching brings the realization of the meaning of inexhaustibility; such profound penetration occurs frequently, yet those who possess it are rare indeed.
Since I have found beauty in this dream-vision, I shall not hesitate to speak even in my sleep. To continue this lineage, one must return to that nostril which reaches the vast heavens;
nodding in agreement, one realizes emptiness and becomes a fellow traveler with me. Thus, I sing: [Song]
At dawn it is the hour of Yin; when the rooster crows and the dog barks, the perfect sound is complete.

This very perfect sound has but one hearing—why labor with deluded thoughts to seek a truth elsewhere? When the bells and drums are struck, there is ultimately no sound; that which is fundamentally soundless is truly worth listening to.
Sound is a hollow shell for the guest at the gate; the essence that merges with sound and emptiness is the person within.
The sun rises at the hour of Mao; eating the morning gruel, one feels full without conscious intent. Having washed the alms bowl, all is naturally tranquil and still.
Only then can one believe that Zhaozhou’s wit was so skillful—a lion cub with golden fangs and claws, who startles to death the tigers and leopards of a hundred years.
He seizes the strange Manjusri and rides him upon his head; even those of the Two Vehicles all say it is a magnificent adornment.
At the hour of eating, the Ox King performs a dance with joyful laughter. "Lacquered bucket, lacquered bucket, eat!"—who among those traveling to study the Way recognizes this grandmotherly heart?
The intent of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is right here and now; there is neither self nor other. Xuefeng pointed to it as a single mirror;
for kalpas on end, the monkey has endured bitter hardship.

At the hour of Youzhong (Yi). I inform you: there is no gate or portal to learning the Way. The Buddha’s words in all the sutras point to this very mind. When this mind manifests, one attains quiescent extinction.
Fundamentally there is no delusion; how could there be enlightenment? The true self is not the body—who is there to act or contrive? Greed, anger, ignorance, and attachment belong to sentient beings;
for the one who realizes this, everything is nothing other than the path to Nirvana.
At noon in the land south of the sun, the great earth originally lacks even an inch of soil. Above heaven and below heaven, he alone is honored;
dazzling the eyes and piercing the pupils, there is nothing to be seen. Stone Gong met Mazu in his folly; when one’s own nature is like space, who can shoot the crossbow?
Sanping spoke the Way by splitting open his chest; failing to brace against the arrowhead, he merely suffered in vain.

Before noon has passed, Xuan Sha, carrying his board, loves the turtle-nosed snake. How many have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives? Opening their mouths, they send forth their eyes—where can they hide?

Not penetrating the source, they speak only of drowsy, confused talk; their karmic consciousness is vast and empty, with no foundation to rely upon. Blind practitioners fail to realize the one who plays with snakes;
they are constantly played with by the snake until its head pierces through their nostrils.

The hour of Bu (the seventh watch), the office drum thuds—a wondrous and fresh sound. Encompassing the earth and including all of heaven and man, none can comprehend it; like wild horses galloping across the plains, they enter the ford of delusion.
Do not grasp at appearances; let there be no distance between the familiar and the strange. The true body stands majestic and grand, utterly free from the dust of obscuration.
In a single thought, the butcher is rid of all karma; in an instant, the dragon girl becomes a Buddha-body.

The sun sets in the hour of You (17–19 p.m.); ten thousand households and a thousand homes have no distinction between them. They call out to one another as they go and return; who recognizes that this single body is neither beautiful nor ugly?
It has neither head nor hand; though the kalpa-fire blazes fiercely, it remains indestructible. Pigs, sheep, oxen, and horses are transformed into reality;
not a hair’s breadth remains, and there is nothing to be grasped.
At dusk, during the hour of Xu, the watches are distinct and the darkness is as black as lacquer. A single ray of constant light transcends all worldly comparison;

its coming and going are impassable, for it is a dense accumulation of gold. Whether known or unknown, whether recognized or unrecognized, from antiquity to the present, it is not to be sought without.
What does the wooden woman do on this clear night? She blends with the moon, idly blowing her holeless flute.

At the hour of Ren-ding (Hai), a stone falls; yet the foolish person continues to pound with the pestle. Suddenly, an ancient rhombus flower is ground out, shining upon earth and heaven without partiality.
Do people of the present day understand this or not? Before you have realized it, you must first eliminate craving.
When sentiment is forgotten and thought is exhausted, one reaches the state of non-reliance; the essence is like empty space, neither internal nor external.
At midnight, the hour of Zi: when all things are devoid of mind, who could reach this state? Upon a single hair-tip, one attains universal perfection;
for eternal kalpas, one shall not be ensnared by demons or malevolent spirits. Ascending the high platform, he beats the great drum; glaring with eyes and shaking his head like a tiger.
When pigs and sheep have been devoured, he further harms men; if one is not true to oneself, there will be suffering for long kalpas.
At the hour of the Cock-Crow (1–3 a.m.), flying through the air and landing on the ground, they run in waves. Śaṇmukha has regained his head; it remains as before, no different from his original one.
There is neither non-existence nor existence; since existence and non-existence do not apply, cease opening your mouth. Who knows when you raise the mallet or brandish the whisk?
To chase tracks and seek out the stench is truly the work of a hunting dog.
The Song of Master Shitou’s Thatched Hut I ask you who travel to study the Way: do you understand? By no means should you compare it to thatch or tiles;
Three inches beyond the hook, he catches the clear waves.
I have tied together a thatched hut with no precious treasures; day and kalpa after kalpa we accompany one another—who understands this?
It is only because the impoverished son has not returned home that he cannot avoid appearing before us to manifest such strange wonders.
Having finished eating, he leisurely seeks a nap; the bright sun shines in the sky, yet there is nothing to bask in. Thin clouds and light mist vanish into the void;
though they fill the void to satiety, they are utterly powerless.
When it was completed, I first saw the fresh thatch; I temporarily donned a hundred-patch robe to force myself to read the sutras. Fortunately, Yaoshan provided a decisive breakthrough;
a single phrase of the separate transmission awakens the human heart.
After tearing it down, he once again covers it with thatch; when rain falls and the wind blows, there is no obstruction. Why would he be willing to cast away his soiled robes?
It is only for fear that sentient beings might find it difficult to understand.
The person dwelling in the hermitage is manifest in their true nature, majestic and beyond old or new. To have even a hair’s breadth of deviation is the seed of the demonic path;

where not a single speck of dust stands, one wondrously penetrates the Truth. It is eternally present—neither sitting in meditation nor performing prostrations. The ultimate reality has never required cultivation; it transcends antiquity and surpasses the mundane.

Now encompassing the Dharma-realm, it belongs neither to the middle nor to the internal or external. Reclining alone upon a solitary peak, who could be one's counterpart? Among the millions of dragons and devas, who knows this?
The golden-colored dhūta understands within a smile.
Where worldly people dwell, I do not dwell; though giving leads to birth in heaven, one ultimately falls. The numinous light shines alone, with nothing else remaining;
ordinary folk who have not yet reached it sleep with their eyes open.
What the world loves, I do not love; this pleasure is the cause of suffering, so one should withdraw from it early. When will the six realms and four modes of birth ever cease?
Only the great man possesses such noble resolve.
Though the hermitage is small, it is silent and vast, beyond all boundaries. Within it dwells alone one who is true and authentic; penetrating form and merging with sound, he is ever luminous.
Encompassing the Dharma-realm, the great earth and Mount Sumeru are contained within a single mustard seed. This is never transmitted to outsiders or *śrāvakas*; it is ultimately—
As the mind itself understands, the Elder of Fangzhang embodies this realization; a single silence encompasses all, without small or great. Mañjuśrī’s praise is truly rare and extraordinary;
his inquiry into the illness was beyond his capacity, for he knew he had failed himself.

The Bodhisattvas of the Supreme Vehicle believe in this without doubt; for the sake of the Dharma they would forget their very bodies—such is rare in the world. Even if one were to grind one's bones to powder and shatter one's body to pieces, one could not yet repay [the Buddha's kindness];
the lesser fruits of the Śrāvakas are ultimately difficult to comprehend.

Those of middling and inferior capacity who hear this will surely give rise to strangeness. Clinging to existence while attached to non-existence is the joy of birth and death. Those who change their heads and alter their faces will return once more;
through vast kalpas they wander in obscurity, receiving retribution in vain.

Questioning this hermitage: who is there who can directly accept and take responsibility for it? Without relying on fine timber or a skilled craftsman, it is adorned with the wondrous majesty of the layered Indra’s net.
Whether destroyed or not, refined adamantine fills the dharma-realm; not even a single atom is established, like empty space. Only then can it be so named.

As Avalokiteśvara, the Lord of both destruction and non-destruction is fundamentally present; having attained this, one should remain earnest and never allow it to grow dim. Even in brothels and taverns, he transforms them into radiant light;
transcending all categories and peerless, what obstruction could possibly hinder him?
Not abiding in the south, north, east, or west—since the myriad dharmas are unborn, what is there to doubt? The trees on the crags and the ferns in the courtyard manifest wondrous forms;
the cries of monkeys and the chirping of magpies respond to the true mechanism.
The firmness of the foundation is supreme; ten billion hammers may strike it, yet it cannot be opened.
When concentration and wisdom are perfectly luminous, there is no "I" or "mine"—only then does one know that Bodhidharma never came.
Beneath the green pines, jade-like sounds fill the earth; who knows their value? Boundless cleverness merely speaks of emptiness; when asked about true emptiness, one fears for one's life.
Within the bright window, all is radiant and free from dust, with no weeds to cover it; yet to point to this and call it Bodhi is not truly real. [The white] at the crown of the head.
Opening up total realization:
even jade palaces and crystal towers do not serve as its counterpart. Guiding sentient beings with compassion only increases their thirst and craving;
he lets loose the water-buffalo of Mt. Gui, its shimmering brilliance difficult to conceal upon the open ground.

Wrapping oneself in a patched robe with the head covered, all affairs come to rest. For nine years facing the wall, he became a model for those lost in delusion. Shen Guang severed his arm—how rare and extraordinary!
Sattva threw himself from a cliff to feed the tigers in search of the Way.
At this moment, even this mountain monk has no understanding. It is like the great void, without interior or exterior; responding and transforming as the occasion demands is not the truth.
To seek it elsewhere is to turn one's back on oneself.
Dwelling in this hermitage, I have never burned the incense of conditioned phenomena. All day long I show it to you, yet you do not see it; there is nothing else remaining for you to contemplate.
Cease forming interpretations. All wonders are profoundly mysterious and beyond grasping. Mañjuśrī brandishes his sword to confront the Tathāgata—five hundred voices!
Upon hearing this, the mind is suddenly opened and liberated.
Who would boast of spreading out a mat to entice others to buy? There is no need for literary skill or scholarly erudition; shatter the void and return home.
Departing from the mundane world, one enters the Dharma-realm.
Turning the light back upon oneself, one returns home; the nostrils are vast and the celestial eye opens wide.
Originally, the Buddha-dharma is not much at all—three successive blows with the fist strike one's own stupidity.
The vast and penetrating spiritual faculty is neither oriented toward nor averse to anything; it has no concern for Mount Nanyue or Mount Tiantai.
That first realization prior to the birth of one's parents was when Xiangyan struck the bamboo and his delusion finally opened.
Meeting the Patriarch, the profound mechanism was not in accord and the Way grew ever more remote. That "spiritual awareness" is not the Dharma before one's eyes;
the Dharma before one's eyes cannot be named or modeled.
Through his personal instruction: "The dull axe opens the mountain into a hundred fragments; do not seek the various sages to enter the Mystical Source—like snow falling on red."
The hearth is square and the facing is symmetrical;
bind grass to make a hut, yet do not give rise to retreat. Though a hundred birds carry flowers, they do not come; though the flowers bloom, they are blown down by the wind.
Without the spring breeze, the flowers would not bloom.

Having cast aside a hundred years, he acts with total freedom; his single shoe returning to the West manifests non-arising. Coming and going, there is fundamentally no permanence—only constant, profound stillness;
mind-to-mind transmission is called the "Lamp of the Dharma."
Waving his hand, he departed without fault. You who travel to various quarters, do not misunderstand this: for ten thousand kalpas, it is but a single radiance;
unmoving, it pervades all realms of dust and oceans of lands.
A thousand kinds of words; the teachings of the sūtras are like the trap and the weeder’s pole. When the fish and the rabbit are caught, they do not reside in the speaking.
When the merchant reaches the shore, he has no need for the boat.
Ten thousand ways of understanding—written with brush, engraved on stone, and sold everywhere. Not a single character is given to others to rely upon; it stands revealed and solitary.
Ah! How bright and clear!
It is simply to ensure that you remain forever unconfused. Wherever the eye falls, there is no limit and no duality. In walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—who is it that comes?
To discard the turnip and seek the mustard leaf.
If you wish to recognize the immortal person within the hermitage, how many times does darkness fall and then dawn again? Light and dark do not come to him, for he remains unmoving;
he is as vast as the heavens and the earth, equal to the emptiness of space.
How could it be separate from this present skin-bag? The mind-dharma is formless like the great ocean; vast and expansive, it harbors no corpses.
For ten thousand ages its radiance blazes forth, never changing.

The Song for Reviving the Living, Great Sage’s Miraculous Efficacy, by Puan Yuan. Widely bestowed upon all sentient beings who encounter the right conditions, it brings forth spiritual resonance through pure faith;
myriad illnesses are simultaneously dissolved, and karmic transgressions are released. The essence and function of Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are manifested within this Song for Reviving the Living.

Immortal! The Kings of Medicine, Bhaiṣajyarāja and Bhaiṣajyasamudgata, employ no other arts; Bian Que and Sun Zhen spoke with one voice: "Divide the dose into three servings and decoct them in pure water.
Do not defile the field of the mind with the flavor of blood. All things that have form are my own body; simply practice compassion and virtue to dissolve enmity and resentment.
When there is no thought within and no conditions without, what need is there for divine prescriptions to be passed down behind the elbow? Body and mind are originally of gold."
The firm body does not understand that the mind is entangled by karma. When medicine and disease are dissolved, the moon of the mind becomes full.

At the time of faith, how could the Buddha be found only in the Western Heaven? He is present everywhere; all people possess him. This peerless spiritual source in the world removes the stains of transgression and liberates one from a hundred grievances.
It enables the dark clouds to clear away, revealing the sky of ultimate meaning. Through faith, one knows that "self" is not the culprit—then who is the illness? This is the Great Being, Vimalakīrti.
Sleeping within a smile; I am not mad for the sake of the sicknesses of sentient beings. When the body merges with sentient beings, my own sickness is healed.
Who dares to speak of the Dharma-gate of non-duality? The golden-maned lion reveals its entire form. Hasten to take the medicine to untie the bonds of worldly conditions.
Do not follow the deluded masses who mistake their eyes for those of a sage. Responding to conditions as they arise is neither difficult nor easy; when grasped by the hand of faith, it costs nothing.
Song of the Great Bell (Composed upon the casting of a bell through the munificence of Yi Jo-won) Jo-won, Jo-won, has offered this one bell;
suspended in space, it warns the blind and the deaf with every strike. Its round sound never ceases as it pervades the dharma-realm;
its pure essence is diamond-like—neither empty nor non-empty. Though it contains resonance, it is penetrated at the moment of being struck; the Buddhas of the ten directions respond to its voice.
Within, the devas and the eight classes of beings feel joy; without, the heretics and demonic armies lose their tracks. This is the great divine power of the Perfect Vessel.
May it pray for the inexhaustible longevity of the Emperor and Kings. May the sun and moon shine long and the state remain tranquil;

may ministers be loyal and sons filial, continuing the legacy of Yao. May the deluded be awakened and the ignorant become wise; the people sing with full bellies as their harmony deepens. Earth, water, fire, and wind are all in accord.
A single nature; the essence of the dust motes of all lands is interpenetrating and harmonious. Encompassing sound, it seals the stubborn void; birds, trees, cliffs, peaks, wind, and moon are one.
Why was it necessary in the Qin era to drive the mountain-bells? The great resonance of the golden bell is entirely free from emptiness. When the time comes, they meet of their own accord.
If you are willing to believe in the mindless, you will reach the fundamental source. To harmonize as one clan, offer gold and jade; turn toward Nanquan to cast [the bell].
This bell, from the twilight until the fifth watch, rings out incessantly, penetrating to the very depths. Near patriarchs and distant masters alike are deluded by intellectual understanding;
hearing this, they return to the Pure Land and prostrate before the Golden Countenance. Fellow practitioners of Nirvana share a single mind; each one fully utters its sound to praise this merit.

Revealing principle and extolling the Truth, there is no second hearing; all sentient beings, down to the crawling insects, are enlightened at once. This is the bestowal of the Dharma upon those who receive it.

This is emptiness. Furthermore, there are neither hells nor boiling bronze. Filial sons and obedient grandsons bring forth radiant and far-reaching blessings; their virtue shines through the ages, upholding the family tradition.
Opening the Bell to Address the Assembly: A Dharma Talk.
In the general there is the particular; in the particular there is the same. Success and failure do not concern this single bell.

Having gathered up the oil-frying cauldron and the fire-griddle, the ritual vessel melts perfectly, bringing relief to the blind and the deaf. (Pointing his finger at the bell, he says: "Does the assembly recognize this object?"
(After a long silence, he said: "It cannot be known by means of wisdom; it cannot be recognized by means of consciousness.

If you wish to attain true insight, this does not descend from heaven nor emerge from the earth, nor is it produced by deluded thoughts. Its solitary standard transcends all kalpas and has never been born;
its singular prominence surpasses all achievements and has never perished. To dream that sentient beings turn their backs on awakening is inevitably to suffer a total failure."
Holding up a yellow leaf to stop a child’s crying, establishing provisional names to point toward Buddha-nature;
realizing that all phenomena are oneself while remaining unattached to conditions, and using the single smelting of the great forge to cast one's entire being into perfection.

If you reach this state, there is no need for the furnace and bellows of the Three Vehicles, nor will you require the tongs and hammers of the Ten Sages; naturally, the single breath pervades everywhere, and the gold [is revealed].
The essence flows through in seamless integration. If one encounters a person of true understanding, why wait for the striking of the sounding board to begin penetrating the truth?
For those who have not yet realized this within, it does no harm to apply oneself. Good son, as for the place where one applies effort, the Buddhas provide their protection;
the dragon’s abode has no roof, yet its fangs and claws are formidable; the eight corners are manifest, and the golden script is clearly inscribed. Since—
"Arriving here, there is no burying it. Everyone who hears this must not give rise to doubt; this very state of 'no-hearing' is the complete self.
(He then picks up the mallet and suddenly looks at the assembly, saying: "O sons of the Buddha, you must by no means misunderstand. Each of you should direct your minds and listen attentively.
(He then strikes once with the mallet, sets it down, and says: "If you wish to understand the inconceivable, [look to] the bell..."
Realize it within the sound. Be careful.
Fifteen Verses on Learners and Those Beyond Learning:

I have often heard that the Way of learning does not depend on form; yet the Way, though not depending on form, is not separate from form. Not being separate and yet not depending—this is still like being asleep.
Speech: To investigate the nature of sleep-talking is to realize its original truth.

Cease seeking here and there; when you have attained it, how could there be further dryness or partiality? All conditioned phenomena are but dreams, and within the dream, the essence of clarity is just so.

Do not speak of right and wrong before others; that such talk does not reach them is truly extraordinary. Even if one were to discourse until the flowers of heaven fell, the mountains and rivers of the great earth would remain entirely unaware.
Wearing a withered skull upon his head, he strikes his own eyes; burning incense and prostrating with great diligence—when one blind man leads a multitude, who can understand?
How many people in the world have been deceived and led astray!

The illness lies with oneself, yet the fault is attributed to the teacher. If the teacher were to leave one, how could one endure the distress? All previously acquired learning and understanding would be forgotten;
bumping one's head and bruising one's brain, the mind becomes even more coarse.
Truly seeing Bodhi is called profound meditation; the great assembly opens up to pass the remaining years. Meeting fellow travelers on the Way, what words need be spoken?
Priceless pearls do not require money.

Bodhidharma came from the West wearing a felt cloak; he sat for so long at Shaolin that he seemed like a dull-witted fool. Such a brilliant manifestation has occurred not only in the past but also in the present;
who among the living beings of the Tang lands could have known it?
Old Lu obtained the robe that is not transmitted; descendants of later generations must not harbor doubts. Both the robe and the Dharma are not truly transmitted;
mind-to-mind, the seal of the heart, is utterly devoid of knowing.
The five schools and sects are in chaotic disorder; before reaching the Gate of Mystery, speech and silence contend. Deception and slander invite the karma of the Avīci Hell;
one must directly and fully fall into the deep pit.
Seizing the vital force of rebirth, he remains silent; though his ears are deaf and eyes blind, wondrous clarity arises. Following the stream, he desires only to transmit the mind-seal;
how could he be a monk who merely seeks sustenance through worldly sentiments?
Last night at the third watch, when the sun was at its zenith, the stars were full and the rain was misty. At the triple gate of the Buddha hall, they joined hands;
they wished to go to the Western Heaven, but the road was impassable.
Emerald bamboos and mountain tea reflect the setting glow; The cries of monkeys and the chirping of magpies—whom do they praise? When a single leaf falls, autumn pervades the entire world;
A slight movement of the spring breeze, and at once the flowers bloom.

The awakened person’s mind is tranquil and vast; the deluded are frantic, erring everywhere. When one universally observes both delusion and awakening, there is truly no cause—this is simply the Tathāgata’s Great Perfect Enlightenment.
A child of one year and an eighty-year-old elder—if one observes them, both youth and age are devoid of the true lineage. The world of sentient beings fundamentally does not exist;
its wondrous essence lies within the single nature of the person here and now.
The worlds of the ten directions devour one another by their very mouths; yet the uninterrupted, perfect sound proclaims the Universal Gate. Only Puan knows where this is preached:
there is but a single destitute man who wears no trousers.

The devas and nāgas sleep while speaking; the devas and nāgas listen in silence. The demonic hordes have their souls dissolved. Throughout the dust-motes and lands, down to the finest hairs, all are the non-duality of Pupan.

Why did he open this hermitage? He came to this place for this reason. Therefore, like water-moons and empty flowers, he manifests forms to respond to things. If one attains the state of no-more-learning...

The scholar, when facing the critical moment, does not rely on verbal explanations; upon a single awakening, he universally hears the wondrous understanding. How could this be associated with sound or form?
The words of Laozi and Zhuangzi do not reach it, and the phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are difficult to transmit. One should know it thus: provisional names are the true reality (*dharmatā*).

This true reality is neither empty nor non-empty. To cling to "non-emptiness" already violates the fundamental principle; when unity and multiplicity have no fixed position, who can make distinctions?
The myriad phenomena are arrayed within a single mirror; the hermitage is fundamentally no hermitage, neither opening nor closing. The nature of awakened awareness is itself the Tathāgata.

Seeking the source to its ultimate end, one is accompanied by mist and clouds; the scenery of the Southern Ridge returns as the days grow long. Above, not a tile of roof; below, not a needle’s point of land.
Having sought quietude amidst the clamor, there is nothing on which to rely. Many seek to strike upon those who possess no mind; yet, once the absence of mind is realized—
How could this be wrong? If you seek the Man of Puan through form, you will inevitably follow the current without reaching the ford.
From a thousand miles away, there is no coming; we share the same enjoyment. Transverse and vertical, wondrous function is one's own treasure. Do not wonder why he does not show his head;
having realized that the mind has no marks, he forever seeks nothing. Meeting him, who would perceive this as a dream within a dream? The waves are stilled, and he idly sails the Prajñā boat.
The Discourse on the Ten Mysterious Gates (with Preface) The Perfected Person has no self;
the Divine Person has no merit. Though they have no self, their formlessness is never-ending; though they have no merit, they penetrate all transformations.
The Way functions spontaneously; only the Spirit acts alone. When it acts, it is not acting; when it penetrates, it is fully penetrating.
If one has not yet attained full penetration and doubt has not been exhausted, so that even a hair’s breadth remains outside the mind, how can the Way of the Patriarchs be fully realized?
Jia Shan merely looks back to preserve the virtue of his teacher; this is far superior to the boat descending the waters at Huating.

If you now wish to inquire about the meaning of the Westward Journey, you will find that deep knowledge of "sleeping words" falls into the trap of stubborn Chan. Chan Master Tong’an Dacha left behind ten poems on the "Ten Mysterious Discourses" for the world. He once said:

It is revealed and manifested everywhere; yet those who frequently investigate its flavor are rare indeed. One might say that every character penetrates the essence without leaving a trace, and every word reveals the truth through selflessness.
These are words that moisten and benefit the world while remaining within it, and essential points that turn the pivot for those entering the secular realm.
They do not omit the balance of even and odd rhymes, nor do they lack literary vigor; they establish neither mere phenomena nor abstract principles—all [of which]...
There are no ten topics here. How could this compare to the paper and ink of the mundane world? It is not transmitted through the ears or eyes; it can only be realized through direct insight.

One may peruse the golden chapters, yet those who have studied much and heard extensively will find them difficult to penetrate. Only those who are free from such intervals of doubt can believe that the old man Puan’s “sleeping talk” was not in vain.
When one’s own mind alone affirms it, then beneath a single phrase, three verses are added, blending the ancient and the modern into one.
It consists of eighty verses. Having completed the verses, I still fear that learners may not yet discern them clearly.

Therefore, regarding the twenty characters of the title as the ten dharma-realms and the three causes, and taking these eighty phrases as the medicine for the eight liberations—whereby the disease of the causes is cured by the medicine of the phrases—I venture to ask about the method to save sentient beings of the future and to give rise to wondrous wisdom as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. For this reason, [I have] first provided the title and then...
Recite: "From the root, the branches are manifested; when both root and branches are fully revealed, it is only Master Chacha who can perceive this.
Puan was adding a head atop his own head—those who understand must recognize this. Those who do not know would simply say: 'The title of the verse is "As It Is" (Ruru).'"

Mind after mind is not non-mind; before one receives the seal, birth and death invade. Only when the single stroke is free from even the slightest obscuration are the six realms all marked as the form of the self—the Mind-Seal.
The patriarchs are like bells and drums; before they are struck, their resonance pervades the heavens. This illusory form and sound are fundamentally non-existent;
suchness is unmoving throughout past and present. This is the meaning of the patriarchs.

Profound and profound, it cannot be expressed in words. The sharp points of their wits meet like the tips of arrows joined together. When one attains the Way, there is no "mechanism" (artifice), for the profound is not limited.
This straightforward Suchness is manifold beyond measure—this is the profound mechanism.
Dust upon dust: turning one's back on awakening and wearying oneself creates the cause for the hells. The mirror reflects diverse forms, distinguishing black from white;
yet when merged with the primordial single nature, it is naturally the Heavenly Truth. (The dusts are distinct.)

Expound, expound! Do not merely hold the written texts spread out upon the desk. Teach others so that their precepts, concentration, and wisdom become firm and stable; let their knowledge, vision, and liberation be grandly manifested.
This is the exposition of the teaching.
Returning, returning. There is no need to descend into the water or climb the mountain; wherever one turns, the source is encountered, for name and reality are one.
From this point on, one wanders everywhere, resting idly amidst the clouds. This is the "returning to the source."
"Da-da. Pervading lands as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and as fine as motes of dust, it is originally wordless, like the springtime.
After the rain falls, the flower branches bloom throughout the night—this is the realization of the fundamental."
Again and again, eye-witnessing and mind-penetrating open everywhere; the faculty is deep while the essence is shallow—no one understands. "The wind and the Way fill the heavens;
I am the Tathāgata. This is the turning of the faculty.
Turn, turn! Do not cling to either end; choose the center. Who is this "true person of no station"? The nostrils of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are strung together like beads. Turning the position.
Each and every one is exactly like bird tracks across the vast void. Form is emptiness, yet emptiness is not empty.
Passing the days, he constantly blows the holeless flute—a single color.
A Verse on the Mind-Seal:

I ask you, what is the appearance of the mind-seal? Its reflection appears in a thousand ponds, its seal is upon ten thousand mountains. At night’s stillness, the jade flute blows from the painted pavilion.
The pipe: every sound corresponds, with no barrier between.
Who dares to receive and transmit the Heart-Seal? Disciples without a teacher—Buddhas and sentient beings alike—how many deluded thoughts have formed strange perceptions!
Clinging to objects and losing the mind, they prostrate before the patch-robed monk.
Throughout kalpas, it remains serene and without differentiation; what east or west could be established, and who would be north or south?
If you say there is a separate spiritual light, recognizing this is not true—it is originally a thief.
To call this the "Mind Seal" was but an early empty word; True Suchness fills the eyes and manifests of its own accord. Throughout the twelve hours of the day, there is nothing that does not respond:
a golden oriole sings by the willow, which holds the mist.
Although one knows that the essence is itself the nature of space, it merges as one with the profound abyss of reality like a mirror;
the myriad phenomena, though densely arrayed, are hidden within its depths, while the mani-jewel remains eternally pure, free from defilement.
This is likened to a lotus in a blazing furnace; refined gold becomes ever more radiant through a hundred smeltings. Dwelling in the world yet unstained, it is employed as circumstances require;
only then does one realize that the wind through the pines expounds upon Chan.
Do not say that a mindless state is the Way; tortoise hair and rabbit horns are not solid jewels. Who could establish a realm out of inert emptiness?
Failing to realize the vast source of the ten directions.
To be without mind is still like being separated by a single barrier; to linger in stillness and sink into emptiness is also a great difficulty.
Crying out to ask one’s mother, "Who is the mother?"—the idle clouds and mountain streams laugh with their gurgling flow.

The meaning of the Patriarchs, the meaning of the Patriarchs, is like space, yet it is not space. The Peng bird’s journey of ninety thousand *li* relies solely on the wind. If it were not for the wind, what use would its body be?
When one realizes that there is no space, the Way naturally becomes accessible.

The spiritual mechanism vies to fall into the functions of existence and non-existence; yet form and emptiness have not yet reached the state of "emptiness of emptiness. Form and emptiness are fundamentally without substance—these names are merely provisional designations.
When namelessness is fully manifest, the golden wind is revealed in its entirety.
The three types of worthies have not yet clarified this principle; the sheep, deer, and ox carts are but children’s play. Counting strokes and pacing back and forth is a labor spent in vain;
these are merely provisional names for the stage of Dry Wisdom.
How could even the ten sages reach this teaching? One must traverse kalpas for the Way to become manifest.
Starving and cold, they fail to recognize the lamp as fire, sitting in vain within their thatched huts by the gate.

The golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net still lingers in the water; the conscious spirit’s illumination and awakening is not the true knower of itself. When the willing mind enters the bird-path, that is *bodhi*;
for three coins, one buys up all of Luling’s rice.

On the return journey, the stone horse emerges from the gauze cage; its neighing awakens the wind after the rain throughout the world. It blows away the evening clouds until the solitary moon shines bright;
atop the perilous peaks, a bell tolls once from the mist-shrouded temple.
He earnestly explained the meaning of the Westward Journey; having attained the meaning, one forgets the words—truly non-dual. Last night at the third watch, he passed through the marketplace;
he heard only that rice was cheap, while oil and salt were dear.
Do not ask about the West or the East; how could one know that Buddhas and patriarchs are one and the same in emptiness? Throughout the four quarters and above and below it is thus;
yet alas, the ignorant and deluded cling to the notion of mutual containment.
The profound mechanism is so remote that even the void kalpa cannot contain it; neither form nor name, it pervades every place.
Without image and without mind, the pearl appears of itself; why labor in vain to seek it abroad?
How could one allow the defiled workings of the mind to form a bond? When will the merit of such practice ever reach completion?
Only by abandoning the views of self and person can the essence and function be fully integrated, attaining true freedom.
The wondrous essence has originally no location; transcending sound and form, it is neither now nor ancient. No title can describe it, and it is inconceivable to discuss or debate.
Do not be surprised that I dance so often.
Throughout the entire body, what further trace could there be? For thirty years I have watched the water buffalo; its nostrils are boundless and difficult to grasp.
It constantly partakes of the clarified butter, blending spring and autumn.
A single phrase, spirit-like, transcends all phenomena; it does not fall into the categories of sage or ordinary, nor does it employ artifice. With one long laugh, the mists and fogs broaden;
containing emptiness and stillness, its illumination extinguishes all thought.
Transcending far the Three Vehicles, it requires no cultivation; The single phrase of the separate transmission encompasses all under heaven. A raised eyebrow is already a sign of contempt;
If one attains the wondrous mind, rest there and cease.
Casting off the hand, one stands beyond the thousand sages; seeing and knowing, one does not congregate with the common folk. At the peak of the highest mountain, one rows a solitary boat;
within the sea, the furnace burns and smoke rises at will.
On the return journey, one is fit to be a bull in the fire; when a single leaf falls, ten thousand nations turn autumnal. With the moon bright and the waves calm, there is nothing else to do:
this mind remains ever upon the tip of the morning pole.
Dust differs from turbidity; the turbid is itself turbid and the clear is itself clear. A single wheel of pure white admits no dust. Who can distinguish beauty and ugliness within a mirror?
The moon in water is a fusion of light, the pure Dharma-body.
Enlightenment and afflictions are equal in emptiness; it is only within form that the application of indigo glue becomes refined. When salt enters water, it cannot be found;
with a light touch of the tongue, one smiles with joy.
Who says the jade of Bian has no one to appraise it? If you simply possess the willing mind, you will never be deceived. Even after burning away his eyebrows, he still knows nothing;
Xu Qi wishes to go to the Western Heaven to seek it out.
In my Way, the black pearl shines wherever it goes; encompassing all existence, it alone is luminous and spiritual.
When its light was matched and its price asked by someone, I opened both hands and displayed my cap-strap.
When the myriad dharmas are extinguished, the whole body is revealed; it is much like the Diamond Sutra after a hundred refinements.
When the light of samādhi melts away all subtle dust, the single eye is perfectly bright—what need is there for further seeing?

The three vehicles are merely provisional names established through conceptual differentiation; out of compassion for sentient beings whose habitual tendencies are deep, the City of Jewels is manifested as a mere transformation upon arrival.
Since when did Avalokiteśvara ever move a single step? He has long been there.
A man possesses his own will to soar toward the heavens; he does not cling to forms or names, nor to "is" or "is not. Penetratingly interfused, his radiant spirit is intense;
a golden-maned lion is truly formidable.
Do not tread where the Tathāgata walks; in a single moment, you will fall into a pit ten thousand fathoms deep. Though hundreds of billions of gods and spirits may support you, you cannot rise;
your ears shall hear no sound, and your eyes will be like those of the blind.

Expounding the teachings of the Three Vehicles, he sequentially unfolds the golden words. Their essential meaning pervades the heavens and should naturally connect. When the yellow leaves stop the child’s crying so he no longer wails, one only then realizes that for kalpas one has been exhausted as if in sleep.
Proclaimed together by the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, it has continued until now, though few have transmitted it. A wild goose is not the person who startles it into flight;
it is the wind striking the reeds that makes them cry out, echoing across the azure sky.
When first taught that there is emptiness, everyone clung to it; failing to clarify the principle and the phenomena, they labored in vain. As the years pass, their deluded attachments only deepen;
my heart feels no shame before others, yet my face burns with its own blush.

Later, when discussing emptiness and existence, the assembly all cast [their views] aside; with every word, they penetrate through emptiness into the vividness of form. From this, the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates enter;
nowadays, this is called "the grandmother’s Chan."
The Dragon Palace is filled with the treasury of medical doctrines; when medicine and disease correspond, the five flavors are eliminated. Jīvaka’s stirring of herbs was but great folly;
his foreign words were a chaotic pulling out of stalks, each one claiming it was the cure.

The crane and the tree finally discourse on the principle, yet it is not yet profound; from his mouth he spews forth what is as white as a lotus. With one flower and five petals, he personally transmits the entrustment;
I only fear that the eyes of sentient beings will be constricted by attachment.
Within the realm of true purity, even a single thought Means one has not yet left the stage of learning; there will always be a lack.
Exert yourself now to sever all names and words, So that for eternal kalpas you shall never again be stained by dust and defilement.
In Jambudvīpa, eight thousand years have already passed; morning and night we are busily dragged along by karma. How can one remain unmoved by the suffering of kalpas within a single dream?
Why not instead receive the manifest light before us?
Attain the source and do not seek the King of Emptiness midway; to kindle fire, one must still require the golden light.
Only by burning away the three thousandfold world-system can one find a way to live again from within death.
Carying my staff, I have returned to my native land of Sudatta; never before had I set foot here to see the Empress. After so long a separation, we meet face-to-face at last;
mother and child share a laugh that reaches the heavens.
When clouds and waters are parted, do not linger; you traverse the azure sky, encompassing heaven and earth. Let all things change and the scenery shift as it may;
I alone am True Suchness, perfectly embodying both Samādhi and Prajñā.
I have not forgotten the depths of the Snowy Mountains; throughout the hundred and ten cities, the seal shines everywhere.
When Maitreya’s tower opens and the path is cleared, one will finally know that the winter snow is like spring frost.

How lamentable that on the day he departed, his countenance was like jade; he often dwelt amidst white clouds, lodging in the void. Through thousands of turns and ten thousand circuits, it remained ever thus:
in the vast silence, he alone sang the song of non-arising.
Yet he sighs that his hair has turned white like frost upon returning; from his eyebrows and eyelashes, rays of light are emitted. What was previously irrational is now all explained;
laughing, he points to the muddy path adorned with the seven treasures.
Casting off all attachments, one arrives where family members do not recognize; tomorrow morning, north and south can no longer be distinguished.
Performing as the occasion demands, one plays with the spirit of Confucius, yet points back to the ox as Maitreya.
There is not another thing to offer in the honored hall; he carves out a silver basin that gleams like snow and frost. Once the arrow has left the string, there is no turning back;
Dongshan’s attempt to withdraw his regret was a failure of reflection.

Returning to the source and reverting to the origin—the matter of returning to the source has already gone astray. Wearing fine silk, one does not seek hemp outside; though weary toil is itself the truth, one still lacks faith.
Suddenly understanding the Way, one beholds the peach blossoms.
Fundamentally non-abiding, it is not called a "house"; there is only the road to the Western Region, which is not far. Three times his supernormal power of reading minds failed;
the National Teacher still caught a dead shrimp.
The pine paths of ten thousand years are deeply shrouded in snow; water cannot leak through, and there is no way to enter. When the gate of liberation opens, one step suffices for all;
with murmuring words in sleep, one distinguishes the black from the white.

A range of peaks is further shrouded by clouds; riding an iron horse backward across the shifting sands, the Buddhas of the East, West, South, North, and Center drink together from a single bowl of tea of heaven and earth.
When host and guest are harmonious, it is entirely delusion; meeting and seeing off, they divide the steps and alleys. The Old Barbarian did not recognize the warning to King Liang;
the Ratnākara-maṇi is the Treasury of Joy.
Ruler and minister dwell together; the center is precisely where the crooked resides. Name and appearance harmonize, yet their substance appears to differ.
One and two do not make three; "not so" is what reveals my own flawlessness.
How should the air of "Returning to One's Native Village" be sung? Butterflies flutter and orioles sing within the Great Dharma Assembly.
Only Heyshan knows how to beat the drum; Nanyue performing a dance is likewise commonplace.
Withered plum blossoms before the Hall of the Bright Moon; snow falls in profusion at the Gate of the Great Sun.
Within the Jewel Pavilion, many are strange and decayed. *Dharmāṇi hūṃ phaṭ*.

Turning the mechanism back toward the city of Nirvana is still fraught with peril; personally arriving at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa is not yet sufficient cause for wonder. Seeing the Buddha, one forgets cognition and is free from the notion of "mine";
the six sense faculties constantly revolve around Amitābha.
Meeting on a crossroad, there is no fixed time; when the serpent-wife comes with her command, who knows? Forty-eight people have become turtle-nosed;
quickly call the stubborn Chan monk to return from within the weeds.
Hanging up his soiled robes and claiming they were the Buddha—Śākyamuni was like a thief stealing a moment’s respite. Suddenly caught in the act, there is no leniency;
within the flames, Danxia is of pure golden hue.

Yet who could name those precious and imperial vestments? Once again, the lapis lazuli case is opened to radiate its original brilliance. To realize the Way, one does not eliminate provisional establishments;
the primordial essence of all things is, from the beginning, without remainder.
The wooden man puts on his boots and departs at midnight; the body born of realized intent has no dwelling place. Its wondrous function is difficult to transmit to the deluded mind;
I know you have not yet understood the phrase that penetrates all directions.
The barren woman returns at dawn wearing a cap; her entire body is clad in a six-zhu robe.
With a tongue that speaks words that are not sounds, she gives birth to a child who cries out, "A-ye! (O Mother!).

The moon in the empty sky over the ten-thousand-year-old emerald pool—how could its cries of the howling monkey ever cease throughout the night? How many have failed to grasp this single orb of light?
Only I share its radiance; who else can discern it?
Only after thrice scooping and searching does one finally know it; to seize a shadow and flee from its form is utter folly. The Great Compassionate One with a thousand eyes received but half;
the old fellow Vimalakīrti first brought forth the whole.
Shifting positions, clad in fur and bearing horns, they enter the vast expanse; beneath the waters, peach blossoms bloom time and again. Before the world was born, there was only this nature;
regardless of its transformations, how could it ever be subject to saṃsāra?
The *utpala* flower blooms amidst the flames; only now do we know that Bodhidharma’s coming was not in vain. Last night, a brief shower of clear and bright rain fell;
ten thousand plants and myriad blossoms surpass all artful cutting and shaping.
Amidst the sea of afflictions, you become rain and dew; the bottomless pit is transformed into a treasury of pearls. Alas, they do not recognize the night-bright curtain;
the painted vase is shattered, leaving nothing more to be done.
Within the mountain of ignorance, clouds and thunder arise; lightning and rosy light flash so brightly they cannot be parted.
With a single crash of thunder, the mountains and peaks tremble; the Great Being Mañjuśrī laughs heartily.
The boiling cauldrons and glowing coals are blown out by the teaching; once a day, three meals, and when full, one rests.
The hell-wardens, ox-heads, and evil yakṣas—being of the same breath and joined as branches, they should not be distinct.

The sword-trees and knife-mountains are shattered by a single shout; the seal of the ten pāramitās resides in the numinous terrace of the mind. Its light-wheel is inexhaustible—how could it have boundaries or limits?
It is not obtained from the roots of greed or anger.
The golden lock of the mysterious pass cannot detain him; piercing clouds and penetrating rock, he fills the universe. Silent through the four seasons, his faith is profound and vast;
transcending ten thousand kalpas, he seeks no peer.
Wandering upon divergent paths within saṃsāra, ten billion emanated bodies cannot be parted. Hell and heaven are not elsewhere;
they call out to one another, hidden within Mount Tiantai.
A single color;

withered trees and crags—before such a place, divergent paths abound. If one does not traverse the Bird Path, one will only become further entangled in confusion. Foxes lead one into the burrows of wild boars;
before long, one will form a mass and be seized by the Lord of Death.

When practitioners reach this point, they all falter; at the tip of a single finger, there is nothing to be done. A hair’s breadth of error leads to ten thousand differences—cranes standing in the snow are not of the same color.
Within the mirror, form and emptiness are not separated by anyone. It is neither green, yellow, black, white, nor red;
it is neither up, down, east, west, north, nor south.
The bright moon and reeds amidst the flowers are not like others; within them, a single breath presses against the celestial net. Amidst the shadow of Nirvana, there is no one to recognize;
with nostrils reaching to the heavens, he laughs at his elder brother.
When there is complete clarity, there is nothing to be clarified. Heaven and earth declare that I have no boundaries;
within the palace of Yama, the golden wind mingles, and in the hall of Tuṣita, all is bright and radiant.
Even the most profound depths of mystery must be rebuked; with a shout, the Black River was severed and its waves turned back. Send word to the elders of Eastern Wu:
it would be better for you to recite the name of Amitābha early on.
With earnest devotion, he sings the song of the profound mystery; the mountain stream joins in, its melody complete.
Only Boya wishes to reveal his artistry, yet the deep meaning of the severed strings remains uncontinued by anyone.

Can one grasp the moonlight within the void? By the time one waits for the wind to follow the teachings of Liezi, it has already slipped away. Though Mount Sumeru is seamless, stretching out one's hands is in vain;
even if one were prior to heaven, there would be nothing to do about it.

Truly, in establishing teachings to bequeath to the world, how could it be said that such persons are lacking? Yet, in manifesting the fundamental and marking the essential tenets, no scripture can compare to this one.

It is truly the eyes and ears of the Tripitaka, and the very source of the fruition of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. Like a vast and magnificent jeweled sword, its auspicious radiance remains unchanging;
like a brilliant and lustrous pearl, its pure brilliance cannot be obscured. [This was written by] Peng Fengyuan, Peng Bao, and Peng Dalin.
Li Shí, Li Guāngguó, and others personally heard this account; how could they dare not proclaim it?
Together they offered their family treasures, commissioning artisans to carve the woodblock in order to widely disseminate it for future generations.

May it serve as a contribution to those yet to come, as a magnificent legacy for ten thousand ages, and as the true sovereign of our own lineage. Thus we know that Pǔ’ān’s manifestation in the world was indeed ancient.
The Buddha’s return may be called an encounter once in a thousand years; how could one fail to record this for posterity?
On the full moon day of the last month of spring in the second year of the Qiandao era, the disciple Heguang Yingshi respectfully inscribed this.
Transforming rice, he strikes through the pass and shatters the golden lock; Buddhas and sentient beings are not two. Fully raising [the Dharma], he swallows the ten directions of space whole;
ten billion dragons and devas serve as his protectors. Singing a snow-song alone atop the ancient peak, wind, moon, stream, and mountain are one with him.
