To Peng Shengbo: A single pearl from the black dragon marks a thousand peaks; transcending antiquity and soaring through the present, it reaches everywhere. Yuan’s Chan path penetrates even the finest hair, yet remains utterly unobstructed;
only then does one know that the Buddha-dharma has never been exhausted. Flakes of solitary clouds manifest the Dharma of the mind; wild cranes perching on pines reveal the Way.
Self-contained, the thousand eyes find it difficult to behold—who can truly perceive it? A crimson banner unfurls directly beneath, raising a pure breeze;

wondrous enlightenment pervades the ten directions without a trace of form, and spiritual awareness within the three realms leaves no footprints. Therefore, one does not fall into the mechanism of coming and going, nor does one sink into the conceptualization of an intermediate state.
Whether true suchness, ordinary beings, or sages; whether hell or heaven—it must be returned to those who have realized the matter. Before one’s very eyes...

The mirror-like awareness breaks of itself; not even a single atom is established. The provisional Dharma is like a demon; being deluded by the pointing finger, one fails to see the moon—this is a great error in two respects.
Come and knock at the gate of Old Man Puan: how can the true mind be otherwise? Unless you yourself are willing, there is only the song of the "Vernal Spring" and the "White Snow.
To recognize the Tathāgata upon the tip of a hair, verbal explanations are mostly idle. When emotion is forgotten and thought is exhausted, [all is resolved].
Never ceasing this "Mahā. Eh? O worthy one, tell me: what is this? Cleverness cannot withstand the barrier of birth and death;
dry wisdom cannot escape the suffering of saṃsāra. Reaching this point, what more need be said of future fortune or calamity, or the causes and conditions of body and life?
Self-nature is fundamentally pure; within this wondrous perfection there is nothing else. Even empty space is...
It arises from delusion. Where else could there be such news? Nevertheless, it is not that it does not manifest within this [reality].
To speak of existence or to say non-existence is intended only for you to know where it falls. Form and emptiness are not different; a wise person should not look elsewhere.
For this reason, I now add these words of sleep-talk: "Yixuan, Yixuan (The Nourishing Studio). At this very place, all is serene. All dharmas return [to their source]."

1. Do not labor to seek it elsewhere; with no-mind, one accords with the Way, penetrating both the transcendent and the subtle. Its great function is majestic and grand—there is nothing that is not auspicious.
Written at Zifu Temple in Liuyang County. [Name] bows his head.

Upon the ancient bank of Xiao and Xiang, clouds of radiance rise from the very depths. Previously, I was graced by the arrival of your flying staff; less than ten days have passed, and here is a scroll.

The precious case fell from within the void; before it was even opened, auspicious light was beheld. As the golden wind pervades all realms, one knows deeply that only those who dwell within this state can truly perceive it.

These wondrous meanings at the tip of the brush serve as a source of merit. The ancients were concerned with the Way; how could they have worried that these peripheral matters would be difficult to accomplish?
If you are such a person, why worry that this matter will not be resolved? I am like a flower in the sky manifesting its form, or the moon in the water discussing Chan—using the Dharma...

The realms themselves constitute the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). To transform sentient beings is to perform the work of a Buddha. Your Lordship has reached the stage of "harmony with others" (*er-shun*), yet your nature remains pure and singular.

Although you were once deluded by non-Buddhist paths (*tīrthika*), you have already awakened to their error. You clearly realize that which is attained within one's own mind—that there is nothing to be attained.
O monk who has left the household life, simply recognize the mind; then there is no dharma that is not complete. Since you have already attained the mind, [all is fulfilled].

Yet the source is clear; responding to the various directions according to the Dharma, the great matter is not truly completed. Without moving, transformation pervades all lands. When Bodhidharma came from the West, he did not build a house;
when Puan entered the mountains, how could it have been for the sake of ascetic practice? A single orb of autumn moon reflects amidst the mournful wind;
several notes harmonize with the sound of pines to mark this meaning. When causes and conditions reach their ultimate end, do not weary your spirit; it is simply a matter of timing.
There is nothing that has not been prepared for your arrival; all that currently exists serves as a witness. You should take up the fishing rod yourself, lest you be toyed with by small shrimp.
As the Sūtra says: "Though it be a good cause, it can bring about an evil fruit. Let the carpenter cease his grieving over the lack of wine and meat;
together, let us avoid falling into the ranks of the māras. Simply attend to the year to come, and it shall ensure that the waves remain undisturbed. Follow along.

Make the mind a temple; let there be no other concerns. There is yet another excellence: it is simply this Amitābha. To provide the provisions for the feast, I have annotated the Heart Sūtra—this priceless *maṇi* jewel.
It awaits a rare merchant who can discern its value. That the impoverished son carries the treasure upon his back is because he has long been lost to the path home.

If one encounters a wondrous friend who points out the pearl, it will not be separated from within one’s robes. By believing, contemplating, and practicing with skill, one will return home before long to retrieve the treasure-store.
This Heart Sutra encompasses the five thousand-plus volumes of the Great Canon; it resides solely within the minds of ordinary beings.
If an ordinary being understands this sutra, how would they differ from a Buddha? One must rely upon the sutra to achieve realization and directly cut through to the source.

One must not pull through the beads of a rosary, thinking that one has finished reading the sutras, and then further burn paper money and draft memorial texts; such empty deception in performing meritorious acts only invites calamity.
If you understand the place where the Buddha taught—that which is neither existent nor non-existent—then you will comprehend the *Puan Anjie Zhu* (The Commentary on the Universal Hut).
If you realize your own nature, it is like space and devoid of marks; birth and death are called nirvana. Transcending others for a thousand ages, do not concern yourself with literary compositions.
To attain liberation upon hearing this once is no easy matter; it requires that one first provide offerings of food and drink with faith, and only thereafter request the sutra.
Furthermore, one must possess firm resolve in the mind. This is most fortunate.

The Song of Realizing Principle by Puan: To realize the mind and realize principle is not mere gibberish. He taught throughout the three thousand great thousandfold worlds, and every single one penetrated through mud into water.
One should give rise to the mind without dwelling on anything; furthermore, do not sacrifice to gods or worship ghosts. At all times, maintain pure mindfulness.
The Dharma-body—what need is there to burn money or transform paper? One shall not be deluded by demons or malevolent spirits. Each person shall exhaustively seek the ultimate truth.
This is neither a gathering at night to disperse at dawn, nor does it involve traveling far to seek mountains and waters.

It does not require making vows or burning incense, nor does it entail abandoning one's wife and children or abstaining from the taste of the blood of sentient beings. Rather, one simply honors one’s six relations and nine generations of ancestors, vowing never to drink alcohol.
Reckless and wild, you do not enter the bitter suffering of prison. When you see profit, your mind does not rest; in every place, you treat others as you would your own parents.
You struggle with ignorance, self, and others, yet I have nothing to do. Repairing bridges and laying roads according to conditions, my very body becomes mountains, rivers, and the land.
I make offerings to all sentient beings upon the great earth. May the imperial realm be eternally firm, and may the winds and rains be harmonious at all times.
The rains fall in season. Day after day, the people sing and dance; all this arises from the natural spontaneity of one's own nature, never entering the gates of others.

Now, seeking nothing at all, one does not cling to demons or succumb to their influence; remaining undisturbed right where one is, even the mundane tasks of carrying water and hauling wood are acts of Buddha-work.
What need is there to strike cymbals? Why use the hammer for the bell or the drum? Enough with such talk—just join your palms.

Taking refuge. Having long been scolded by those who travel to study under various masters, I realize that when the mind is universally present within the lotus, how is it any different from the Western Pure Land?

Since antiquity, there has fundamentally been no delusion; how could there ever have been awakening in the first place? Even if the three vehicles and five teachings were established, they would be like adding salt to vinegar.
Birth and death, as well as nirvana, are like a dream; the Buddha taught that there is nothing to be done. Yet you still ask about Bodhidharma.
The Patriarch from the West came with no other path; he pointed directly to the human mind as Buddha, without allowing for even a single step’s deviation.
As soon as there is the slightest trace of right or wrong, one enters the heterodox gates of Māra. Those who have attained life within death are protected by all Buddhas and celestial dragons;
they are men of iron resolve who cut through nails and sever steel. Such ordinary people settle their affairs once and for all. Nowadays, people praise...

The gods revere them; throughout ten thousand kalpas, the multitudes of spirits look up to them with longing. If one does not turn the mind upon reaching this point, how can one recognize the treasury of the *maṇi* jewel?
Benefiting self and others without exhaustion, passing through kalpas without fear or dread—clad in clouds and whistling at the moon, they chant the ancient style;
penetrating stones and piercing mountains, they discourse on the True Dharma. This very mind is like a skillful painter; this very body is like a seamless stupa.
The old woman of East Village is my mother; my father is Old Zhang of the South Gate.
*Puan Lu*, Volume Two; *Puan Lu*, Volume Three.
The Song of the Paper Quilt. To instruct the young novices:

the Buddha, through his great compassion, reveals to all sentient beings the gateway of skillful means. This is because all wriggling creatures and living beings possess, in essence, the single Buddha-nature.

It is only because emotions arise that wisdom is obstructed, and because conceptualizations shift that the physical form becomes distinct. Thus they drift through the four modes of birth and revolve within the six realms.

The realms of rebirth: through five hundred births and deaths, one may encounter a sage; if one accords with the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpāda*), one will forever transcend the ocean of suffering.
Failing to recognize such an encounter, one becomes further estranged by delusion and ignorance, desiring only to loathe death and cherish life, unaware that one has already donned fur and horns.

Having just departed from human form, one craves water and grass to survive. Once this human body is lost, it is difficult to recover for ten thousand kalpas. As vast as the sky hanging over the earth...
Yun: "Subtle as fine dust or ants, they arise in every thought-moment and perish in an instant. Thus we know what the Buddha taught: 'The three realms are mind-only;
all phenomena are consciousness-only. Consciousness is like a dream or an illusion; when the dream awakens, the truth remains. Now I lament for you:

your nature is originally true and divine, yet you have been deluded by these worldly pursuits. Having now encountered Puan to leave the household life and seek the supreme Dharma, this is surely due to your past merit."
This cause is likewise not accidental; it enables one to sever the conditions of craving and approach the ultimate principle. The *Complete Enlightenment Sūtra* states:
"If sentient beings, though seeking a virtuous friend, encounter those with false views and fail to attain correct awakening, this is termed the lineage of external paths.
This is the fault of the false teacher, not the blame of the sentient beings. If, upon seeing forms or hearing sounds, they seek the self..."

Your own conduct is perverse; how could it concern my faults? In general, one merely seeks to transcend the world. Regarding objects of desire, one points to tiles, rubble, walls, and fences as the reality.
Cutting through like iron and steel—such a fierce man! When leaving the household life, how could there not be a time of success?
Each and every one extinguishes the mind; everyone is in a state of tranquil illumination. If you attain this middle way, you will become one body with the great void.

Furthermore, what do you call the Dharma-body? It is that which enables one to be fully self-reliant and free from private interests, understanding that the billions of transformation bodies are one's own essence.
Let others become donkeys for the eastern house or horses for the western house; laugh loudly and sing with joy—who understands the "Snow Song"?

Unchanging through birth and death, transcending both past and present, this is the realization of the man of affairs. The merit of leaving the household life is by no means slight; it is simply this.
An ordinary person [was] partially in accord with Puan; they formed a karmic bond as master and disciple.

It was granted that for thousands and tens of thousands of kalpas, he would preach the Dharma without interruption, deliver immeasurable multitudes, and forever serve as an object of refuge for those in the heavens and an object of veneration for those in the human realm.
Had it not been so, he would have had no connection with Puan at all. Now, each of you has received the Three Refuges and the Five Precepts; however—
I shall cover you with this single mat. You may clearly take responsibility for it before the great assembly of devas and humans.
From early morning until late evening, as you wrap yourself from east to west—whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—examine closely: what kind of thing is this?

If you are a person who possesses nostrils, it is beyond the reach of words and explanations; but if you encounter one who is blind, you will find only a corpse that has ruined my bedding through its stench.
It is understood. Yet, though you speak, you do not know; though you act, you do not comprehend. You have alienated your own parents and turned your back on your six relations.

Having entered my sacred grove, you defile the latrines and walls with excrement and urine. Throughout the twelve periods of the day, you eat the food of the donors from the ten directions and wear the clothes of the parents from the ten directions.
You do not cultivate the Way, yet your karma is like the waters of the ocean. With a nature rooted in ignorance, why do you give rise to such thirst?
Cease! Your wisdom and compassion are not even a hair’s breadth present. For now you are but a novice monk; hereafter you will become a village dweller again.
Moment by moment, your own karma will entangle you, and at death you will sink into the Avīci Hell. How bitter, how painful! Once more, sighing in lamentation, it is truly pitiable:
even when the Buddhas appear in the world, they have no means to save you. Go properly to another's house and receive a full meal of chaff. *Jin*.
Neither of the two is lacking; each is fully sufficient. Furthermore, they are meticulously accounted for. Moreover, there are no idle people waiting about.
Each of you must exert yourselves with all your might. If the Old Monk were to recklessly assume responsibility for this, he would enter hell before long and fall forever into Avīci.
If you are here, do not let your days pass in vain. Take heed. A song says:
"A single sheet of white cloud hangs upon the body; When donned, it shall not be stained by the red dust of the mundane world. Light silk and fine textures can hardly compare to it;
Even pondering heavy brocade, one finds it cannot truly approach it. Is it not that its color is as white as jade? In its manifestation, it is entirely complete."
A single scroll. Its crimson window reveals a seductive beauty bowing her head. The six thieves and three corpses are all subdued. By day it serves as clothing; by night it provides a covering.
It is neither long nor short, neither large nor small. When people of the world ask me where to find it, I say: "The disciples of Cai Lun have brought it forth for sale.
Having purchased it, one wears it; not even demons or shadows are permitted to know of it. It can be used to shield oneself in the marketplace.

Clouds and rain; I wish to keep myself apart from idle people and their disputes. Though I may be wild and reckless, or even fall into ruin, I enter the villages with my robes on, regardless of others' loathing.
Even if offered purple ribbons and golden seals of office, I would not lightly exchange them for such things.
It is further said: "The black-sleeved cold robe fits the body; its rosy radiance flashes and swirls around the person. Whether walking or sitting, one looks at it repeatedly;
whether lying down or sleeping, one wears it every time. Several times I have entered the mountains to roam through sublime realms; many times I have sought it upon the sea."
Dragon-rider! Even if one possessed a thousand measures of gold, it would be difficult to purchase this robe of the mountain monk.

The great mirror of perfect wisdom is neither form nor name in the Puan hermitage; realizing the source and forgetting emotions, no person is seen. The solitary moon gathers all in its entirety, free from intention.

Consciousness: The moon in the cassia tree shines alone, utterly free from even a speck of dust. Three *kalpas* are but a single thought; boiling water melts snow. Ten thousand practices vanish in an instant; fire consumes ice.
Reaching this point, what need is there to inquire about sound and form? Together with you, it has been inherently a perfect and luminous mirror.
If one treats a bronze vessel as the true nature, its dark back and blue face will only deceive the student. The original nature is like space, containing all things; wondrously bright and tranquil.
How could illumination tolerate dust? Mountains, rivers, and stone walls are the mist of three springs; emptiness and form are fully manifest as the ice of six months.
Wisdom is naturally perfect and luminous, not belonging to a self; it is not constrained by the sun and moon, yet its radiance is constant.
In discussing the great matter with my attendant Zhong Yuanheng, I was diligent and pure; here, the great affair is a high-sounding song of the snow-flakes, riding upon the white ox.
"Chang-chang-lo fills the air! On this side they are pounding rice; over there they are threshing grain. Tell me, by whose power does this occur? It is the Great Wife of Heaven.
Lately, the fellow practitioners in the South have been cutting through nails and severing iron to subdue demons themselves.

Carrying water and hauling firewood—there is nothing that is not so. Their supernatural powers and wondrous functions manifest the Mahā. One person exerts their strength, and all the heavens are provided for."
How can one contend with what has been cultivated through countless assemblies? To transplant the roots and uproot the trees is not an evil act;
by turning the conditioned into the unconditioned, all things are in harmony. The pavilions suddenly span the azure heavens; may the merit of every person not pass in vain.

The flavors of the Fragrant Accumulation depend upon those who know; you must teach that they are neither few nor many. Within this, there is no need for further entrustment—it is clearly and simply thus.
This Mida (Puan) was told by a fellow practitioner that Chen Tuan practiced "beating sleep. The Master warned him, saying:
"At midday there is a core essence; do not be like this fellow who beats a drowsy sleep. His vital spirit is stagnant and his conscious intellect is led astray."
Falling into the three miserable realms makes escape difficult; here with me it is not so. If the eyes do not sleep, all dreams are dispelled;
sitting upright and still, one is free from entanglements. Moving freely in all directions, there is no binding attachment. Let those who study the Way give rise to a sense of shame and remorse.

The eyes of the Universal Hut have not closed for ten thousand kalpas; its nostrils reach to the heavens as it calls out, "Elder Brother! It embraces the minute within the vast flow, transmitting the Great Meaning.
I urge you to cultivate the resolve for renunciation and withdrawal. Seizing the heavens and earth in a single sitting, there is no other principle:
this backbone is forged of pure steel, supporting heaven and earth without a second. This radiance is the entire body, filling the mountains and rivers with majesty and abundance.
Precious! The bright moon shines resplendently across the azure sky. When the responsive clarity that transcends all conditions lets go, one matter is resolved and the mind ceases;

there is nothing more to do. A single phrase from the Patriarchal Gate encompasses all under heaven. Free from marks yet not empty, there is nothing else: the music of no sound resounds with a chirping cry.
Buying rice at the residence of Li Guangyuan—how laughable!
Old Nanquan, that ancient sage, lived in the conditions of mountain dwelling with nothing to rely upon. He was able to have a wooden man come to buy rice;
he already knew this before the light of wind and moon appeared. How extraordinary! The eyes of willows and the cheeks of peach blossoms are all mechanisms. Not a single blade of grass...
Born tens of thousands of li away, the spring colors linger together as one leaves the gate. How deluded! Not sparing even three thousand *li* to exchange for a dragon pearl.
If you ask where Puan’s intention lies, his radiance pervades everywhere, his essence is suchness.
Together with the elder layman Tang Heng, we cook the five flavors in the Hall of Fragrant Accumulation. Feet tread upon heaven and heads touch the earth;

though horns and heads may each spread apart, not everyone has yet attained complete mastery. Otherwise, Elder Heng possesses great compassion; one day he will harmonize all things without partiality.
The assembly deliberated: "The Dharma friends of the South are not one-sided; within their ranks, everyone is fully equipped.
They have truly blocked the mouth and the throat, so that whatever message leaves the gates is nothing but the truth."

Together with Li Guangyuan, we transform grain into emptiness and take that emptiness as reality; we resolve that the objective realm is none other than the mind. Only then can one receive the deluded masses within this very place and truly manifest the function of the Tathāgata.
In ancient temples, incense and flowers are abundant and abbots are countless, yet they lack but one thing: the eye. Therefore, the sites fall into ruin.
The days have long passed. Today, at this site of practice (*dōjō*), a blink of the eye reveals the Dharma; the finger points to the lantern.

The wind and banner remain unmoved, yet the mind of the worthy one perceives the tip of a needle and finds the *dharmakāya* fully present. Thus, one attains lofty generosity whose radiance reaches afar, and the spirit of the Confucian sages fills the belly.

Whether speaking or remaining silent, all is thoroughly penetrated; one is willing to believe in the wordless, entering the principle as if space itself. Beholding the mountain hermitage, the winds from the four directions converge; the fish-drum is difficult to strike.

Ming! If you wish to forget a thousand hungers for the sake of one full meal, you must understand the price of the true rice of Luling. Seeking characters and eyes together creates a momentum that will cause them to be scattered;
do not let them meet a person of true substance. A single shoulder-pole of Mount Sumeru moves beneath the eaves. I earnestly hope you will cherish and honor this.
Two Verses on Perfect Penetration by the Junior Disciple:
This faith is so rare and sparse—who can know it? The wind dances through ten thousand branches of the cliff pines. The cuckoo calls out, its voice never ceasing;
Where the partridge cries, green willows hang down. In the midst of the bustling marketplace, the whole body is revealed— Deeply penetrating, he has reached the state of the ancient masters.
Pāṅki. Mindless yet responding to things, things are not things; like a single bead of a magical *maṇi* jewel, the wondrously perfect *sarvajñajñāna* (all-knowing wisdom) universally provides access.
In every atom and every world-system, radiance is manifested. A single expression of skillful means is beyond words and phrases; its extraordinary auspiciousness shall endure for ten thousand years.
Inconceivable!
Yuan Tong further instructed the assembly of novices:
"O sons of the Buddhas, in approaching wise persons there is no distinction between self and other. You must strive with all your might to bring this present life to its conclusion."
Ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes cease from this point on. It is better to undergo all the sufferings of the mountain gate than to fail to hear the Vajra-Marrow of all Buddhas.
When the Vajra-Marrow is raised at every moment, it directly causes the life-blood to flow through to the bottomless depths. Its application is inexhaustible and its intent is perfect;
from this, ten million dharanis emerge. Spread far and wide without a fixed abode, its secret application according to the occasion is nothing other than this.
Calculation: Entering the mud and entering the water without self-interest. The Samādhi of Turning the Non-retrogressive Wheel.
[○@Tong] Entrusting it to all myriad practices, one should maintain it with perfect clarity and diligence as the Buddha-work of one’s own mind.
Verses in Praise of the Three Jewels:
The Perfect Radiance manifests as formless things; The great earth, mountains, and rivers seem as if they do not exist. A single pearl from the black dragon—neither being nor non-being.

Regarding this sign: those who have faith may temporarily use it to create painted diagrams, but to point directly at the human mind and personally see the Buddha—why labor to strike tiles and fashion the lines of the hexagrams? A single sheet of white cloud spans the mouth of the valley;
how many returning birds are utterly lost in their nests?

Delusion and enlightenment are fundamentally the same light; when one has faith, there is nothing hidden. The illusory emptiness is like the substance of a dream; this is the King of Samādhi, the Flower of Awakening.

To praise Bodhidharma’s wondrous accord as "Bodhi at every touch" is merely to observe that the old barbarian returning to the West was simply playing a trick. One should give him— [The text ends abruptly.]
"Thirty strokes of the bamboo whisk. Let me ask those who have traveled among the masters: do you know or not? Your wild scribbling has already forfeited your advantage.
[Sighs] "This too deserves thirty blows of the staff. Is there anyone here who dares to strike? Try to cut through it!"
Praise to Subhūti, who, being utterly devoid of skillful means, first understood emptiness. He rained flowers and shook the earth to unleash his sharp spiritual edge;
seeking a place for quiet meditation, he found none, walking alone amidst the vast and silent universe. Tut!

The lay devotee, a master painter, requests a eulogy for that which is neither delusion nor enlightenment—who could forcibly name it a model? In the samādhi of formlessness, there is no room for paint or plaster. Transcending color and surpassing sound, there is not a single thing;
with the voice unceasing, one recites "Sulu. Where the tip of the eyebrow quivers, a thousand lights are contained. If you are willing to let go yourself—remove it!

Not a man of great capacity; though he maintains his mind, he does not lose it, yet when planning affairs, he forgets the Truth. Who recognizes the precious jewel of primordial clarity? In vain, how many springs have passed!
Because I met the Old Man Puan, he showed me that the essence of all things is pure. Simply rely on the nature of non-attachment;
within the delusion of this nature, one hesitates for a moment. *Ei!*

Universally, heaven and earth are not external objects; everywhere one hears the Dharma-realm as a perfect sound. Sentient beings enter the pores of my body; being neither form nor name, where can they be sought?
At Mount Potalaka, everything meets the eye, yet no one sees it; its wondrous substance is dignified and majestic, indestructible gold.
Like a bell containing resonance that responds according to conditions, upon seeing me, you should know this is your own mind. Śākyamuni Buddha, universally...

An-guang: The non-dual body of the Tathāgata is not hidden; who would know it exists apart from offerings of incense and flowers? It resides solely within the hall of the mind-seal of sentient beings.
This Dharmakāya is subject to neither change nor decay; within its nostrils, it contains the three realms. Like the moon in water or flowers in the sky, it cannot be pinpointed.
Always sovereign within the light of non-characteristics. [O @ Yi].
Taking the emptiness of phenomena as a seat and the vajra as one’s essence, one is like a board—free from delusion, empty, and bottomless. With non-dual faith, one swallows the mountains.
Heaven, O Heaven! Awakening to the Dharma of Non-arising, he speaks without preaching Chan. Opening his two flaps of skin, he encompasses the earth and embraces the heavens.
"What is the Buddha?"—one hundred and eight thousand [miles].
The myriad colors of the world are easily exhausted, yet why does the crown-mark (uṣṇīṣa) of Pupan remain? It is of one essence with the vast empty sky;
mist, dew, clouds, and rosy mists serve as his outer robe. The eyes behold it not, and the ears hear it not; yet he is ever-vigilant and never obscured—how could such clarity be diminished?
Having understood the picking up of the flower, one knows its source; with a cold laugh, Bodhidharma returned to the West. Using obscurity to conceal and reveal requires no toil or loss;
from antiquity to the present, how truly marvelous!
A Dharma Talk for the Assembly:

When the ore is removed and the gold remains, it survives a hundred refinements. Since I first set my price, no one has been able to match it. Shining upon the present and illuminating the past, it is neither sound nor form.
Once, I worked as a bullock for Moshan. My body is like drifting clouds; my mind is like the wind—dwelling in a state of constant instability.
In the void, the wind suddenly sweeps away the clouds until no trace remains. Who can recognize the true Master? The great hermit dwells in the marketplace; the small hermit dwells in the mountains.
When the mind is realized as being without affairs, there are no longer many complications. Cease from conditions and reach this state where dust and grime are worn away;
severing attachment, one must ultimately endure the cold of the years. Upon the hundred blades of grass, inquire of the Many-Jeweled Buddha; by the cauldron, examine Zhaozhou.
The state gates: let not one strike connect heaven and earth. In an instant, the axis of the earth is shaken;
shown to Yang Zhongzhi, who recognizes it as a single mote of dust? Within this is hidden the original Buddha, who constantly emits light from time to time, illuminating all things.
It is permitted only for those with faith; at all times, never be negligent. If this time does not meet the requirement, one shall not depart from the adamantine bone.
Encountering the hammer and tongs of one's own fundamental portion, one is forged into something that is not an external object. [○@、]
Huagong read the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The Master showed him a verse:
"The Daoist reads the scripture but does not recognize the characters; in a single instant he must turn a thousand billion copies. The Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges enter into atoms;
reaching the source, the sūtra is free from fabrication."
He Shuyi requests a verse on the Ten Powers:
Whose practice has reached such sublime heights? He Shuyi again knocks at the gate of Puan. Within the profound mystery, the myriad wonders possess spiritual awareness;

one must personally accept that mind alone hears what cannot be heard. At this time, faith penetrates the Vajra and realizes the Buddha-wisdom; when emotions are forgotten and thoughts exhausted, one is in accord with reality.
Heaven and Earth: The news of the night moon and morning breeze is everywhere; in the realm of the Unseen and the Inaudible, the Way alone remains.
The *Pòwù Sòng* (Verse on the Tattered Hut).
Addressing the assembly: "A single idle person wears a tattered hut; when the wind blows and the rain drips, it turns ever more radiant. The lanterns and the pillars are present at every moment."
Case: It is simply said that one repays injustice with equanimity. On the Lapis Lazuli Palace, a golden horse is whipped; though it could chase the wind, it cannot catch up to a three-legged donkey.
*Duḥ!* This would kill a person with its intensity. (After a long silence, he says: "I let this move pass. Do you understand?
A mound of earth rises from level ground. Many people will not grant you their approval. [Circle with a dot inside] *Ei!* What is this?
The patched robe shown to the assembly:
a single idle body encompasses the myriad existences. Unable to hold the needle and thread oneself, the patchwork must be fine when gathered from various conditions.
Its wondrous form is solemn and majestic—a great penetration. Every stitch of the needle-point is without exception real; every strip of cloth is threaded through.
Emptiness within emptiness: mountains and waters spread across heaven and earth. When all is unified in perfect completion, one first escapes the cage.
Yet there is another extraordinary marvel: the withered tree before the cliff laughs at the spring breeze.
The monk in plain clothes shows the assembly:
this one robe of mine surpasses Zhaozhou’s seven-pound scale; even the Four Heavenly Kings cannot lift it.
You all may try to take hold of it, but you must simply seek to achieve it directly; no coarseness is permitted. It must be so.
As for the place of entry and exit, no one can see it; this is precisely what constitutes "fine hands and feet.
I wonder, how would you express the final phrase? *Ei!* A swift strike!
I show my disciples that I have a dharma-name called "Liberation. Wherever I am, I stir up the dust; let me not stir up a single ordinary person.
What is the use of shaving one's head and spreading out one's alms bowl? Heh! Layman Pang, together with his wife and children, has attained Buddhahood all at once.
All is included: if the deluded mind is not extinguished, calamities will not cease. Leave all petitions and divinations to the great void. To realize the Way, there is no need for many words;
within the very presence of the gate, there is naturally a bright pearl. At midnight, do not waste oil; when will the pursuit of the moon in the clear pool ever end?
In winter, do not entangle yourself with guests of the red dust; let the household remain at peace and the body naturally complete.
I address my disciples and followers: once you have attained peace and happiness of mind, what else need you seek?
Until the afflictions of the mundane world have ceased, you must rely upon a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*). If you are willing to learn with compassion, make a vow and exert your mental strength.
Enter the mud and enter the water; do not engage in idle play. In the movement of eyebrows and the flickering of eyes, the Dharmakāya is infinite and boundless.
Those who practice indolence therein will surely find themselves without food to eat. Chasing after the crowd merely fills the mouth; wearing fur will never come to an end.
If you do not believe in the sutras of the Buddha Vehicle, you pursue the branches while losing the root. Alas, O Great Man! By whose power do you ride?
When the root is fundamentally devoid of self or person, what benefit is there in greedy haste? Why not rest from ignorance and listen to the blowing of the holeless flute?
The five notes and six pitch-pipes are complete; the bright moon and mournful wind are still. A single sound fills the vast universe; those who hear it within find it real.
In harmony, they become the body of wisdom, with nothing capable of obstructing them. I urge you, shadows of grass and trees: gather yourselves up while there is yet time.

That the Imperial Uncle Xia ascended to the heavens on a bright day was no mere coincidence; becoming a Buddha in a single instant is likewise so. Within this state, one utterly transcends sound and form;

the light of grace fills the eyes, and the mind reaches unto heaven. One should clearly realize this vast penetration, which is beyond conceptual thought. Having once received the Imperial Edict, it pervades everywhere.

Samantabhadra, the wind and moonlight of Jiangxi are inexhaustible; in the imperial capital, True Suchness (Tathatā) is perfected in all phenomena. Drinking and swallowing right where one is, there is never insufficiency;
one protects and maintains the secret without ceasing for years on end.
The Dharma has been entrusted to ministers since ancient times;
today it has met one of great resolve. Transcending birth and death through the transparent realization of *huazhu*, you discern all things without partiality to aid the imperial court.
(After a long silence, he says: Do you understand? Bodhidharma was not for posterity; it was Śākyamuni.
This was not yet the ultimate. In immeasurable kalpas to come, the indolent elder shall attain spontaneity.

Together with Liao Weigao, he mastered the three teachings and surpassed the Zen mechanisms; in speech and silence, they shared the same wind, yet those who harmonized with them were rare. A world-renowned lay practitioner (*upāsaka*) whose fame pervaded the earth and encompassed the heavens.
The eye has always been but a hair’s breadth away. (He also said: But tell me, what connection is there with that hair’s breadth?
I say it is not something external.
When Zishan Huoguang first visited the Master, he requested a verse;

his heart was in accord with the truth as he stepped forward to knock at Nanquan’s gate. Clouds adorn the vast, empty crags, and the chamber is silent and profound; the pure breeze within this single room is the intention of a thousand ages.
Were it not for transcending sound and form, how could one inquire into the profound mystery?

The practitioner is shown a place at the absolute summit where no one dwells; there, the integration [of all things] is not difficult. Walking alone, one relies on non-abiding; how could the perfect mind come or go?
Its profound depth lies in being beyond words and speech. Do not let idle fingers move the wind-blown banner. To thoroughly penetrate this great matter, one must press forward to the very end.
Walking along, white clouds stretch for a thousand li to the pass of my native home.
When the Master saw his disciple, he composed a verse and inscribed it upon the window, then continued the rhyme to admonish him:
"Your many words are like knives that do not pierce; a single word at the window is even more tattered. My own house has its own shared tradition."
Though he comes from a thousand miles away, he is nonetheless accepted. (He says to himself: "My whole body is eyes; I see a single point. My whole body is a mouth;
I can speak only half. If you wish to understand Nanquan’s intimate meaning, nothing surpasses boring a hole through the crown of his head.
The stone man beats the drum and the wooden man blows [the horn]; the incense pillar hears it personally, its head shrouded in a veil.
Such a perfect sound has no place for utility; Lord Yan is not yet willing to let him off. (He says to himself: "Heaven! Heaven! The deficiencies are no small matter.

When the time comes and the season arrives, one understands it for oneself clearly. Do not harbor deluded thoughts at all. No night travel is permitted; you must arrive by the break of dawn. It does not hinder.
Try to speak of it. Do you still know it? I will not say it, I will not say it. Even in death I will not say it.
Whose are these nostrils that pierce the heavens? He takes clouds and mist as his robe.
Delusion and awakening are fundamentally non-existent; there is only the One Nature. You are entirely me, and I am not "it. (He says to himself: Is there any fault in being thus? I give it to you.
Thirty blows of the staff. (Sighs) Puan’s three verses naturally follow the picking up; they are sent with the original tongs for handling the net.
When the furnace and bellows are steady, there is no dull iron; why not add even more sharpness to the arrowhead? (He picks it up and says: A scene of drowsy chatter—old and decrepit.
How fitting that one feels such shame!
The Master inscribed these four characters on his study window to seal the true reality (dharmatā) with the seal of cessation (śamatha).
Having attained the correct [state], there is nothing that is not the departure from the one-pointed tranquility. The seal of emptiness is perfect and complete, its jewel-like radiance overflowing;
how could celestial māras or heterodox paths exist? Its essence is like empty space—how could the world ever interfere?
[Contemplation]. A fine vehicle with two mouths and grass marking its head; together we see and observe the water buffalo. Last night the herder had no blanket to cover him;
this morning he still laughs, saying there is nothing to seek.

[○@Dhyāna]: In reality, the principle of detachment and penetration cannot coexist. When one person directly realizes their identity with that [source], those who sit stubbornly for a long time give rise to perverse thoughts;
they instead slander the Tathāgata’s true awakening as empty.
[○@惠]. At the crossroads at the edge of the fields, majestic and vast; clenching the mouth and gathering the mind, one immediately encounters the truth.
Having attained the true jewel-treasury of the *maṇi*, he returns to awaken dreams and manifest the essential framework.
The Old Man Pupan brings forth this samatha-vipaśyanā and samādhi-prajñā from within a single mote of dust.
If a person can understand this, what connection is there between it and these words spoken in sleep? I grant him one eye.
If a person does not understand, I likewise grant him one eye. Hūṃ hūṃ! For now, look at that one-legged bridge by the side of the road. Go well, go well! Alas, heaven! Alas!
Heaven. Furthermore, a verse says:
"The single wheel of the heart-moon illuminates the dark thoroughfare; who knows when dreams and illusions shall swallow it whole? Fortunately meeting one of like mind, I shall explain it once more."
Lifting up the mind, turn the thought back toward the radiance of the fundamental principle. A single phrase, when it meets the day, is the rare and true faith.

If you wish to speak, words fail; if you seek to strike the pivot, you will grow weary. Since High Peak is far away, cease your searching. Without sparing my own eyebrows, I shall reveal this for you:

the single body is pure and originally without flaw; with clear understanding, returning home is superior to leaving the household life. The red leaves dance in the wind—awaken to this early! Do not take that which exists...
Restrict yourself to chasing away empty vanity; with a single mind, perfectly maintain the manifold states of mind. Let the mind of faith sever all pursuit of external objects;
within this state there is no division, so it is difficult to reach. It is best to turn the light back within to avoid sinking into the abyss.

The verse says: Cutting off the tip of the vase-heart, dharmas are neither severed nor extinguished. Kicking over a single pure vase, the flowering grove can do nothing about it. Not freed from sound, form, and name, true suchness is but play.
Mind and objects are equal and level; they do not fall into the utility of existence or non-existence. Samādhi is fundamentally empty and clear.
Tsk! A Verse for the Double Ninth:
Last year, on the Double Ninth, the elegant host received the guest; amidst the yellow chrysanthemums they discussed Prajñā, and in pure Dharma they delighted in the true nature.
Tonight there shall be a noble gathering; the High Peak vanishes amidst the four neighboring villages. With a solitary staff, I pick out the sun and moon—what path has no ford?
Baizhang first commanded the Senior Seat Qing to prostrate and seek a verse from the Venerable Qing of Xichuan:
"From the beginning, there are no brothers; one must know that self-nature is like the essence of space. It is like the moon in water—"
In the midst, one has not yet understood the truth. This matter is not transmitted through sounds, colors, or phrases; originally, the mind-dharma alone is numinous and bright.

A verse for sending rice to Baizhang: Baizhang’s solitary clouds enter the Dao-forest; True Suchness is unmoving, its intent difficult to seek. When practitioners meet, it is not coming from anywhere.
The past, speech, and silence are fully manifest throughout all time. Recently, in Luling, he personally attained the price; at once, he bestowed the grandmotherly heart.
Baizhang’s response in verse:

Pupan’s dignified bearing stands out from the dense forest; traversing a thousand li through parting clouds, I have sought him out with purpose. Upon seeing him once, his sharp wit was like clouds casting shadows;

upon further probing his profound eloquence, there has been none such in antiquity nor today. He further bestows upon me grains of jade-like rice—this is precisely the iron-and-stone heart of the man himself.
The practitioner who clearly understands the verses on seeking finds resonance in every instance;
rare indeed is one who can meet this. In every object, the true essence is no different. If you simply prepare a heart of resolve, you will never be deceived;

when emotions are forgotten and thoughts exhausted, one enters the state of non-remainder (*anupadhiśeṣa*). It is only because those who have left the home-life lack eyes that they say ascetic practice falls into [emptiness].
Empty and void. While Gan-zhi was still in the secular world, he already mastered the principles; he wondrously understood that by seeking nothing, one naturally attains the pearl.
When Shao-chun the practitioner requested a verse, [the Master said]:
"Even if it were eight thousand five hundred years, the cypress and cranes of Shao-chun would not be considered extraordinary. It is not as good as the radiance of Shao-ming."

Transformation. At this time, one should truly leave the household life. Contemplating the Way, what worry need one have for matters of food and clothing? Amidst a thousand shifting shadows, one listens to the warbling of the oriole;
hearing it sing a single note, the entire message is conveyed. Everywhere the eyes meet lotus flowers, yet not a single branch is seen.
Chen Daxian offers chrysanthemums. I seek a verse:
The splendor covering the earth is not yet marvelous; Before the frost and after autumn, golden branches burst forth. Only Kāśyapa personally received this upon Mount Ling;
Today Chen brings it forth for all to know. Not merely for seasonal use by the likes of Tao Yuanming, It is now transformed into an offering to the Flower Treasury (Huazang).
A-mi. Upon hearing and seeing, one surely returns to the other shore; only then does one know that this is the time for offering flowers.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, these thirty-two verses [are recited] at the morning gruel.
With the universal eye, there is no restriction on whether the eyes are open or closed; why must the light of the mind wait for the break of day? Before the multitude...
The arising of self-conceit spreads everywhere; practicing for the benefit of others, my own belly swells.

At the hour of noon, I eat from a bowl of turbid water where grains have been rinsed of sand. Without oil, salt, soy sauce, vinegar, or tea, I partake of a small amount whenever hunger or thirst strikes.
I only wonder: why did he awaken to the peach blossoms?
Whether walking or staying, severing attachment and bidding farewell to kin—one practices in this manner. How could this be for the sake of seeking food, clothing, or the status of a monk?
At every step, pure radiance shines forth without other thoughts; standing tall and solitary, wondrous clarity arises.

Sitting Meditation: The night is still and the wind mourns; all people are silent. All worldly affairs concluded, all is vast and tranquil. Sitting cross-legged in the *paryaṅka* posture, one enters the samādhi of the Milky Way.
Who would have known that lying beneath the moon, dawn would suddenly arrive?
Habitually listening [to the Dharma], I see how birth, old age, sickness, and death torment one with suffering; only I know how to swiftly cast them aside.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, I constantly mindfully recollect the Buddha; upon hearing the Master utter a single phrase, my ears reach the boundless.
Uphold this: hearing the Way of true emptiness, do not cling to words; with pure faith, remain steadfast and reverent. Simply let this luminous nature pervade all;
whether speaking or remaining silent, acting or concealing, how could you ever depart from Chan?
Having finished bathing, one realizes the body is like an illusion—whom would one speak to? Carrying water and hauling firewood, the conditions for transformation are met.
Suddenly encountering someone at the bathhouse pointing toward the water, its light, pure, and wondrous touch becomes even more radiant.
Facing the fire—clouds freeze, winds intensify, and birds leave no trace. Dongshan said nothing more than that there is no "west" or "east.
In the midst of this, who can truly entrust themselves to this direct encounter? Fortunately, we met Danxia, whose charcoal glows red.
The Rice Cooker: Making up for one's shortcomings through diligence, he enters the kitchen; regardless of whether it be green mud or other matters, everything is provided.
Shide and Hanshan clarified this meaning: now they have attained Buddhahood, filling all of space.

Offering incense and lamps for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges: if one’s merit remains incomplete, the eye shall not open. One must know for oneself that the numinous light is inherently present;
let the incense and lamps never cease to awaken the deluded and the dull-witted.
The Guest Attendant does not neglect sweeping the floor or brewing tea; he opens and closes the gate according to the Lotus Sūtra.
Cloud tracks and rain footprints come and go without ceasing—who among them would be willing to return home quickly?
Sweeping the ground, the mind-ground is luminous and the Pure Land is perfected. When all people see me, I remain silent;
I merely take up the broom and sweep here and there, shaking the three thousandfold world-systems and the great chiliocosm.
Attending the Master: Though my faith has not yet been perfected through a thousand villages and ten thousand hamlets, I have come here to burn but a single fathom of incense smoke.
Now, morning and evening, I hear and see him; though I were to grind my bones and shatter my body, my repayment would still not be complete.
Tea and Soup: Before host and guest have exchanged a word, tea and soup are already served at the edge of their lips.
Discerning the principle and listening to the sound, these are not external things; they bind others in joy for ten thousand years.
The head-shaver maintains purity; he keeps the scalding water for cleansing close to the pit. With the samādhi of compassionate harmony, he benefits the blind masses.
All Buddhas of the ten directions act in this way; how could he emulate those born through the karmic retribution of wearing fur?
Bathing the Head: Sentient beings have heavy defilements and are mired in worldly conditions; how can they gather their own minds and turn toward the source of awakening?
The time has come to draw water and gather firewood; when the three beats of the drum cease, all things are fresh.
Fuel for the hearth: a thousand-year-old withered tree, ancient and sprawling. Ghosts fear it, gods doubt it; it is a lamp for the yakṣas.
Were it not for a man of the Way, who would dare to move it? Such as this surely cannot be an ordinary sentient being.
The charcoal head has vanished; fire has emerged from the wood, and embers, ash, and smoke have been extinguished. Black and white are without even a trace that could serve as a teacher.
This is like the spring breeze melting the winter snow, universally causing both cold and warmth to cease their partiality and decay.
At the head of the assembly, how many times has it been unfurled and rolled up to aid the deluded masses? Mazu ascended the hall and Baizhang understood;
from that time on, a single thread was passed through. Now, in gathering and releasing, do not let it be delayed.

Carrying timber, leading the way, he travels through ten thousand mountains; He deeply understands the difficulty of the first step. When the work is fully accomplished, lotus palaces appear before one's eyes;
The wind-bells ring with clarity, and the mind is naturally at ease.
Stemmed bamboo with green joints amidst idle clouds, an ancient air; where the thickets are lush, east and west are lost.
No one asks for news of Prince Zhiyou; the phoenixes fly forth, their footprints filling the void.
Carrying bricks and mortar, mixing mud and water with great toil—had it not been for meeting a wise teacher, this task would not have been accomplished.
Now, already stretching across the heavens and covering the earth, through favorable conditions and the absence of outflows, one will surely pass through the ford.
The bricks are dry; the secret traces are all-encompassing yet reveal no dust. The eight classes of devas and nāgas rejoice and yet are startled.
Amidst the blazing fires of the kalpa, there is no decay or change. Within this, one recites the Universal Gate Sūtra.
The dry stone has accumulated dust and sand through kalpas, forming caverns and crags. The Buddhas of the ten directions all participate therein together;
when the Many Treasures Buddha hears the sutra, he personally surges forth from it. Therefore, it is not merely cypress, catalpa, pine, or fir.
Compounding the Medicine: Bian Que and Lu Yi quickly retreat to the borders. Everyone shall eat their fill of Puan’s pills.
They resolve grudges, untie knots, and eliminate all ailments; their responsive efficacy is boundless and requires no money.
The Stupa-Head: Now, seamless and of ancient ridges, it penetrates stone and pierces clouds, delivering all living beings.
Universally embracing all conditions without attachment, its form is like a single room containing a hundred thousand lamps.
A main street with golden ground is not for the sake of wealth; a white jade crossroad invites bandits. When the ground of the mind is level and firm, no dust can enter;
even ten billion asuras cannot touch it with their hands.

Building the Bridge: A direct, rootless tree is laid out. To transcend both the mundane and the sacred, one must have a great mind that is bold. Only by forgetting one’s own body for the sake of the Dharma can it be so;
carrying a wooden board, such a person is truly a great man.
Filling the roads, thunder roars and lightning shrieks warn the ignorant and deluded. When the rain ceases and the wind clears, it is as if emerging from emptiness.
The Buddha teaches sentient beings the Great Way; supporting their families and serving the state, they continue the ancestral tradition.
Garden Master: An ancient adept from a thousand or ten thousand years past, who cleared the mountains and tilled the fields to demonstrate his instructions.
When he picked up the snake, no one understood; he tossed it straight across—do not doubt it further.
The Grain Head: Lingyuan’s chariot tracks reveal the source. When a single grain pierces through, gather it with swift alacrity.
Do not wait for the high price demanded by Linling; when the moment arrives, the mouth opens to speak, yet it is difficult to repay.
Treasury Office: You should collect this priceless mani jewel; vow never again to seek gold, jade, or fleeting wealth.
From now on, you shall enter among those with horns and hair, becoming donkeys and oxen for hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas.

The above consists of thirty-two verses. Through the Dharmakāya, Sambhogakāya, and Nirmāṇakāya, they universally support all practices. By serving the Buddha with diligence and sincerity, one seeks the Supreme Vehicle;
thus, the cause becomes the true cause, and the fruit will surely be the true fruit. For eternal kalpas, one shall not fall from this school.

Universally responding throughout the past, present, and future—thus was it written and shown by the Elder Puzhan. At that time, a hundred flowers and ten thousand willows were stirred by fluttering butterflies.
Yingge: "We shall together verify this matter, leaving nothing out and without residue. We shall directly reach the Buddha Hall at the three gates, where all phenomena grant their assent.
Even the incense pillar and the lantern bow their heads in prostration. As for the final word—how do you speak it? [A circle with a dot inside]. "Be careful."

Building a stupa to show the assembly—to seek outside is not as good as seeking within oneself. When one is willing within oneself, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished. Now, this precious stupa is about to be completed;

may all people give rise to the single-minded resolve. How frustrating it is to kill oneself with anxiety! It was through this that I awakened to the Way. On the assembly at Vulture Peak, there was none...
Whether man or woman, great or small, all pull the stones; high and low alike turn the Puan Sutra. The mountains, forests, cliffs, and valleys all smile;
this is the supreme cause of the Tathāgata. If there are those who are foolish and stubborn and refuse to turn it, let them find their rest in the pigsty or the sheepfold.
This old monk has eyes upon the tip of his staff; he does not strike those with fur and horns. Thus it is said.
Cutting through nails and severing iron: one person settles all matters, and the myriad conditions become new.
A letter to Layman Hui Peng.

I, [Name], respectfully address you. Regarding what you seek (as your "seat-counsel"): though your eyes have never been away from me, your inquiries into the distinctions of the ancestral source are as far apart as the wind and the oxen.

Whether slow or fast, if one does not cease, both remain stuck in study. Within this very point, one must personally consent to rest. This humble one is a strange form of earth and wood; the grace received has been no small matter.
Without artifice, I respond to things, always striving with sincere diligence. Having tasted the flavor of your letter, I have reflected deeply:

Your noble nature takes the Dharma as its self, perfectly identical to the Great Void. Such realization is rarely found among others. Delusion arises from the causes and marks of confusion, which belong to the consciousness-spirit (*vijñāna*). This is false...
Recognizing that the transformations of birth and death are the illusory root, one attains the wondrous wisdom of oneness. One does not take forms or sounds as obstructions;
this is what it means to have realized and penetrated. Unconfused by the illusory affairs of the world, such a person is provisionally called a "transcendent practitioner.
One must directly realize that a single nature is perfectly pervasive throughout all natures, and a single dharma universally contains all dharmas. Not...
Moving through the *dharmadhātu*, one’s own *dharmakāya* pervades the ten directions throughout the inexhaustible void, leaving not even a space the size of a needle’s point vacant.
Only then does one accord with the Original Buddha; the initial awakening sought in the present shares the same source as that [Original Buddha].

Thus, one understands that the two gates of emptiness have never been attached to, and that the essence of the Tathāgata of single nature is inherently identical. One should then, during the twelve periods of the day, practice while walking, standing, sitting, and...
Whether lying down, or a single phrase or a single word, all return to the gate of the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
Speech, silence, singing, and chanting are all the functioning of non-nature. This is as Master Ma and Master Damei said: "Simply recognize your own mind;
there is no dharma that is not complete therein. But how, then, is this mind to be recognized? An ancient said: "It cannot be known by wisdom; it cannot be..."
"Recognize, recognize. *Ei!* If you can fix a single eye here, you may truly be said to "recognize the mindless and penetrate the mind-possessing;
once the mind is recognized, the three realms naturally subside. How pitiable are those who, deludedly longing for a state of no-mind, claim that the realm of no-mind cannot be invaded by the mind!
Therefore, the Sūtra says: "When the Bodhi-mind arises, the arising-and-ceasing mind ceases. If one attains the arising of the Bodhi-mind, then...

All these are the daily affairs of your own house. To say they exist is acceptable; to say they do not exist is also acceptable. You will not be deceived by others. Existence and non-existence both fail to reach it;
how could arising and ceasing possibly interfere? One who has attained responds according to conditions; those who have not yet reached it must not remain muddled.
Verbal proliferation leads one further away from the Way. Now tell me: is it "attaining the rank with a mind," or is it "attaining the rank with an empty mind"? What is the meaning of this?

As for "sameness and difference," it is not so. One merely attains the functioning of the mindless; what more need be said of what is reached or not reached? Everything encountered corresponds to the truth;
there is nothing that is not so. You should seek the ultimate ground. Suddenly, upon seeing through it, it will instantly shatter like ice melting.
How profoundly refreshing! Today’s letter contains not a single word. Having twice received your gracious visit, I realize that the principle is not dependent on the jade whisk. May you be blessed.

I have received [your letter] in my ears. You, Guangban, should seek it out. I have sent the *Xuexiu Yuan* Record (along with) the *Fengshui Chan*. It was sent late, but there has been no interval in our correspondence.
Though we are a thousand miles apart, we share the same breeze. May you and yours be most treasured for ten thousand billion kalpas.

Answer: Peng Zishen, you have realized the substance within the universe; forgetting artifice, you preserve your own radiance. The words of Laozi and Zhuangzi do not reach it; the phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs cannot conceal it.
A withered tree is not the attainment of the Way, and a heart of extinguished ash is not free from busyness. Zishen, you lack nothing; that which is fundamentally present need not be forgotten.
I, with these humble words, seek to express my succession to the solemn tradition. I earnestly hope that you, O virtuous one, will not dismiss this as mere poetic composition.

This mountain monk, [Name], deeply regrets his own innate stubbornness and folly, lacking the seed of wisdom. Having mistakenly taken up residence in this region, I don the robes upon my moon-crowned head to manifest the work of the Tathāgata.
Fortunately, amidst the howling winds, the needle and the magnet have met; suddenly awakening from the toil of this worldly life, I realize it is all but an illusion.
Dream: In every thought-moment, one enters the realm of the *Avataṃsaka*; at every step, one ascends the gate of *dharmatā*.
Gathering the objective world back into the mind, there is nothing else; the mind itself is the object. When stillness and illumination transcend cognition, the great function manifests before one.

Responding to conditions and engaging with things according to their capacity, there is nothing extraordinary—only taking responsibility for oneself. Now, having investigated the profound depth of what has been done, I see that Master Heiguang’s poetry is truly transcendent.
Nature. To awaken to those worldly afflictions is to possess a gradual realization of radiant brilliance, as if within true emptiness, wherein all wondrous essences reside.
If this mindfulness is applied with diligent speech, then in departing from objects and encountering events, one attains the perfect penetration of the single essence.

All things are gathered together and realized as illusory. This is what is meant by "penetrating the One, and all matters are completed. Departing and abiding become spontaneous; the wheel of birth and death [is transcended].
[The text] turns. Chan Master Yanshou said: "This principle must not be forgotten for even a single moment; otherwise, one will suddenly fall into contradiction. Dharma Master Zhao said:
"The perfected person is empty and formless, yet there is nothing that is not the self. One who unites all things to constitute the self..."
It must be the Sage! Master Shitou attained enlightenment upon seeing him once, and then said: "The Sage has no self, yet there is nothing that is not his self.
Thus, he offered these words in harmony with the teaching: "That which is fundamentally present need not be forgotten. This is not unlike what the Old Master [Laozi] said:
"When the superior man hears the Way, he practices it diligently; when the mediocre man hears the Way, he may preserve it or lose it; as for the inferior man..."
Upon hearing this teaching, [the Master] laughed heartily. Therefore, he spoke to me: "The Way is of one flavor and consists of direct speech.
The Way has no form; those who look cannot see it. The Way has no direction; those who walk cannot reach it. It resides simply within one's own nature.
How could it be fully explained by a mere few tens of thousands of words? These are the words shown at Guifeng Caotang by the young monk Liaoben.

After this, one should constantly savor this; it is not only this alone.
