Placing head upon head—how well he saved Nanquan!

When the moment arrives, failing to bring forth the full teaching shows one lacks a true master. The monks in the hall lie in vain amidst the mist and clouds. Zhaozhou’s single stoppage leaves nothing more nor less;
ten thousand ages of enduring firmness, yet flowers must still fall.
To cite Chan Master Deng Yinfeng: One day, while he was pushing a cart, Mazu Daoshi was sitting on the road with his legs outstretched.
The Master said, "I ask the Teacher to withdraw your feet. Mazu replied, "Once extended, they are not withdrawn.

The Master said, "Once advanced, there is no retreating," and he pushed the cart over him, crushing Mazu's leg. Upon returning to the Dharma Hall, Mazu took up an axe and said, "Just now, that fellow crushed old..."
"Monk-jiao-di, come out! The Master then stepped forth and extended his neck before the Great Master. The Great Master then set down his axe. [The commentator] remarks:
"Master Ma let go; Deng Yinfeng took up. Pushing the cart and crushing the feet—what a refined elegance between father and son!
As for these coarse-behaved Chan practitioners, what cause for concern is there?

In the light of formlessness, such people are rarely encountered; I fear that those who have not yet penetrated the essence remain mired in lingering doubts. To push aside these obstructions with directness—what hindrance could there be?
Grind out the numinous clarity, and it will shine ever anew like the sun.
To cite Chan Master Nanquan Puyuan: Grand Master Lu Xun asked him, “In my home, I have a large stone slab upon which I sometimes sit and sometimes lie.
Now, I intend to carve it into a Buddha; would this be permissible? The Master said, “It is permissible. The Grand Master said, “Is it not also impermissible?
The Master said, “It is impermissible, it is impermissible. Yunyan remarked, “When sitting, one is the Buddha; when not sitting, one is not.”
"Then he is not the Buddha. Dongshan said, "If one does not sit, one is the Buddha;
if one sits, one is not the Buddha. [The commentator] remarks: "Official Lu Xian was fortunately at ease at home, yet he further set up a slab of stone.
He could neither sit nor lie upon it, yet he was not the Buddha either. Nanquan followed up with two lines that the Official could not utter. Official Lu Xian.
In the blink of an eye, the eyes go blind and the ears are blocked. Yunyan was one whose body was at ease but whose mind was not;
Dongshan was precisely one whose mind was at ease but whose body was not. Do you wish to understand this easily? Return the Buddha to you.

Within this, one must grasp the meaning; yet doubts may arise once more. Fundamentally, there is no need for cultivation or construction; once recognized, it is perfectly manifest and complete. To cite Master Bailin:
one day, while Master Pang was on the road, he encountered the Master. The Master said, "In the past, Layman Pang..."
“Have you ever yet brought forth the ‘sentence of attaining the meaning’ from Nanyue to anyone? The Layman said, “I have brought it forth. The Master asked, “To whom did you bring it forth?
The Layman pointed his finger and said, “Pang Gong. The Master said, “Even Miaode and Śūnyatā-jāti would sigh that they could not equal you, Layman.
The Layman then asked, “Who knows the sentence by which you attained your power? The Master then—
He put on his hat and departed. The layman said, “May you have a safe journey. Once the Master had gone, he did not look back. [The Master] comments:

"People say that all the spirits praise Pánggōng. But when I look at Layman Páng, he has been doused right over the head with a full ladle of foul water by this old monk—no small amount. Yet when the Layman asked him a question, [the Master] was left with nothing to say."
To speak of "responding with reverence":
he enters directly onto the solitary peak; his intent is profoundly deep. Meeting fellow travelers on the Way, few are those who understand. Nothing can compare to Layman Pang;
he clearly understands how to listen to the stringless zither.
To cite Zen Master Nanquan Puyuan. When Grand Councilor Lu Xun said to the Master, "Dharma Master Zhao is truly extraordinary;

he says that all things share the same root and that right and wrong are one body," the Master pointed to the peony flowers in the courtyard and said, "Grand Councilor, when people of this age see this single stalk of flowers, it is like being in a dream. The Grand Councilor was at a loss for words.
The Master [Zhaozhou] held up [the case] and said: "Dafu Lu Xun was repeating the 'sleeping words' of Dharma Master Zhaoming before he had finished them;
yet Nanquan arrived right here and his stratagem failed. Puan added a comment: "A peony flower."

Who created the red, yellow, azure, and green? If you understand this, nothing fails to accord with the innate truth. It is just this single sprout that startles one from a dream, causing one to know that the hundred flowers of the great earth are newly blossomed.
Master Shilin was once visited by Layman Pang. The Master held up his whisk and said, "This does not fall within the scope of Danxia’s device;
try and say a single word. The Layman snatched away the whisk and instead raised his fist. The Master said, "That is precisely Danxia’s device.
The Layman said, "Let us see who does not fall [into that trap]. The Master said, "Danxia suffers from muteness, Old Pang."
The Master suffered from deafness. The layman said, "Exactly so! Exactly so! The Master was speechless. The layman said, "Tell him it was merely a coincidence.
The Master remained speechless once more.
The Master picks up the whisk and says: "Shilin raises his whisk; Pang’s spirit does not fall into the categories of existence or non-existence. Who is wrong? Who is right?
If you do not understand this mind, you are merely opening your eyes to sleep. [O@Sa].
When adepts meet, there is no interaction; they do not fall into Danxia’s trap, yet they naturally deceive themselves. Fortunately, Master Pang possessed no dualistic understanding;
his welcoming and sending off were all of one and the same kind.
Citing Chan Master Nanquan Puyuan, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Old man Wang wants to sell himself; who is willing to buy?
A monk stepped forward and said, "I will buy him. The Master said, "He does not ask for a high price, nor does he accept a low price.
How will you buy him? The monk was speechless. Wulong spoke on his behalf, saying, "He belongs to me. Heshan spoke on his behalf, saying, "It is so."
"What is the principle here? Zhaozhou answered on his behalf: "Come back next year and I will sew a cloth bag for you, Master.
He commented: "For so long, Nanquan has been the master of himself; who would have known that today his house is cold and he has suffered a total defeat?
Fortunately, that monk could not reach a consensus. Had he purchased it, who would have had to carry the burden? Wolong loved this.
"Make it abundant. Heishan relied on his fundamental allotment; Zhaozhou’s hand was too slow. Puan added a comment: "Too noble!
A single idle body is more than enough to use. To those willing to accept it, I offer this presentation: ten thousand taels of gold are not worth it."
The *Biyan lu* (Blue Cliff Record), Case 10: To the east, west, south, and north, everything is perfectly clear.
It cites the story of Master Xiuxi of Tanzhou. One day, Gushan asked him, "When sound and form are pure and true, what is the Way?"
The Master said, "Why do you speak so confusedly? Guishan then moved from the east side to stand on the west side.
The Master said, "If you had not done so, disaster would have ensued. Guishan then moved back to the east side. The Master then descended from his meditation seat;
having taken only two steps, he was seized by Guishan, who asked, "Regarding the matter of sound and form being utterly true—how is it? The Master then struck Guishan with his palm.
Tangshan said, "Ten years from now, there will not even be anyone left to serve tea.
The Master asked, "Why would you want Tangshan, this old fellow? Tangshan laughed heartily three times.
The Master [Zhaozhou] held up the staff and said: "Gushan wanted to sail on the same sea-going vessel as Xiuxi, yet he feared Xiuxi lacked capital.
Xiuxi intended to stay one night at Gushan’s place, yet he feared Gushan had nothing to cover for him.
Having no choice but to exhaust their resources together, they reached this point. Therefore, Gushan laughed three times. Puan said: "Gushan was no good man. This—
In the laughter of men there is a blade; you all must first take care of your left and right.
On a ten-thousand-fathom peak, he steers a bottomless boat; relying on his knowledge, he holds aloft a lamp in the sea.
Lying on ice in the sixth month, he spreads auspicious snow—what is the meaning of these three loud laughs?
To cite Chan Master Nanquan Puyuan: He, along with Magu and Guizong, went together to pay their respects to National Teacher Nanyang.
Before they had even reached the road, the Master drew a circle and said, "If you can speak, then you may go.
Guizong immediately sat down within the circle; Magu performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, "If it is so, then you shall not go. Guizong replied, "Yes."
"What state of mind was he in? The Master called him back; he did not go further to pay respects to the National Teacher.

[The Master] picked up the case and said: "This fellow of immeasurable self-importance—neither truly foolish nor truly ignorant—he has performed every kind of trickery, yet in the end, he could not get out of this National Teacher’s circle. It would have been better to call him back and let him rest."
Departing is good;
the light of the sun, moon, and lamp are utterly beyond comparison. Why need one seek companions to study True Suchness?
The National Teacher’s Way lies in non-appearance; where there is a true knower, it is Mañjuśrī.
Citing Chan Master Guishan Lingyou: While on a communal work assignment picking tea, he said to Yangshan, "All day long we have been picking tea;
I hear only your voice but do not see your form. Why do you not manifest your physical presence so that we may meet? Yangshan shook the tea tree. The Master said:
The Master said, "You have only attained the function; you have not attained the essence. Yangshan asked, "I do not understand how it is with the Master. The Master remained silent for a long time.

Yangshan said, "The Master has attained the essence, but not the function. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows! Xuangjue said: [Note: The provided text contains a fragment of a dialogue concerning the relationship between "essence" (ti) and "function" (yong) in Chan practice.]
Now tell me: where does the fault lie? [The Master] held up his staff and said:
"To give a son a thousand pieces of gold is not as good as teaching him a single craft. Thus we know that if one wishes to travel every road under heaven, nothing surpasses mastery in a single craft.
At this time, the father and son of Mount Mui—body and function reflected together, compassion and wisdom operating in tandem—were picking tea.
Within the garden, many have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives. Xuangjue could not avoid following them, running restlessly through the weeds.
His nostrils reach the heavens—this ancient adept enters the mud and water to startle the poor child; this is the sharp edge of awakening from death to life.
Swiftly, he continued the profound tradition that penetrates the Purple Microcosm (*Zǐwēi*).
To cite Chan Master Dèng Yìnféng: when he arrived at Nánquán, Nánquán pointed to a pure pitcher and said, "The copper pitcher is an object.
There is water in the pitcher; do not disturb the object. Bring me some water. The Master picked up the pitcher and held it before Nánquán’s face.
Before he had finished speaking, the spring ceased its flow.

[The Master] picked up the case and said: "Nanquan, in a single moment, together with Deng Yinfeng, finished expounding the twelve divisions of the scriptures and the teachings of the Great Canon, yet not a single word was spoken.
Deng Yinfeng heard five thousand and forty-eight fascicles and remained silent and still. Now tell me—"
Deng Yinfeng: "Does he have an offense or not? If you say he has an offense, how could Nanquan have brought it to rest?
If you say he is without offense, how can one account for his having touched the pure pitcher? Try to pass a judgment on this."

The Lion’s full majesty is heard throughout the realm: who would dare knock upon the gate of the ghostly pass? Unless one realizes through both essence and function that there is no self, the vessel will not tip, and awakening will not be difficult to attain.
Master Daci addressed the assembly, saying: "To speak for ten feet is not as good as practicing for one foot;
to speak for one foot is not as good as practicing for one inch. Dongshan said, "I do not speak in that way. A monk asked, "How then do you speak?
Dongshan said, "Speak that which cannot be practiced; practice that which cannot be spoken. Yunju said, "Practice..."

At the time when there is no speaking, there is no path of speech; at the time when there is speaking, there is no path of action. When there is neither speaking nor non-speaking, what path could one possibly traverse? Le Pu said:
"When both speaking and traversing reach their destination, the original substance is absent; when both speaking and traversing do not reach their destination, the original substance remains."
The Master held up the staff and said: "In a past life, Daci was merely a single carpenter’s line.
Why is this so? Observe his actions; his habitual tendencies remain. It is best to teach him to abandon all verbal measurements of length and breadth."
"Bring forth a single phrase of the Way! If you do not speak, I shall give him three blows of the staff; I will not let him pass.
When Dōsō reached this point, he too sought his life upon the tips of the hundred grasses. Unju had already arrived, yet how could one avoid the toil of such coming and going?
Rakuhō was wide awake, yet he continued to babble in his sleep.
The Honored One of Immeasurable Light, Perfect and Immovable—how can words describe Him throughout the present and the past? Universal clouds spread far and wide with fragrant perfumes;
He moves everywhere, dwelling nowhere, at the Gate of the Sea Banner.
The Master Changsha Cen was cited. A monk asked, "Where has Nanquan gone after his passing?
The Master said, "He became a donkey for the eastern neighbor and a horse for the western neighbor. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "If you want to ride him, ride;
if you want to dismount, dismount."

The Master picks up the case and says: "Great as the Venerable Changsha was, when he arrived here and was questioned by this monk, he was left with nothing for it but to run wild in all directions—like a donkey hitching itself to a horse.
How much more so for those who have not yet transcended numbers and quantities, or who dwell in the realms of existence and non-existence?
But tell me, within the words of Changsha, how was this monk’s life and death? Look! The wise, upon merely hearing this, should seize it with vigor. Do not...
If you wait even a moment, you will lose your head.

That ten billion manifested bodies are known only by the Buddha. Sentient beings pass through kalpas in ever-deepening delusion; like empty flowers and the moon reflected in water, they divide the three realms.
To return to the source in a single thought—how wondrous!
Citing Chan Master Guishan Lingyou, he addressed the assembly, saying: "After this old monk has passed away, I shall become a water buffalo on the mountain below.
On its left flank, I will write five characters: 'Guishan Monk [Name]. At that time, if you call it 'Guishan Monk,' it is a water buffalo;
if you call it a 'water buffalo,' it is Guishan Monk. What would you call it?"
He immediately attained it. Yunju spoke on his behalf, saying: "The Master has no other title. Zifu spoke on his behalf by drawing a circle and holding it up. He commented:
"Although Muzhou had obtained the body of a beast, he did not receive the retribution of a beast; therefore, he spoke of that while pointing toward this."
To speak this to that person is the same as that person speaking to oneself; there is no connection whatsoever.
It is best to pierce right through the nostrils of Guishan, making him unable to utter a single word. Yunju’s judgment in this manner leaves his own feet off the ground.
Zifu suffered from a wind-illness and could not stop talking, yet he managed to avoid mad ravings; even so, he is still somewhat inferior.
With his horns and peaks, he never dwells in conditioned activity; Guishan strides alone, startling the deaf and the blind. The cowherd boy has yet to discern the news of the ox;
even now, he falls into ditches and deep pits.
Jǔyún Jìshī Cānzhuǎn asked Nánquán, saying, "The *maṇi* jewel no one recognizes; it is personally held within the *tathāgatagarbha*. What is this 'garbha'?
Nánquán said, "That which comes and goes with you is the garbha. Jìshī said, "What about that which does not come and go?
Nánquán said, "That too is the garbha. He asked again, "What is the jewel? Nánquán called out to him, "Master! Jìshī immediately realized it.
The Patriarch replied, "Yes. Nanquan said, "Go away; you do not understand my words. [Commentary:
The Patriarch posed a question whose meaning pervades heaven and earth. To speak of it in a way that merely resembles it is to have no door of entry.
Nanquan’s thorough great compassion allows guest and host to coexist in harmony, manifesting both the inner and the outer. A voice calls and a voice responds—this is a black-lacquered Kunlun.
"Eh! The son of Yama is truly fearsome.

I have heard that the priceless jewel, the maṇi, has been obtained; yet as it passes from hand to hand, it seems more and more like that of a pauper. Since the Master-Grandfather did not yet understand, he posed a question;
Nanquan responded, for he would not transmit [the Dharma] indiscriminately."
He cited Master Chen of Changsha, who presented this verse: "One who sits atop a hundred-foot pole, Though they have gained entry, it is not yet true.
One must advance further from the hundred-foot pole; Throughout the ten directions and the Dharma-realm, the whole body manifests.
A monk asked, "As for that hundred-foot pole, how does one advance? The Master said, "Mountains of Langzhou, waters of Lizhou. The monk said, "Please [explain further]."
The Master spoke of the Way of the Teacher, saying: "The four seas and five lakes are within the imperial transformation.
[The Commentator] says: This person cannot do anything about these four lines of Changsha; only this monk dared to step forward and strike him down.
Yet, he still lacked the final line.
Seizing the clouds and grasping the waves, he penetrates mountains and rivers; alone he rows the solitary peak Prajñā boat.
Having ferried all four classes of beings across to the other shore, he sat facing the wall for nine years, transmitting the Dharma at Shaolin.
Citing Chan Master Zhaozhou Sheng, he asked Nanquan, "Where does a person who 'knows there is' find rest?
Nanquan replied, "He goes to be a cow beneath the mountain. The Master said, "Thank you for the instruction. Nanquan said, "Last night at the third watch, the moon shone through the window."
The Master held up [the whisk] and said: "Zhaozhou lets go; Nanquan gathers in. If you have not yet clarified the essential point, there is no need to seek the ox elsewhere.
It is like a surging current of blood that pierces through the skull. For those who do not understand, it is a wall of copper and iron; for those who can penetrate it, [it is open]."
The bright moon clarifies the autumn;
those who know it do not show their heads. They pass their years within the light of nirvāṇa. A single water buffalo has its nose pierced by a golden ring;
for ten thousand kalpas they roam at ease, attaining true freedom.
When Chan Master Zihu Yanzong called out "Thief! in the middle of the night, the assembly all fled in alarm.
The Master went to the rear of the Sangha Hall, seized a monk, and shouted, "The *vina* has caught him! He’s caught him! The monk said, "It is not I.
The Master said, "It is indeed you; it is simply that you are unwilling to take responsibility."
The Master picks up the case and says: "At midnight, Zihu saw the sun at its zenith; his heart was filled with urgent sorrow and compassion.
He could not help but stir the skull, seizing at emptiness to create a thief. This is not only a 'white-robbery' (stealing in broad daylight) like Linji’s;
even Nanquan, arriving here, would have suffered a total defeat. I say that this monk has long since lost his life; how could he now possibly accept [the Dharma]?"

The wind dances through the craggy pines, yet people do not perceive it; they vainly employ clever stratagems and become increasingly bewildered. Throughout the night he remains steadfastly unconvincing;
one knows not in what kalpa he will finally accept the responsibility. Alas! Heaven! Heaven!
Citing Chan Master Zhaozhou Sheng, he asked a presiding lecturer (zuozhu), "What sutra are you lecturing on? The lecturer replied, "The *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*.
The Master said, "May I ask about a certain passage of meaning? [The lecturer] said, "Yes. The Master kicked at the air with his foot, blew upon it once, and said, "What is the meaning of this?
The lecturer said, "There is no such meaning in the sutra. The Master said, "That is the meaning of the five hundred strongmen lifting the rock; yet you simply say..."
[The Master] said: "None. He held up his staff and said: "Zhaozhou knew deep down that the Master was dozing, so he gave him another 'sleep-talk' line.
Now tell me, when Zhaozhou kicked at the air and blew a breath, what was the meaning? If you still do not understand, you are ultimately being deceived."
He kills a person;
with every kick, there is a blast. The golden-haired lion manifests its full majesty. Zhaozhou’s application is beyond form and speech;
yet, alas, those who lose their heads refuse to return home.
Regarding the practitioner Gan-zhi: while serving congee at Nanquan, he said, "I request the Master to recite.
Nanquan said, "Practitioner Gan-zhi, you have served congee and invited the assembly; for the sake of the 'cat-spirit' and the 'white ox,' recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā."
Gan-zhi then prostrated and departed. Nanquan, however, went back into the kitchen, smashed a cauldron, and held it up, saying:
"Gan-zhi has not finished; this corpse fills Nanquan's nostrils and brings trouble upon this master.
I have smashed these stubborn implements and revealed a streak of golden light to bear witness to the rice gruel offering. This band of orphaned spirits still remains—"
Not knowing the proper time. Hūṃ hūṃ! Merely eating—when will it ever end?
A gentleman arrives at the gate; no one understands. Striking these idle implements: Ganqi and Nanquan.
The great earth cannot be supported. Why cannot it be supported? The retribution is indeed like this. [Difficult to fathom.

Citing Chan Master Fazhen of the Great Sui Dynasty: A monk asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder whether this very thing is also destroyed?
The Master said, "It is destroyed. The monk said, "If that is so, then one follows along with it. The Master said, "One follows."
The other [monk] departed.

[Dongshan] took up the case and said: "Da Sui Fazhen and this monk both entered the mud and the water; yet this monk alone was like someone propping against a fence and feeling his way along a wall—separated by ten thousand mountains.
Had it been Da Sui, he would have been narrow-minded and small-hearted, and this monk would have been difficult to save. Fortunately, Ta..."
In the Sui dynasty, Kuang tied a rope to the monk’s head; he nearly ran this wild fox spirit to death.

If it had been Puan, as soon as he saw this monk intending to open his mouth, he would have immediately jammed his tongue shut. Had he done so, the monk would have suddenly attained realization and avoided the exertion of displaying literary artifice.

East, west, south, and north—pervading and intersecting everywhere. For those who awaken, there is refreshing clarity; for those who are deluded, there is great calamity. Following the stream or flowing with it, the Dharma is true and does not fall away.
If it has not been fully brought forth, who would dare to take up this burden?
To cite Chan Master Zhaozhou Sheng: A monk asked, "The myriad dharmas return to the One; where does the One return?
The Master said, "When I was in Qingzhou, I made a cotton robe that weighed seven catties."
The Master held up his whisk and said: "This monk has managed the treasury for thirty years, yet he does not recognize a single coin.

Zhaozhou traveled as a mendicant for eighty years, yet he did not even know there were such things as words. If you wish to understand the point where the spiritual spark meets its source, you must directly don the robe of Zhaozhou."

Following the water upstream, I sought its source but could not see it; meeting people along the way, how could I bear to speak? I know that you have turned your back on awakening and understood the toil of worldly life;
these idle words are all the true intent of Samantabhadra.
Once, while Yunyan was sweeping the floor, Guishan said, "What a great fuss you are making. Yunyan replied, "You must know that there is one who does not make a fuss.
Guishan said, "If that is so, then there is a second moon. Yunyan held up his broom and asked, "How many moons is this?
Guishan lowered his head and departed. When Xuansha heard of this, he said, "That is precisely the second moon."
The Master held up his whisk and said: "At the place where Yunyan raised his broom, Guishan’s mouth was full and he could not utter a word;

Xuansha still would not let him go. Examining this from beginning to end, Guishan was fortunate indeed to have been left in peace, yet he stirred up dust and dirt, and in the end he took a blow from him that will keep him from emerging for kalpas."

Casually sweeping away the dust from level ground, one must first realize there is something to acknowledge before being willing to keep company. With mournful winds and bright moonlight, the cries of the monkeys grow urgent;
when will the destitute son who left his home ever return?
To cite Master Wuduo of Guannan: At times, he would take a wooden sword, rest it across his shoulder, and perform a dance.
A monk asked, "From where did you obtain the sword in your hand? The Master threw the sword to the ground; the monk then placed it back into the Master's hand.
The Master said, "From where did you obtain this? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I grant you three days to produce a single phrase."
The monk also had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, taking up the sword upon his shoulder and performing a dance, saying: "Only by doing so can it be achieved. He added:
"Daowu sails alone in a solitary boat; casting a line a thousand feet long, he travels far across rivers and seas, yet rarely does anyone swallow the hook."
Suddenly, the line was startled; he thought it must be a massive whale thrashing about. But when he reached down to seize it, it turned out to be merely a shrimp playing in the water.
His mental exertions were in vain.
The old woman of Guannan brandishes a wooden sword; its edge is never revealed, yet it is most efficacious. She casts it down, its majestic radiance beyond the reach of sight or hearing;
standing alone like the blade from Fengcheng, it lacks nothing. ○ [O @ Yi].
He cited the case of Grand Master Lu Xun, who asked Nanquan, "In ancient times, someone raised a gander in a bottle.
As the gander grew larger, it could no longer get out of the bottle. Now, one must not break the bottle, nor may one harm the gander.
How can this be resolved? Nanquan called out, "Grand Master! Lu responded, "Yes. Nanquan said, "It has come out."
The Master held up the whisk and said: "In the end, he could not get out. Layman Lu Xian spent his entire life investigating only the ancient saying, "He could not get out of the bottle.
Nanquan was skilled at grasping the essence of the gander that did not break the bottle; thus, with a single cry, he pulled straight through, leveling delusion and enlightenment.
Penetrating past and present, he became a true master of our school. I ask those who travel to study under teachers: have you gotten out yet? Hurry!
Only through correspondence can one truly attain it.

To establish doctrines and define tenets while grossly deceiving people—such a person’s arrogance toward Amitābha is narrow-minded and petty. When black and white cannot be distinguished, it is difficult to take action;
yet, by letting one move pass, even the great spirits are struck with awe.
To cite Chan Master Linji Yixuan: One day, while Huangbo was leading a work party to hoe the garden, he arrived late.
The Master greeted him and stood there pressing down on his hoe. Huangbo said, "Are you exhausted? The Master replied, "I have only just begun to hoe the ground;
why do you speak of exhaustion? Huangbo raised his staff and struck him. The Master seized the staff and pushed Huangbo to the ground. Huangbo then called for the *vinaya-dhara* (the disciplinarian).
"Venerable Karmadāna, help me up! The Karmadāna helped him up and said, "How can you, O Abbot, tolerate such a madman?
Huangbo then struck the Karmadāna. The Master himself continued digging in the earth and said, "In other places they perform cremation; here, we bury them alive."
The Master holds up the whisk and says: "When masters meet, it is like facing an enemy face-to-face. When the adept sets forth their device, it is like the mutual clashing of arrow-points.
Roaming throughout the ten directions, there is not even a shadow to be found. Surveying the entire dharma-realm in a single glance, one does not fall into the extremes of existence or non-existence.

How could this be like a stinking hound chasing a clod of earth, or a madman in a frenzy? To seek words and cling to phrases is to turn one's back on awakening and exhaust one's life in toil—a mere seeker of empty fame."

It is of no benefit to oneself or others. Consider, for instance, when Master Linji Xuan encountered Huangbo during a communal work assignment; there he manifested a subtle indication of the ultimate meaning.
His wisdom and function were teacherless, naturally vast and open, brilliant, wondrous, and beyond perception.

While the rector was receiving a blow in his dreams, Linji buried people in an ocean of wisdom. Pu’an wished to strike Huangbo, treating a superior as an inferior out of contempt. Now, if one wishes to...
To awaken such people, one must first reveal the eye.
With the jewel of wisdom hidden in the heart, those who understand it are few. Entrusting the entire mechanism to the "Water Dragon’s Roar," suddenly they encounter that which has no likeness.
Who can comprehend this light that brings the living and the dead back to life?
To cite Chan Master Huairan of the Three Sages: When the Master arrived at Deshan, as soon as he spread out his sitting cloth, Deshan said, "Do not spread out your cooking cloth;
there is no spoiled rice here. The Master said, "Even if there were, there would be no place for it. Deshan struck him with his staff;
the Master caught it and, in turn, pushed Deshan onto the meditation seat. Deshan laughed heartily, while the Master wept bitterly.
He departed for heaven.
[Zhaozhou] picked it up and said: "Great as De Shan was, in the end he could not manage a single thing against San Sheng.
San Sheng, in turn, threw this De Shan down so that he could never rise again. Puan added his comment: "Alas! Alas! But you all—"
People, how will you deliberate upon this? *Hoo!* Letting one move pass. San-sheng is the horned tiger;
De-shan is the one-eyed dragon. Before the mechanism is even unfolded, they are in accord; beyond words and thought, they have already communicated.
Wind and clouds dissolve the myriad phenomena; who shares in this laughter and weeping? If one does not return to life from within death, how can one avoid being trapped by others?
The Master Xinghua Cunchang addressed the Vinaya Master Kebin, saying: "Before long, you shall become a master of the sangha’s leadership.
Kebin replied: "I will not enter your community. The Master said: "Do you enter it because you have understood, or do you not enter it because you have not understood?"
He replied, "There is no connection. The Master then struck him and addressed the assembly, saying: "Venerable Kebin has been defeated in the battle of Dharma.
He is ordered to forfeit five strings of cash from his robes and bowl to provide a meal for the community, and he shall be expelled from the monastery."
The Master held up his whisk and said: "To build a mound of earth on level ground—let Xinghua pass for now.
Why was the Rector Kebin subjected to such fiery poison within the Great Snow Mountains? If one cannot resolve this kōan, one is not yet a true master.
Suddenly, the Pillar of the Eastern Ridge said: "I, however, know how to resolve it: Kebin is difficult to support; he should be expelled from the monastery."
Transgressions fill the heavens. Those who give rise to a calculating mind while receiving food fall directly into hell.

To examine the manifest is to reveal its gravity; to verify the void is to find it lacking substance. Before long, one will be fit to act as a guiding teacher, yet remains unaware of the movement of the marks of arising and ceasing.
At the critical moment, one must grasp the essentials to distinguish the refined from the coarse.
The Master of Shanyang Hermitage was brought forward. A monk arrived to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Who is it?

The monk replied, "The Master of Shanyang Hermitage. The Master said, "It is I. The monk then gave a shout. The Master made a sound of sighing. The monk said, "I still require the staff. The Master struck him. The monk then asked:
"What principle did the abbot realize that he later came to dwell on this mountain? The Master said, "I too wish to communicate my own origins, yet I fear being scrutinized by others.
The monk said, "How could one possibly avoid it? The Master then gave a shout. The monk said, "Exactly! The Master then struck him.
The monk laughed loudly and departed. The Master said, "A total defeat! A total defeat!"

The Master held up the whisk and said: "To examine and discern according to the universal principle is to know before the question is even raised. One who lacks the 'nose' (the core insight) merely exerts themselves in coming and going. I say:
the Abbot and this old monk share a single eye, yet looking with it, we see nothing at all; we share a single nostril."
Furthermore, they do not know the fragrance; they cannot avoid laughing loudly and being utterly defeated. Those with the true eye—do you all understand this? After a long silence, he said: "Zha!
When the clouds leave no trace and the rain leaves no mark, the continuity of phenomena and principle is boundless; to sell gold, one must indeed possess gold.
People here—if you truly do not recognize [this]—take the case of Chan Master Qingfeng Chu, who visited Baishui. Baishui asked, "Lepu has a path of vital function; is this so?
The Master said, "It is. Baishui said, "Cease the path of life and come from the path of the familiar. The Master said, "The path of life..."
[The Master] said, "Above, there are countless dead people piled upon the road; they do not touch a living man.
Baishui said, "This is Lebu’s [work]. What about yours? The Master said, "It is not only Lebu; even Jiashan could do nothing about it. Baishui said, "..."
"Why was Jia Shan at a loss? The Master said, "Have you not heard it said: 'The path of the living mechanism'? [The Master] added, commenting:
"Qingfeng was fortunate enough to be so majestic; the green peaks and lush forests should not have been disturbed by even a single spark of fire."
It was burned until it was red-hot and charred; even unto this day, there is no lingering attachment.
When the Path is seen, the vital impulse does not arise; when the vital impulse arises, the Path is not seen. The Blue Peak is green year after year; the White Water is ever vast and surging.
The paths of the born and the matured do not intersect; both delusion and enlightenment fail to reach it. Before blue and white have even sprouted, Le Pu is profoundly deep and mysterious.
"Ha! [This refers to] Chan Master Xinghua Jiang. One day Emperor Zhuangzong said to the Master, "Since I captured Daliang, I have obtained a priceless pearl, yet no one has offered a price for it.
The Master said, "I beg Your Majesty to let me see this pearl. The Emperor [held it out].
He opened his hands and released the strap of his *fotou* (headgear). The Master said, "This is the treasure of a sovereign; who dares to appraise its value?

He then held it up and said, "The benevolent ruler has realized the fundamental source, yet there is no gate through which this vision may be presented. A master who has perfected the benefit of the lineage—rare indeed is one who encounters such a peer.
As for that point of benefit, when meeting face-to-face, he did not bring it forth; yet as soon as an intention arose, one knew it existed. Emperor Zhuangzong granted him a single thread of leniency.

If one examines it closely, Xinghua has acted with excessive recklessness; one must distinguish right from wrong. It truly must be so. [○@、] The Way!
